body:
## Problem (current behavior)

The structured error envelope is excellent (`type`, `code`, `title`, `detail`, `exit_code`, `examples`, `next_steps`, `recovery` with `suggested_retry`). However every error also carries two fields of generic, constant-across-all-errors prose:
- `required`: e.g. *"Use values that match documented command constraints."*
- `why`: e.g. *"Validation protects data consistency and deterministic behavior across commands."*

These are identical for an unknown flag, a bad status value, a missing required option, etc. — they never vary by error and carry no actionable information for an agent. In a long agent loop with frequent retries, this boilerplate is paid on every error.

## Proposed improvement

Add a lean error mode (`--lean-errors`, `PM_LEAN_ERRORS=1`, or simply omit `why`/`required` when `--json` is set unless they carry error-specific content) that keeps `code`, `detail`, `examples`, `next_steps`, and `recovery.suggested_retry` but drops the generic prose. Keep the verbose form for human/TTY output.

## Agent benefit

Smaller error payloads in retry loops while preserving the parts an agent actually acts on (`code`, `detail`, `suggested_retry`). The `suggested_retry` field alone often makes the error self-correcting.

title: Add a lean error mode that drops generic boilerplate

> **Migrated issue.** Originally filed as moldovancsaba/mvp-factory-control#798 (created 2026-05-10). Moved to `moldovancsaba/messmass` on 2026-07-03 as part of the board consolidation (all open board work now lives in this repo, per docs/PROJECT_MANAGEMENT.md).

---

## Objective

Measure paid and organic campaign performance in one reporting model so sponsor impact can be evaluated holistically.

## Unified Context

Relo Metrics explicitly calls out paid plus organic measurement as part of a complete sponsorship view. `{messmass}` currently leans on organic and operational metrics, leaving paid amplification less integrated.

## Problem

Campaign performance is incomplete if paid amplification and organic reach are reported separately or not connected. Without one model, sponsor value discussions miss a major part of the media mix.

## Goal

Unify paid and organic campaign evidence in the same attribution and reporting layer.

## Scope

### In Scope

- data model for paid campaign signals alongside organic signals
- shared attribution view across paid, organic, and tracked-link outcomes
- reporting outputs for combined and separated campaign performance
- governance for labeling which metrics are platform-provided versus internally derived

### Out of Scope

- full ad-buying or campaign execution tooling
- every ad-platform integration in the first version

## Execution Prompt

Focus on holistic measurement and clear labeling. The product should help users understand total campaign contribution without obscuring what was organic, paid, or inferred.

## Constraints

- paid and organic metrics must remain distinguishable
- attribution assumptions must be explicit
- the first version should target the highest-value integration path

## Acceptance Checks

- [ ] paid and organic inputs can exist in one campaign-performance model
- [ ] reports can show combined and separated views
- [ ] attribution assumptions are documented in-product
- [ ] users can evaluate total sponsor campaign contribution

## Risks

- platform metric mismatch can complicate comparisons
- users may overinterpret blended performance without clear labels

## Delivery Artifact

A unified paid plus organic campaign measurement model for `{messmass}`.

## Developer Notes

Research basis: Relo Metrics.

**Shape:** Large, goal-oriented (decompose into the suites below). **Source:** Tim-directed full LYB audit 2026-06-13. Grounded in a test-coverage audit of `apps/ios/LogYourBodyTests` (+UITests) @ 7d2a915.

## Goal

Build the test net a launching **paid** app needs: protect revenue integrity, data integrity, and the body-comp math. Front-load suites that prevent the **already-filed production bugs** from recurring.

## Current state

XCTest only; ~115 unit tests in one 125KB file (`LogYourBodyTests.swift`) + 13 XCUITests. Strong: feature-flag routing, source normalization, paywall preflight. **Absent:** `ValidationService`, FFMI/lean-mass math, Core Data delete/restore lifecycle, `RevenueCatManager.purchase()/restorePurchases()`, HealthKit midnight/timezone, account-deletion cleanup, EMA trend. Only one mock exists (`MockHealthSyncCoordinator`); no protocol-backed mocks for RevenueCat/CoreData/Supabase/HealthKit → some suites need a thin protocol-extraction refactor first.

## Priority suites (children)

P0: ValidationService; BodyMetricLocalDate timezone/midnight; sync tombstone-resurrection; RevenueCat purchase/restore (mock); account-deletion lifecycle. P1: FFMI/unit-conversion math; EMA trend; HealthKit import dedup. P2: snapshot tests for Paywall states.

Each P0 suite links to its existing bug ticket (JovieInc/Jovie#10420/2949/2950/2941/2942).

Here's a complete English bounty post template you can copy, paste, and adapt. It's designed to be easily parsed by bots (e.g., GitHub Actions, Discord "action board" scrapers) and follows typical Lean/Mathlib collaboration style.

```markdown
[Bounty] $XXX – Formalize (or disprove) the "Prime Emergence Conjecture"

## Problem in plain language
I propose a new conjecture related to prime emergence.  
*(Replace the following with your actual conjecture – keep it concise and precise)*

**Conjecture (natural language):**  
For every integer n > 1, there exists a prime p such that [your precise statement here].

## Formal statement (Lean 4 / Mathlib)
If you already have a Lean formalisation, put it below. Otherwise, a bounty hunter must produce one.

```lean
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime
-- Example placeholder – replace with your own
example (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) : ∃ p, Prime p ∧ [your predicate] := sorry
```

Bounty goals

Choose one or both:

· A) Formalise the conjecture in Lean + prove it (requires a full proof that compiles with Mathlib).
  Bounty: $___ (paid via GitHub Sponsors / PayPal / crypto)
· B) Disprove the conjecture (provide a counterexample, either in natural language or formalised).
  Bounty: $___

Merge / acceptance criteria

For the bounty to be paid and the contribution merged:

· The work is submitted as a Pull Request to a public GitHub repository (e.g., my own repo or a designated “conjecture-collection” repo).
· The PR includes a clear lean file containing either a proof (with #check) or a concrete counterexample.
· All Lean code passes lean --verify and uses Mathlib 4 (latest stable).
· The PR is merged by me or a designated maintainer.

Optional – to make it "action board" friendly:

· Add label bounty / prime-emergence
· The PR description must contain the exact phrase "Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"

License

All contributed code will be released under MIT (or CC0 / Apache 2.0). The mathematical statement itself is public domain.

How to claim

1. Fork [my-repo-link] / create a new PR in the target repository.
2. Write your proof/disproof.
3. Reference this bounty post in the PR description.
4. Once merged, I’ll pay the bounty within 7 days.

Contact / discussion

Open an issue in [my-repo-link] or ping me on [Discord/Keybase/Zulip].

```

### 🤖 Tips to make it machine‑scannable for an “action board”

Many bots watch for:

- **Keywords in title**: `[Bounty]`, `$`, `Prime Emergence Conjecture`
- **Checklist syntax**: `- [ ]` (GitHub task list)
- **Label**: add a label like `bounty` or `help-wanted`
- **Exact phrase**: put `"Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"` in the PR body

If your “action board” is a specific Discord bot or GitHub Project automation, check its documentation – but the template above follows the common pattern used by **GitHub Issues**, **Gitcoin**, and **OnlyDust** bounties.

### ✏️ What you still need to fill in

- Your exact conjecture (replace the placeholder text)
- Bounty amount
- Your GitHub repo link (or specify where the PR should be sent)
- Your payment method

Once you have those, copy the template into a **GitHub Issue**, a **GitHub Gist**, or a **Discord channel** that the bot scans. Good luck!
```

## Update documentation for lex-app v2.0.0rc209 → v2.0.0rc210

**Context:** A new version of `lex-app` has been released. The code changes below need to be reflected in the documentation in this repository.

### Writing style

**Read the existing docs first** to match their tone. The docs are written for developers who use the framework — not for contributors to the framework internals. Follow these rules:

- **Keep it practical and conversational.** Write like you're explaining to a colleague. Example of good tone: "You don't need to pass IDs manually — it figures out which calculation is running."
- **Don't expose internals.** Don't mention internal class names, error classes, or implementation patterns (like "LIFO stack", "ContextResolver pipeline") unless they're part of the public API the user calls directly.
- **Feature docs (`content/features/`) should explain what things do and how to use them.** Save class names, constants, and pgcodes for reference docs (`content/reference/`).
- **Keep changes minimal.** If the code diff is mostly test files or internal refactoring, the docs probably don't need updating. Say so and make no changes.
- **One-liners are fine.** Not every change needs a paragraph. A short addition to an existing bullet point is often better than a new section.

### Instructions

1. Read the existing documentation files under `content/` to understand the current writing style and structure.
2. Identify which pages are affected by the code changes below.
3. Update existing pages to reflect new behavior, parameters, or features — matching the existing tone.
4. If a completely new user-facing feature was added and has no doc page, create one following the existing structure and frontmatter format.
5. Do **not** modify pages unrelated to the code changes.
6. Do **not** create docs for test files, internal refactors, or CI/CD changes.
7. Keep all existing Quartz/Obsidian frontmatter (`---title:---`) intact.

### Commits (2)

```
59f3ba7 perf(core): make lean _initial_state the default (opt-out)
23b934d perf(core): add opt-in lean _initial_state to cut per-row memory

+    # -- Lean initial-state -------------------------------------------
+    # django-lifecycle keeps a full-field snapshot (``_initial_state``) on
+    # every instance so it can answer "has this field changed since load?".
+    # On a large calculate-all that snapshot is a second full copy of every
+    # field per live row, pinned for the instance's lifetime — the bulk of
+    # the v1->v2 per-instance memory regression that remains after the
+    # pre-validation buffer is freed.
+    #
+    # When ``lex_lean_initial_state`` is True the snapshot is narrowed to only
+    # the fields whose initial value is actually consulted: ``edited_at`` (the
+    # framework's own dependency, see ``_has_explicit_edited_at_override``),

+    # -- Lean initial-state machinery ----------------------------------
+    @staticmethod
+    def _expand_field_ref(ref: Any) -> Set[str]:
+        """Candidate snapshot keys a single field reference can map to.
+
+        We deliberately over-include — the raw reference, its head segment
+        (for FK paths like ``customer.status``) and the FK attname
+        (``customer_id``) — because the lean snapshot is built by *filtering*
+        the full snapshot (see :meth:`_build_lean_initial_state`): any key that
+        is not actually present is dropped, so an extra candidate costs
+        nothing, while a missing one would silently break change-detection.
+        """
+        if not ref or not isinstance(ref, str):
+            return set()
+        head = ref.split('.')[0]
+        return {ref, head, head + '_id'}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _field_names_from_condition(cls, condition: Any) -> Set[str]:
+        """Field names referenced by a (possibly chained) hook condition.
+
+        Modern ``@hook(condition=...)`` conditions (``WhenFieldHasChanged``,
+        ``WhenFieldValueWas`` …) expose ``field_name``; ``&`` / ``|`` compose
+        them into a ``ChainedCondition`` with ``left`` / ``right`` children.
+        Walk the tree and collect every referenced field.
+        """
+        found: Set[str] = set()
+        seen: Set[int] = set()
+        stack = [condition]
+        while stack:
+            obj = stack.pop()
+            if obj is None or id(obj) in seen:
+                continue
+            seen.add(id(obj))
+            field_name = getattr(obj, 'field_name', None)
+            if isinstance(field_name, str) and field_name:
+                found |= cls._expand_field_ref(field_name)
+            for child_attr in ('left', 'right'):
+                child = getattr(obj, child_attr, None)
+                if child is not None:
+                    stack.append(child)
+        return found
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _fields_from_hook_config(cls, hook_config: Any) -> Set[str]:
+        """Every field a single hook declaration consults for change-detection.
+
+        Covers the legacy ``when=`` / ``when_any=`` parameters and the modern
+        ``condition=`` object form (the documented public API).
+        """
+        names: Set[str] = set()
+        when = getattr(hook_config, 'when', None)
+        if when:
+            names |= cls._expand_field_ref(when)
+        when_any = getattr(hook_config, 'when_any', None)
+        if when_any:
+            for entry in when_any:
+                names |= cls._expand_field_ref(entry)
+        condition = getattr(hook_config, 'condition', None)
+        if condition is not None:
+            names |= cls._field_names_from_condition(condition)
+        return names
+
+    @classmethod
+    @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+    def _lean_tracked_field_names(cls) -> FrozenSet[str]:
+        """Snapshot keys to retain in lean mode (cached per concrete class).
+
+        ``edited_at`` is always tracked (the framework's own
+        ``_has_explicit_edited_at_override`` depends on it); every field named
+        in any of this class's hook ``when=`` / ``when_any=`` / ``condition=``
+        clauses is tracked so those hooks keep firing; and
+        ``lex_initial_state_extra_fields`` lets a model declare fields it
+        queries imperatively.
+        """
+        tracked: Set[str] = set(LexModel._expand_field_ref('edited_at'))
+        for extra in cls.lex_initial_state_extra_fields:
+            tracked |= cls._expand_field_ref(extra)
+        for method in cls._potentially_hooked_methods():
+            for hook_config in getattr(method, '_hooked', ()):  # noqa: SLF001
+                tracked |= cls._fields_from_hook_config(hook_config)
+        return frozenset(tracked)
+
+    def _build_lean_initial_state(self):
+        """Build a ``_initial_state`` holding only the tracked field keys.
+
+        The full snapshot is built first (so the stored values are byte-for-
+        byte what django-lifecycle would have stored) and then filtered to the
+        tracked keys. The transient full copy is discarded immediately; what is
+        *retained* on the instance is the narrowed dict — that is where the
+        per-row memory saving comes from.
+        """
+        full_state = ModelState.from_instance(self).initial_state
+        tracked = self._lean_tracked_field_names()
+        lean = {key: value for key, value in full_state.items() if key in tracked}
+        return ModelState(lean)
+
+    def _reset_initial_state(self):
+        """Re-baseline change-detection after a save, lean when opted in."""
+        if self.lex_lean_initial_state and ModelState is not None:
+            self._initial_state = self._build_lean_initial_state()
+        else:
+            super()._reset_initial_state()
+
+    def refresh_from_db(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        """Reload from DB, re-baselining change-detection lean when opted in."""
+        super().refresh_from_db(*args, **kwargs)
+        if self.lex_lean_initial_state and ModelState is not None:
+            self._initial_state = self._build_lean_initial_state()
+
     def post_validation(self):

         Base post-validation method - called first in post_validation_hook.

 | 2026 | 79 | **Sub-cluster 1u landed — lex-app installed version is now pushed from the running customer instance to the LEX Instance Controller at startup, so the IC instance-details "LEX APP VERSION" row reflects the framework version actually running in the pod (not whatever IC's DB last stored).** Driver: IC's stored `image_version` is unreliable because release Terraform applies can fail silently (state-lock + UI auto-refresh flipping `ERROR` back to `RUNNING`), leaving either a stale value or an attempted-but-never-deployed target version on screen. First try was a live `kubectl exec` from IC into the customer's `django-backend` container to read `importlib.metadata.version('lex-app')` — blocked by RBAC (`pods/exec` is essentially "shell into any customer pod" and operations declined to grant it). Solution: the running customer pod is authoritative for its own `lex._version.__version__` and pushes it to IC over the **already-existing instance→IC HTTP channel** (env-injected `DOMAIN_BASE` + `LEX_API_KEY`, header `Authorization: Api-Key <key>`, same shape `lex.api.views.lex_api.LexAPI.send_email` already uses; no new credentials, no new cluster RBAC, no public exposure on the customer instance). **Source (new file `lex/lex_app/report_lex_app_version.py`):** `report_lex_app_version_to_ic(force=False)` schedules a **daemon** background thread targeting `_do_report` so startup cannot be blocked even if IC is hung or paused; a module-level latch + `threading.Lock` makes it once-per-process so multiple `AppConfig.ready` invocations (workers, replicas, restarts) do not flood IC; `force=True` is the documented test-only escape so cluster tests can drive the push path twice without leaking the latch. Three env vars (`DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT`, `DOMAIN_BASE`, `LEX_API_KEY`) gate the whole thing — local dev / CI / pytest runs never accidentally ping production IC. `_do_report` POSTs `{"version": __version__}` to `https://{DOMAIN_BASE}/api/report_lex_app_version/` with a 10-second timeout and **swallows every failure path** (network exception logged at INFO, non-200 response logged at INFO) so a broken or unreachable IC can never crash the customer pod's startup; the worst case is that IC keeps the previously-known version and the UI renders `Unknown`. Hooked into `LexAppConfig.ready` (`lex/lex_app/apps.py`) so the push fires on every server-process startup, wrapped in `try/except` for belt-and-braces protection. Backwards-compatible by design: customer instances running older lex-app versions (without this module) simply do not push and IC keeps `lex_app_version=""` → UI shows `Unknown`. **Cluster 1u** (next-free letter after 1t; 1.171 picks up after the cluster max at 1.170): 1.171 not-deployed env skips the push entirely (no thread started); 1.172 deployed env first call schedules a daemon thread targeting `_do_report`; 1.173 second call without `force=True` is guarded by the once-per-process latch; 1.174 `force=True` bypasses the latch (single documented escape); 1.175 `_do_report` POSTs the exact URL + `Authorization: Api-Key <key>` header + `{"version": <v>}` body that IC's `ReportLexAppVersion` view expects (drift here lands as 401/404 silently); 1.176 a `requests.RequestException` from the POST is swallowed without raising; 1.177 a non-200 response is swallowed without raising. Test file: `lex/test_project/tests/init/test_1u_lex_app_version_reporter.py`. **Local validation:** 7 pass / 0 fail in 0.31s via plain `pytest` with `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=lex.lex_app.settings` (this batch is pure-logic `SimpleTestCase` so the lex pytest wrapper's Postgres test-DB setup is not needed; the sandbox does not have a local Postgres). | 1u | 7 (1.171–1.177) + source in 2 files (`lex/lex_app/report_lex_app_version.py` new; `lex/lex_app/apps.py` adds the `ready()` hook) | 7 pass / 0 fail locally via `python -m lex pytest` (0.04s once the Postgres test DB was created/destroyed; pure-logic `SimpleTestCase` so the wrapper's DB setup is incidental, not exercised) |
 | 2026-06-10 | 80 | **Sub-cluster 1u superseded the startup-push design with encrypted runtime metadata on `/health` / `/api/health`.** Goal expanded: IC must show both the running lex-app package version and the running customer-project commit SHA. +"""Cluster 3f — lean ``_initial_state`` opt-in must not weaken any hook.
+
+Intent (from docs/features/data-pipeline/lifecycle hooks.md and
+docs/reference/LexModel Internals.md):
+
+    django-lifecycle keeps a per-instance ``_initial_state`` snapshot — a full
+    copy of every field captured at ``__init__`` and re-captured after each
+    successful save — so that change-detection (``has_changed`` /
+    ``initial_value``) and the conditional-hook forms (legacy ``when=`` /
+    ``when_any=`` and modern ``condition=`` objects) can compare a field's
+    current value against its value at the start of the save.
+
+    On a large calculate-all that snapshot is a second full-field copy pinned
+    per live row — the bulk of the v1->v2 per-instance memory regression that
+    remains after the pre-validation buffer is freed (Cluster 3e). LexModel now
+    offers an opt-in ``lex_lean_initial_state`` that narrows the snapshot to
+    only the fields whose initial value is actually consulted: ``edited_at``
+    (the framework's own ``update_edited_at`` depends on
+    ``has_changed('edited_at')``), every field named in this class's hook
+    ``when=`` / ``when_any=`` / ``condition=`` clauses, and anything listed in
+    ``lex_initial_state_extra_fields`` for imperative ``has_changed`` callers.
+
+    The customer-observable contract this sub-cluster pins:
+      - opting in is a pure memory optimisation: every conditional hook fires
+        exactly when it did before (proven field-for-field against an
+        identical full-snapshot control model), and ``edited_at`` auto-stamping
+        plus explicit-override handling are unchanged;
+      - change-detection stays byte-for-byte correct for tracked fields, and an
+        untracked field cleanly reports "unchanged" (the documented trade-off);
+      - the snapshot really is smaller (the whole point); and
+      - the post-save re-baseline and ``refresh_from_db`` re-baseline both keep
+        producing the narrowed snapshot, so the optimisation survives an
+        instance's full lifecycle.
+
+Cluster 3f — scenarios 3.11–3.32. Type: E.
+Covers: lex/core/models/LexModel.py.
+Run: python -m lex pytest lex/test_project/tests/validation_hooks/test_3f_lean_initial_state.py -v
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import unittest
+
+import pytest
+
+from lex.test_project.tests._e2e_test_case import E2ETestCase
+
+from .models import (
+    ALL_MODELS,
+    FullConditionalItem,
+    LeanConditionalItem,
+    LeanExtraFieldItem,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.validation_hooks
+
+
+class TestCluster03f_LeanInitialState(E2ETestCase):
+    """Cluster 3f: the lean ``_initial_state`` opt-in preserves every hook."""
+
+    e2e_models = ALL_MODELS
+
+    # Field set the lean snapshot is expected to retain for the conditional
+    # models: edited_at (framework dependency) + every field named in a hook
+    # when=/when_any=/condition= clause. ``name`` and ``note`` are referenced
+    # by no change-detection clause, so they must be dropped.
+    _TRACKED = {"edited_at", "status", "amount", "a", "b"}
+    _UNTRACKED = {"name", "note"}
+
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        super().setUp()
+        # hook_log is class-level and shared across a test session; reset the
+        # per-class logs so each scenario observes only its own mutations.
+        LeanConditionalItem.hook_log = []
+        FullConditionalItem.hook_log = []
+        LeanExtraFieldItem.hook_log = []
+
+    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
+    @staticmethod
+    def _snapshot_keys(instance) -> set:
+        """Field keys retained in an instance's current ``_initial_state``."""
+        return set(instance._initial_state.initial_state.keys())
+
+    def _create_reset(self, model, **kwargs):
+        """Create a row and return it with a freshly re-baselined snapshot.
+
+        The create path runs through ``save()``; its ``transaction.on_commit``
+        re-baseline fires immediately under ``TransactionTestCase`` autocommit,
+        so the returned instance's snapshot reflects the persisted values and
+        ``hook_log`` is cleared ready for the update under test.
+        """

+        model.hook_log = []
+        return item

+        snapshot.

+        Given the framework default is ``lex_lean_initial_state = True``,
+        And a model that explicitly sets ``lex_lean_initial_state = False``,
+        When that opt-out model is instantiated,
+        Then its ``_initial_state`` still holds the untracked fields (``name``)
+        exactly as stock django-lifecycle would — opting out restores the full
+        snapshot.
+        """

+        Given a model with ``lex_lean_initial_state = True``,
+        When it is instantiated,
+        Then its ``_initial_state`` keys are a subset of the tracked set and

Related public work: #1431, #1439, #1273, #1357, #1359

## Business value

PDD prompt structure should preserve source-truth semantics without spending tokens on repeated boilerplate that does not improve the generated change. A lean PDD prompt mode gives the public project a measurable way to reduce prompt cost while preserving bounded output, verifier, and source-truth contracts.

This matters for multi-shot and routing work because token overhead compounds with `k`: every unnecessary prompt token is paid once per candidate.

## Current public state

Public `main` has model/cost primitives and context-compression work, but no public lean PDD prompt mode:

- `pdd/data/llm_model.csv`, `pdd/llm_invoke.py`, and global CLI options expose model/cost-related controls.
- #1357/#1359 track output-inclusive token/cost estimates.
- #1439 tracks budgeted context selection and compression research.
- #1431 tracks routing across model, harness, thinking, and multi-shot count.
- The public repo does not currently have the private RQ5 harness paths referenced by the source issue, so this issue should land against public code paths or a new publishable `research/` harness.

## Requirements

- Add a selectable lean PDD prompt mode for the public generation path or a publishable research harness.
- Keep the default mode unchanged.
- Lean mode must preserve:
  - source-truth prompt/spec/contract content,
  - allowed output files,
  - verifier command and visible test contract,
  - machine-parseable output delimiters/schema,
  - safety/non-goal constraints.
- Remove or shorten only nonessential workflow framing, duplicated narrative, and boilerplate.
- Emit a `prompt_policy.json` artifact describing:
  - mode,
  - removed sections and reason,
  - preserved contract fields,
  - source inputs and hashes.
- Emit a `prompt_token_audit.json` artifact with:
  - tokenizer/model used for counting,
  - per-task current tokens,
  - per-task lean tokens,
  - ratios,
  - aggregate ratio.
- Evaluate on a publishable frozen fixture/benchmark suite; do not depend on private corpus rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- A CLI flag, config field, or harness parameter can select `current` versus `lean` mode.
- Existing behavior is unchanged when lean mode is not selected.
- Lean mode emits both policy and token-audit artifacts.
- A fixture test proves lean mode does not drop required source-truth, output, verifier, or parseability fields.
- The token audit can prove the lean/current average input-token ratio on the publishable suite.
- If the target ratio is not achieved, the audit reports the structural floor instead of removing required contract fields.

## Implementation hints

- Prefer deterministic section-level pruning over LLM-based compression for v1 so the policy artifact is auditable.
- Build on public context-compression and token-estimation primitives where possible.
- If adding research harness files, place them under `research/` with docs and deterministic fixtures.
- Keep selector changes out of this issue; pair with the public multishot/selection issue instead.
- Use the same tokenizer/counting path that production model calls use, or record the approximation clearly.

## Test expectations

- Unit tests for pruning policy rules and invariant preservation.
- Golden prompt fixture showing current and lean prompt outputs.
- JSON schema tests for `prompt_policy.json` and `prompt_token_audit.json`.
- CLI or harness test proving default mode remains current.
- No tests should require private RQ data.

## Sanitized provenance

Adapted from internal migration source notes. This public issue omits raw nonpublic study counts, nonpublic corpus rows, unpublished verifier scripts, internal branches, job IDs, and costs.

Reported via beta user feedback (band space module): "Faire la soustraction des dépenses aux revenus pour ce qui est des sommes prévues et engagées."

## Current state
No schema change is needed. Each `FinanceEntry` already carries:
- `type` = income | expense (`FinanceEntryType`)
- `status` = planned | committed | paid (`FinanceEntryStatus`), i.e. "prévu" / "engagé" / "payé"
- an effective amount (`amount`, or the mid-point of `amountMin` / `amountMax`).

Today the metric cards "Prévu" and "Engagé" (`assets/js/components/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceMetricCards.vue`) sum income and expense together (their tooltips even say "dépenses + revenus"). No revenue-minus-expense net is computed anywhere. `FinanceEntryRepository::getSummaryByBandSpace()` only splits income / expense at the `paid` level.

## Proposed approach (no migration)
Preferred (single source of truth): extend `getSummaryByBandSpace()` to split income / expense per status (mirror the existing paid split), add net fields to `FinanceSummary`, and display them in `FinanceMetricCards.vue`.
Alternative: compute the net client-side from the already-loaded `entries` (the store holds all in-range entries; `FinancePoleAccordion` already does ~90% of this aggregation).

## Decisions needed
- Add net figures alongside the current Prévu / Engagé cards, or redefine those cards? Redefining changes numbers users may already read a certain way - I lean toward adding.
- Does "engagé" (committed) roll in "payé" (paid)? Money already spent is also engaged. Suggest showing Prévu / Engagé / Payé nets so it is unambiguous.

## Files
- `src/Repository/BandSpace/FinanceEntryRepository.php`
- `src/ApiResource/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceSummary.php`
- `src/State/Provider/BandSpace/FinanceSummaryProvider.php`
- `assets/js/components/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceMetricCards.vue`

# PRD — Dance To the Max (v1: Lean Validation MVP)

> Synthesized from the `grill-me` / `grill-with-docs` sessions. Uses the canonical vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md` / `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md` and respects `docs/adr/0001–0006`. Decisions log: `refinement-decisions.md`. Original wishlist: `specifications.md`.
> _Also filed as a GitHub issue; per-slice sub-issues track the build._

## Problem Statement

A ballroom dance studio has instructional video content but no way to sell access to it online. Dancers who want to learn at home can't subscribe and stream lessons, and the studio can't earn from its content, control who watches, or stop one paid account from being shared endlessly. Above all, there's no validated evidence that people will *pay* for online access — so any large build is a gamble.

## Solution

A responsive web app where a dancer signs up with email and password, picks one of **three subscription Tiers**, optionally starts a free **Trial**, pays via secure checkout, and immediately streams the **Dances** their Tier unlocks — each Dance's **Videos** organized by difficulty **Level** (Primeras veces → Max) and filterable by **Tag**. Each **Account** can stream on up to three concurrent **Sessions**. A **Super Admin** uploads Videos and configures Dances, Tiers, and prices; an **Admin** supports Subscribers. The release is deliberately lean: it does only what's needed to prove willingness-to-pay.

## User Stories

**Discovering & subscribing**
1. As a Visitor, I want to see the three Tiers and which Dances each unlocks, so that I can choose what to buy.
2. As a Visitor, I want to sign up with email and password, so that I can create an Account.
3. As a Visitor, I want to start a free Trial when I subscribe, so that I can try the content before being charged.
4. As a Visitor, I want to choose monthly or annual billing (annual discounted), so that I can pick my level of commitment.
5. As a Visitor, I want to pay through a secure checkout, so that I can become a Subscriber.

**Browsing & watching**
6. As a Subscriber, I want to browse the Catalog by Dance, so that I can pick a style to learn.
7. As a Subscriber, I want a Dance's Videos grouped by Level (Primeras veces → Max), so that I can start at the right difficulty.
8. As a Subscriber, I want to filter and search Videos by Level and Tag, so that I can find relevant content fast.
9. As a Subscriber, I want any Level of any Dance my Tier includes to be watchable, so that I can progress at my own pace.
10. As a Subscriber, I want Videos to stream with adaptive quality, so that playback is smooth on my connection.
11. As a Subscriber, I want Dances outside my Tier shown as locked with an upgrade prompt, so that I know what upgrading would give me.

**Account, sessions & billing**
12. As a Subscriber, I want to be logged in on up to three devices/browsers at once, so that my household setups work.
13. As a Subscriber, when I sign in on a fourth device, I want my least-recently-used Session ended with clear feedback, so that I understand the 3-device limit.
14. As a Subscriber, I want to stay signed in across visits, so that I don't re-authenticate constantly.
15. As a Subscriber, I want to change my password from my profile, so that I can keep my Account secure.
16. As a Subscriber, I want to reset my password by email, so that I can regain access if I forget it.
17. As a Subscriber, I want to upgrade my Tier and immediately access the newly unlocked Dances, so that I get more content when I choose.
18. As a Subscriber, I want to downgrade or cancel and keep access until the end of my paid period, so that I control my spending fairly.
19. As a Subscriber whose payment fails, I want a short grace period with automatic retries before losing access, so that a temporary card problem doesn't cut me off.
20. As a Subscriber, I want to see my current Tier, billing period, and renewal date, so that I know my status.

**Super Admin (content & pricing)**
21. As a Super Admin, I want to create and manage Dances, so that the Catalog reflects what we teach.
22. As a Super Admin, I want to set each Dance's minimum Tier, so that the cumulative Tier ladder matches our pricing.
23. As a Super Admin, I want to upload a Video and assign it a Dance, a Level, and Tags, so that it appears in the right place.
24. As a Super Admin, I want uploaded Videos transcoded and delivered via Signed URLs, so that content streams securely and adaptively.
25. As a Super Admin, I want to configure the three Tiers and their monthly/annual prices, so that I can sell access.
26. As a Super Admin, I want to publish and unpublish Videos and Dances, so that I control what is live.

**Admin (support)**
27. As an Admin, I want to find and view Subscribers, so that I can support them.
28. As an Admin, I want to see a Subscriber's Tier and Subscription status, so that I can answer billing questions.
29. As an Admin, I want to deactivate or block an Account, so that I can handle abuse.

**Returning & unsubscribed**
30. As a returning person whose Subscription has lapsed, I want to log in and re-subscribe to my existing Account, so that I keep my history and settings.
31. As a logged-in Subscriber with no active Subscription, I want to see the plan picker and my account settings rather than locked content, so that I understand I must subscribe to watch.

**Staff & roles**
32. As a Super Admin, I want to promote an Account to Admin (and demote it back), so that I can delegate Subscriber support without sharing my own credentials.

**Localization**
33. As a Visitor or Subscriber, I want to switch the app between Spanish and English, so that I can use it in my language.
34. As a Super Admin, I want to enter each Dance name and Video title/description in both Spanish and English, so that content reads correctly in either language.

**Public site (pre-login)**
35. As a Visitor, I want a public landing page that explains what Dance To the Max is, so that I understand the product before signing up.
36. As a Visitor, I want to read a biography of Max, so that I trust the instructor behind the content.
37. As a Visitor, I want to learn what ballroom dance is and how it originated, so that I'm drawn into the discipline.
38. As a Visitor, I want clear calls-to-action from the public site into signup / plans, so that I can start subscribing.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Shape.** Responsive web app (web-first; ADR-0001): a single web client over a backend API and a database. No native apps in v1.
- **Modules (favor deep modules behind small interfaces):**
  - **Identity** — signup, login, password change/reset; an Account has exactly one Role (Super Admin / Admin / Subscriber). Public signup always assigns `Subscriber`. The first Super Admin is seeded at deployment; the Super Admin promotes/demotes Admins from the console. No self-serve path to elevated roles.
  - **Session** — issues and tracks Sessions; enforces the 3-concurrent-login cap (ADR-0004): a 4th login evicts the least-recently-active Session; Sessions expire after ~30 days of inactivity; logout frees a slot. The cap counts logins, not simultaneous streams.
  - **Catalog** — Dance, Video, Level, Tag; browse/filter/search; publish state. A Video has exactly one Dance, one Level, and 0..n Tags. A Video is live iff `Video.published` AND `Dance.published` (Dance is the master switch); a published Dance with no published Videos is hidden from the Subscriber Catalog but visible to the Super Admin.
  - **Entitlement** — derives the set of Dances a Subscriber may watch from their Subscription's Tier. The core access check: *a Subscriber may play a Video iff their Subscription grants access (status ∈ {`trialing`, `active`, `past-due`}) AND the Video's Dance minimum-Tier ≤ the Subscriber's Tier rank.* A `past-due` Subscription keeps access through the dunning/retry window; access is removed only on `canceled`.
  - **Subscription/Billing** — Tier configuration; Subscription lifecycle (`trialing → active → past-due → cancelled`); Billing Period (monthly/annual). Delegates checkout, Trials, proration, and dunning to a payment provider (Stripe recommended) and consumes its **webhooks** to set Subscription status.
  - **Playback** — after the Entitlement check passes, requests a short-lived Signed URL from the hosted video provider for that Video.
  - **Admin console** — Subscriber management (Admin); content + Tier/price configuration + upload (Super Admin).
  - **Localization** (ADR-0005) — bilingual ES/EN UI with a language switcher; content metadata (Dance names, Video titles/descriptions, Tag labels) stored per Locale. Fixed Level values stay canonical with translated display labels; Video audio/subtitles are not localized.
  - **Public site (pre-login)** — bilingual marketing pages a Visitor sees before auth: a landing explaining the app, an About page with Max's biography, and a "What is Ballroom" page (definition + history). Copy lives in the i18n string catalog (no CMS in v1); pages link into signup / the plan-picker.
- **Tier → Dance mapping is data, not code** (ADR-0003): each Dance carries a configurable minimum Tier; the cumulative ladder (T1 ⊂ T2 ⊂ T3) is derived.
- **Video delivery** (ADR-0002): upload → provider transcodes → store the provider asset id; playback is authorized per-Video via expiring Signed URLs. No self-built transcoding queue.
- **Auth.** Email is the identifier; password reset via emailed token; sessions persist across visits.
- **Account lifecycle.** An Account is created at signup, independently of any Subscription (signup and checkout are separate steps). An Account has zero or one active Subscription; with none, its Entitlement is empty and it sees the plan-picker/paywall + account settings but cannot watch. Cancellation never deletes the Account — history is retained and the Subscriber can re-subscribe.
- **Schema (conceptual, no file paths):** Account(email, passwordHash, role); Session(accountId, createdAt, lastSeenAt); Dance(name{es,en}, minTierRank, published); Video(danceId, level, tags[], title{es,en}, description{es,en}, providerAssetId, published); Tag(label{es,en}); Tier(rank 1–3, monthlyPrice, annualPrice); Subscription(subscriberId, tierId, billingPeriod, status, currentPeriodEnd, providerSubscriptionId). Localized text fields carry one value per Locale (es/en).

## Testing Decisions

- **Test at the highest seam — the backend domain operations / API — not UI internals.** Assert external behavior ("can *this* Subscriber play *this* Video?"), not implementation; don't test what the type system already guarantees.
- **Entitlement check** (highest-value, pure logic): table-driven tests over (Subscription status, Tier rank, Dance minimum-Tier) covering the cumulative ladder and the `trialing`/`past-due`/`cancelled` edges.
- **Subscription lifecycle**: drive the billing module at its **webhook seam** with simulated provider events (`trial_will_end`, `payment_failed`, `canceled`, `updated`) and assert the resulting status and resulting access. Mock the payment provider at its service interface — never call the real one in tests.
- **Session cap**: exercise the login operation repeatedly and assert the 4th login succeeds and ends the least-recently-active Session.
- **Catalog**: query operations return the correct Videos by Dance/Level/Tag and respect the two-level publish rule (a Video is live iff `Video.published` AND `Dance.published`).
- **Playback / Signed URL** and the **payment provider** are integration boundaries — stub them at their interfaces.

## Out of Scope

Deferred (still in the eventual model, not in v1):
- Public comments & Admin replies; likes and view counts.
- The premium video-feedback loop (Subscribers submit Videos; Admins leave private notes).
- Badges/achievements, progress counters, continue-watching/resume, playlists, favorites/watchlist.
- Live class calendar/events; notifications; social sharing.
- 2FA; activity/audit logs.
- Offline downloads and native mobile apps (ADR-0001).
- Video subtitles/captions and localized audio — Videos remain in their original spoken language; bilingual v1 covers UI + content metadata only (ADR-0005).
- Full device management — named device list, "sesiones activas" panel, remote logout. Only the 3-Session cap ships in v1 (ADR-0004).
- Self-built transcoding queue (using a hosted provider; ADR-0002).
- Usage/reporting dashboards beyond the minimum; promo codes/discounts; a custom invoice portal (rely on the provider's hosted billing portal).

## Further Notes

- **Backlog issues to file** (from `refinement-decisions.md`): (1) *Billing & subscription details* — trial length/card-required/access scope + lifecycle specifics; (2) *Tier & content lineup* — the Dance list, each Dance's minimum Tier, and price points; (3) *Video provider selection* — choose Mux / Bunny Stream / Cloudflare Stream and signed-URL setup.
- **Open data** (don't block design): trial length, prices, the Dance lineup, the provider.
- **UI language** is resolved: bilingual ES/EN with localized content metadata (ADR-0005). Video subtitles deferred.
- **Vocabulary discipline:** use `CONTEXT.md` terms exactly. Most importantly, **Tier** = subscription and **Level** = difficulty — never interchange them; avoid the bare word "category."

## Summary

Create a lean paid-unlock system for CozyBlock built around a single Gumroad purchase, Netlify-hosted backend functions, and local entitlement persistence in the app.

## Locked Product Contract
- one Gumroad product: `Unlock Full Game`
- one purchase unlocks all premium worlds, including future premium worlds
- `World 0` and `World 1` are free by default
- the free/premium split remains configurable in content data
- no accounts or email restore in v1
- restore uses a user-saved restore code
- restore codes can be reused without limit
- claim is automatic from Gumroad redirect data
- refunds/revocations are not handled in v1
- hosting and backend live on Netlify

## Child Issues
- [ ] Define Premium Content Contract In Level Data: https://github.com/rschroed/CozyBlock/issues/28
- [ ] Make Navigation And Progression Paywall-Aware: https://github.com/rschroed/CozyBlock/issues/29

- [ ] Create Gumroad Product And Hosted Purchase Configuration: https://github.com/rschroed/CozyBlock/issues/31

- backend failures degrade to clear user-facing errors

**Category:** Bug — budget-governance contract violations (\`tools/cost_tracker.py\`)

Three related defects in \`reserve()\` and persistence undermine the spend-governance contract that AGENT_GUIDE.md leans on.

**1. WARN mode never signals a budget overrun** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:143-148\`
\`\`\`python
if estimated > self.usable_budget_usd:
    if self.mode == BudgetMode.CAP:
        raise BudgetExceededError(...)
# WARN falls straight through and reserves — no log, no flag, no return signal
\`\`\`
The module docstring promises "Budget overruns trigger pauses (in warn/cap mode)." In WARN mode an overrun produces **nothing** the orchestrator can detect. Fix: emit \`logging.warning(...)\` and/or set \`entry["budget_warning"] = True\` (surfaced in \`cost_snapshot()\`).

**2. \`BudgetMode.OBSERVE\` silently waives BOTH approval gates** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:127-140\`
The single-action-threshold check (127) and the new-paid-tool check (135) are both gated on \`self.mode != BudgetMode.OBSERVE\`. So \`require_approval_for_new_paid_tool=True\` becomes a no-op the moment mode is OBSERVE, and a brand-new paid provider runs unapproved. Spend-cap mode and consent are orthogonal and should not be coupled. Fix: keep new-paid-tool / single-action approval active regardless of budget mode (or add a separate flag).

**3. \`_approved_tools\` is not persisted — resume re-prompts for already-approved tools** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:59, 155-157\`, \`_save()/_load()\`
\`_approved_tools\` is an in-memory \`set\` never written by \`_save()\` nor restored by \`_load()\`. On any pipeline resume (a fresh \`CostTracker\` built from an existing \`cost_log.json\`), every previously approved paid tool is forgotten and \`reserve()\` raises \`ApprovalRequiredError\` again — breaking resumability of paid stages. Fix: persist approved tool names in the saved JSON and rehydrate in \`_load()\`.

## One sentence

Everything an agent can install — **knowledge, skills, MCP addons, grammars** — becomes one package model (`.ctxpkg` + a single new `kind` field), served by one registry (ctxpkg.com), verified by one trust chain (ed25519 + SHA-256 + audit + revocation), billed by one commerce rail — **consolidating four grown subsystems without inventing a single new format, service, or command universe.**

Full design: `docs/specs/unified-distribution-v1.md` (ships with the Phase 1 PR).

## Why now

We currently run **two parallel distribution universes** that overlap and drift:

| Concern | ctxpkg world | Addon world |
|---|---|---|
| Payload | knowledge (`.ctxpkg`) | capabilities (MCP servers), grammars (dylibs) |
| Registry | ctxpkg.com (hosted) | `addon_registry.json` + `grammar_registry.json` (bundled, hand-maintained) |
| Signing | `core/context_package/signing.rs` | `core/addons/signing.rs` (second ed25519 impl) |
| Billing | **live** (Stripe, 402, verified publisher) | prepared only (`core/addons/commerce.rs`) |
| Marketplace | ctxpkg.com | leanctx.com/addons |

…and one open gap that just became user-visible in PR #721: **an MCP addon's binary has no managed distribution path** — the gateway spawns `command` from `PATH` and hopes. The lean-md contributor's distribution question (crates.io vs. side-loading vs. registry) is the first external collision with this gap.

The consolidation is already half-built by our own code: `commerce.rs` describes itself as *"generalising the ctxpkg paid artifact to addons"* on the *"existing ctxpkg billing rails"*, and the `.ctxpkg` v2 spec already claims *"npm for AI context"* and reserves a blobs layout. This epic finishes that thought.

## Guiding principle

> An agent installs two things: what it should **know** and what it should be able to **do**. Both are packages. Every package is a `.ctxpkg`. One registry, one publisher identity, one trust chain, one marketplace, one billing rail.

**Consolidation discipline: every phase closes an existing construction site.** Non-goals: no new registry service, no new package format, no new signing scheme, no new CLI universe, no breaking change for existing packs/authors/registries, no commerce launch before catalog traction.

## The `kind` taxonomy

| `kind` | Payload | Runtime gate (all pre-existing) |
|---|---|---|
| `context` *(default)* | knowledge/graph/gotchas layers — unchanged, byte-compatible | redaction on load |
| `skills` | markdown/script documents as verified blobs | redaction on load |
| `addon` | embedded `lean-ctx-addon.toml` + per-platform artifact refs `{url, sha256}` | capabilities consent, sandbox, binhash spawn-pin, revocation |
| `grammar` | embedded `GrammarManifest` | mandatory hash+sig (in-process = highest bar) |

Install resolution chain (first match wins): **prebuilt artifact** → **`[install]` bootstrap** (uv/pip/cargo/npm/brew/dotnet, exists) → **`command` on PATH** (today's behavior, kept).

Dependencies already exist in the manifest — Phase 3 activates them: `@dasTholo/lean-md` declares `@dasTholo/lean-md-skills: ^1.0`, and `addon add lean-md` installs both. Skills update without binary releases.

## Phases

- [x] **Phase 0 — unblock lean-md now (no code):** crates.io publish + `[install] manager="cargo"` in its registry entry; works with the shipped bootstrap engine today (tracked in PR #721)
- [x] **Phase 1 (v3.9.2) — `kind` field + unified artifact installer:** #725 — **merged** (PR #729), `status: integrated`
- [x] **Phase 2 (v3.9.2) — `addon publish` + registry consolidation (bundled registries become CI snapshots):** #726 — **merged** (PR #734), `status: integrated`
- [x] **Phase 3 (v3.9.2) — `kind=skills` + dependency resolution (lean-md reference case):** #727 — **implemented** (PR #743, in review)
- [ ] **Phase 4 (after traction) — signing + commerce consolidation (one publisher identity):** #728

## Positioning (what this buys us)

1. **MCP distribution is wild-west** (`npx x@latest`, unsigned, unaudited). We become the only MCP host with a cryptographically closed publish→audit→sign→sandbox→spawn-pin→revocation chain.
2. **Skills are becoming the dominant workflow format.** Nobody has a signed, versioned, billable skill channel — `kind=skills` makes ctxpkg the first mover, with lean-md's skill pack as launch case.
3. **Enterprises want private agent infrastructure.** Private registry + token auth exist; with `kind` unification that is a company-internal app store for agent knowledge *and* capabilities, per `addons.policy = locked`.
4. **Publisher network effect:** one identity and reputation across context, skills, addons — instead of three trust silos.

## Determinism (#498)

Snapshot generation is content-addressed and timestamp-free; artifact paths are version-dir addressed; dependency resolution is lockfile-recorded and offline-reproducible. Regression guards ride with each phase.

**Problem:** The same body-comp snapshot shows two different FFMI values depending on screen. On a paid measurement app, the headline number contradicting itself destroys trust. **Evidence (Tim screenshots, 2026-06-21, #product):** * 'Share Body Score' card: Weight 170.4 lbs, Body Fat 12.1%, **FFMI 17.7**. * Home/Timeline (Oct 28 2024 selected): Weight 170.4 lbs, Body Fat 12.1%, **FFMI 18.5**.
Same weight, same BF%, same 30-day deltas ('+1 lbs last 30d', 'No change last 30d') = same snapshot. FFMI = lean mass ÷ height² — for fixed weight + BF it depends ONLY on height, so it MUST be identical across surfaces. **Severity/Priority:** P1 — visible self-contradiction on the headline metric; data-integrity bug, not cosmetic. **MRR opportunity:** HIGH (trust). Reach=anyone who views both home + share; Annoyance=high (looks broken / untrustworthy); Effort=low (single source of truth for the calc). Trust is the whole value prop of a measurement app. **Root-cause hypothesis (high conf):** two different FFMI computations/inputs — likely one surface applies the height-normalized/adjusted FFMI (e.g. +6.1×(1.8−height_m)) and the other the raw FFMI, OR one reads a stale/default height. Inspect the FFMI calc in MetricsInterpolationService / GlobalTimelineService vs the share-card builder; unify to one function. **Proposed fix:** single canonical FFMI function consumed by home, share card, and stats; add a unit test asserting all surfaces return identical FFMI for the same input. **Acceptance:** FFMI identical across home, Share card, and stats for a given snapshot; unit test guards it. **Issue shape & model:** Small, well-spec'd → Kimi K2 / DeepSeek. **Note:** also observed — the Body Fat % chart already has a working Smoothed/Raw toggle and reads reasonably smooth (re: JovieInc/Jovie#11352 'charts need smoothing', confirm WHICH charts are jagged); and the home full-bleed Avatar/Photo layout looks strong (JovieInc/Jovie#10880 delivered visually). Share-card crops the torso oddly vs home full-body — minor framing polish, not filed separately. **Related:** JovieInc/Jovie#10241 (unified timeline aggregation), JovieInc/Jovie#10226 (paid launch).
title: LYB data-integrity: FFMI differs across surfaces — Share card 17.7 vs home/Timeline 18.5 for same snapshot

Followup from PR #55 review (https://github.com/aaronsb/jira-cloud/pull/55#issuecomment-4425735490 / #55 item 4).

`projectKeyFromIssueKey(issueKey: string): string` in `src/handlers/issue-handlers.ts:425` is private — both call sites (handleGetIssue:465, handleUpdateIssue:578) go through it, but the contract that it always uppercases the result isn't asserted anywhere. A future "simplification" that drops `.toUpperCase()` would not be caught by the test suite.

## Why it matters

The uppercase normalization keeps two things deterministic regardless of agent input casing:

1. The rendered breadcrumb URI emitted by `markdown-renderer.ts:206` (`jira://custom-fields/{proj}/{type}`) — an agent caching by URI string sees the same key for `paid-192` and `PAID-192`.
2. The cache key passed to `field-discovery.ts:209` (`issueTypesCache`) — already self-normalizes via its own `.toUpperCase()`, but if the helper drops uppercase, the two layers fall out of sync.

## Options

- **Cheapest:** add `// @internal` comment + export `projectKeyFromIssueKey`, write a 4-row test in `src/handlers/issue-handlers.test.ts` (or co-locate in a new `*.test.ts` next to the source). Cases: `PAID-192 → PAID`, `paid-192 → PAID`, `Mixed-1 → MIXED`, `noprefix → NOPREFIX` (documents the no-dash fallback).
- **Cleaner but heavier:** move the helper to `src/utils/jira-keys.ts`, export from there, test it there. Justifies the move only if a third call site appears.
- **Don't:** lean on review to catch any future drop of `.toUpperCase()`. Reviewer flagged this as acceptable given the small surface.

## Acceptance

`projectKeyFromIssueKey('paid-192')` returns `'PAID'`, asserted in a unit test that runs as part of `npm test`.

Low priority — nothing observable breaks today, this is just a contract-locking exercise.
title: test: lock the casing contract on projectKeyFromIssueKey

## Problem

The header comment on `engine/content/IContentPack.h` states:

> Linking exception: content pack implementors (mods, plugins) may link against this header without being required to license their work under GPL v3. **See GOVERNANCE.md for the full exception text.**

`GOVERNANCE.md` contains no linking-exception text — nothing matching "exception" appears in the file. The one-sentence summary in the header is currently the only statement of the exception anywhere in the repository.

## Why it matters

- The exception is load-bearing for the content-pack ecosystem: it is what allows non-GPL plugins to implement `IContentPack` (the engine's distribution docs have positioned fa-bridge as possibly paid/non-GPL on exactly this basis).
- fa-bridge's distribution/licensing decision ([fa-bridge#37](https://github.com/fighters-legacy/fa-bridge/issues/37)) leans on this exception being well-defined; a dangling reference weakens it.
- There is no standard SPDX identifier for a custom linking exception, so the authoritative text has to live somewhere in-repo — the header promises GOVERNANCE.md delivers it.

## Fix

Write the full exception text (scope: which headers it covers — the vendorable interface set `IContentPack.h`, `AssetTypes.h`, `TrustLevel.h`; what "link against" permits; what remains GPL) into GOVERNANCE.md, or move it to a dedicated `LICENSES/`/`LICENSE-EXCEPTION` file and update the header comment's pointer.

body:
## Problem

A new contributor's first build is the onboarding bottleneck. Measured from a clean clone on a 12-core machine (Lean `v4.31.0-rc1`):

| Phase | Time |
|---|---|
| `git clone --depth 1` | 2 s |
| `cache get` (mathlib oleans) | seconds–minutes (download, not compile) |
| **`lake build LeanPool` — 2038 modules from source** | **72.8 min** |

The build dominates, and it is paid **in full on every fresh checkout** because Lean Pool publishes no olean cache for its own code. (mathlib only *feels* fast because contributors download its prebuilt oleans; compiled from source on the same machine mathlib takes ~135 min.)

The fix is the same one mathlib uses: **host a prebuilt olean cache and fetch it.**

## Why this is the right lever

- Build is CPU-bound and embarrassingly parallel (90 independent projects on mathlib); per-file tuning has a realistic ceiling of ~10–15%.
- The olean payload is **1.5 GB raw → ~460 MB gzipped**. Fetching ~460 MB (1–5 min) instead of a 72.8 min compile is a **~20–30× onboarding win**.
- CI already builds the whole pool on every PR — we just discard the output instead of keeping it.

## Proposal

### Tier 1 — whole-pool tarball keyed by commit (ship first, ~80% of value)
- [ ] On merge to `main`, CI tars `.lake/build/lib/lean/LeanPool` (~460 MB gz) and uploads it keyed by `<lean-toolchain>+<commit-sha>`.
- [ ] Add `make cache-get`: download the tarball for `HEAD`, unpack into `.lake/build`, fix mtimes + trace hashes so `lake` treats the oleans as fresh.
- [ ] Storage backend: Cloudflare R2 (zero egress) preferred; Azure or GitHub Releases (460 MB < 2 GB/file) acceptable. Retain last N commits.
- Outcome: fresh `main` checkout 73 min → ~3 min. Editing one project rebuilds only that subtree.

### Tier 2 — per-module content-addressed cache (only if needed later)
- [ ] Adapt mathlib's `Cache` exe to hash each LeanPool module by (source + transitive imports + toolchain) and store per-module tarballs, so any branch fetches every olean except the few its change invalidates.
- Defer until Tier 1's "rebuild the whole edited project" proves too slow for projects people actually touch.

## Gotchas (all solved by mirroring mathlib's cache)
- [ ] **Freshness:** `lake` rebuilds unless a stored hash/trace matches — the client must write those (the one fiddly part).
- [ ] **Toolchain keying:** oleans are toolchain-+-mathlib-specific; the key must include both, and **every version bump must re-upload** or everyone cache-misses. Wire the upload into the version-bump workflow.
- [ ] **No poisoning:** upload only from a clean, green `main` build, never a partial one (cf. partial-cache poisoning already seen on the docs build).

## Out of scope (intentionally)
Build-speed tuning of the slow files (`GardamTheorem` 105 s kernel-`decide`, `Monlib4.QuantumGraph` cluster 40–53 s, `BrauerGroup.IsoSecond` 42 s). These are vendored/intentional proofs; tuning saves ~5–8 min of 73 and risks the proofs. The cache is worth ~30×; tuning ~1.1×.

---
*Numbers from a from-scratch build experiment, 2026-06-23.*
title: Host a prebuilt olean cache so contributors fetch instead of building (73 min → ~3 min)

body:
## Task

Investigate and prototype support for the x402 payment protocol (and optionally MPP / UCP / ACP) on a single dmarcheck endpoint, so AI agents can pay-per-scan above the free rate limit without going through the human-oriented Pro signup flow. The goal is twofold: (1) give agents a frictionless paid escape hatch when they hit `10 req/IP/60s`, and (2) earn early-mover discovery on agent-readiness directories like isitagentready.com and the x402 ecosystem showcase. Outcome: a working `x402`-gated endpoint deployed to prod, real economics validated against actual usage, and a decision (kept or removed) after a 30-day observation window.

## Context

isitagentready.com scores sites on five categories including "Commerce" protocols (x402, MPP, UCP, ACP). dmarcheck already leans hard into agent discovery (RFC 9727 api-catalog, Agent Skills RFC v0.2.0, OpenAPI 3.1, WebMCP) — supporting x402 is consistent with that posture, and x402 has the most momentum (Coinbase-backed, real SDKs, real merchant directory). The free `/check` API is fully agent-discoverable today; the only friction for an agent is the 10/60s rate limit. Pro is $19/mo monthly subscription, which doesn't fit per-call agent commerce. This is a marketing bet, not a revenue play — the revenue ceiling is tiny but the discovery upside is real if we're early.

## Motivation

**User story:** As an AI agent that needs to scan more than 10 domains/minute, I want to pay per scan via x402 so I can keep working without a human in the loop creating an account and entering a credit card.

**What triggered the ask:** isitagentready.com surfaced this as a gap; weighing whether early adoption could drive traction back to dmarc.mx via agent-discovery directories.

## Real economics (the load-bearing part — do not skip)

**Marginal cost per scan on Cloudflare Workers Paid ($5/mo base):**
- Worker invocation: $0.30 / 1M after the included 10M = **$0.0000003/scan**
- CPU time: ~30ms typical → $0.02 / 1M ms after the included 30M ms = **~$0.0000006/scan**
- Subrequests (DNS + MTA-STS HTTPS + security.txt HTTPS): included in Workers fee, no marginal $
- Cache API (rate limit + result cache): free
- D1 (analytics writes if enabled): negligible at this scale

**Total compute marginal cost: ~$0.000001/scan (one-millionth of a dollar).**

**Crypto rail cost (x402 on Base USDC):**
- Base L2 gas for USDC transfer: ~$0.0001–$0.001/settlement
- Coinbase x402 facilitator: free at time of writing
- **Crypto rails dominate marginal cost at ~$0.001/scan**

**Pricing recommendation:** $0.005/scan as a defensible test number.
- Floor: $0.001 (covers crypto rails, breaks even)
- Ceiling cross-check: Pro $19/mo at ~5k scans/mo = $0.0038/scan; at 10k scans/mo = $0.0019/scan. We must price *at or above* Pro per-call equivalent or we cannibalize the subscription.
- $0.005/scan: clears Pro per-call rate for a 4k-scan/mo user, ~5x marginal cost, simple round number, "half a cent per scan" reads well in marketing copy.
- Alternative: $0.001/scan as an aggressive marketing posture ("scan a domain for a tenth of a cent"), accepting that it's break-even at best.

**Revenue ceiling sanity check:** Even at 100k paid scans/mo (an optimistic outcome), $0.005/scan = $500/mo gross, minus gas. This is a marketing bet, not a P&L line item. Frame the success metric as referral traffic from agent directories, not USDC received.

## Pointers

- `src/rate-limit.ts:17` — `FREE_CONFIG = { limit: 10, windowSec: 60 }`. The x402-gated endpoint should sit *above* this limit, not replace it.
- `src/index.ts:346` — `rateLimitMiddleware` and the Pro-bearer identity logic. New endpoint should reuse this with a higher / no limit when payment is verified.
- `src/index.ts:416` — existing `/check` handler; the new endpoint likely mirrors this but adds an x402 middleware in front.
- `src/api/openapi.ts` and `src/api/catalog.ts` — the new endpoint needs to be advertised here so agents can discover it.
- `CLAUDE.md` "Agent discovery" section — update to document the new well-known path / endpoint.
- x402 spec: https://docs.x402.org/getting-started/quickstart-for-sellers — Hono middleware exists (`x402-hono` or similar); confirm Workers compatibility before committing.
- isitagentready.com scoring: https://isitagentready.com/dmarc.mx — re-run after deploy to confirm score moved.

## Constraints

- **Workers runtime only** — no Node-specific APIs in the x402 middleware. Verify the chosen SDK's compatibility before integration.
- **No private key in source or env vars without KMS-style protection.** Receiving wallet's private key must be in Cloudflare Secrets, never `wrangler.toml`. Prefer a watch-only address that settles to a custodial wallet (Coinbase Commerce, Base smart wallet) over self-custody.
- **Free tier untouched.** Existing `/check` stays free at 10/60s. x402 lives on a *new* path (e.g. `/check/paid` or `/v1/scan`), not gating the public endpoint.
- **No new dependencies in the hot path of free scans.** x402 SDK only loaded for the paid route.
- **Discovery surfaces updated atomically** — `/openapi.json`, `/.well-known/api-catalog`, and `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` must all reference the new endpoint in the same PR that ships it.
- **30-day kill switch.** Ship behind a wrangler-vars feature flag so we can disable without a deploy if abuse or cost surprises appear.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New paid endpoint deployed (e.g. `/v1/scan`) returns HTTP 402 with valid x402 `payment-required` headers when called without payment proof.
- [ ] Endpoint accepts a valid x402 payment proof for $0.005 USDC on Base mainnet and returns the same JSON shape as `/check`.
- [ ] Rate limit on the paid endpoint is meaningfully higher than free (e.g. 100 req/IP/60s) or absent.
- [ ] Endpoint advertised in `/openapi.json`, `/.well-known/api-catalog`, and `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`.
- [ ] Receiving wallet address is a custodial / smart-wallet setup, not a self-custody EOA private key in env vars.
- [ ] Feature flag (`X402_ENABLED` wrangler var) gates the route so it can be disabled without a deploy.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "Agent discovery" section updated to describe the paid endpoint.
- [ ] isitagentready.com re-scan run and result attached to the PR.

## Out of scope

- MPP / UCP / ACP support. Ship x402 first; revisit the others after the 30-day observation window based on which (if any) gain traction.
- Replacing the Pro $19/mo subscription with pay-per-call. Pro is for humans/SaaS; x402 is for agents.
- Building a Coinbase Commerce / fiat off-ramp UI. Receiving wallet flows are out-of-band ops, not a product surface.
- Pricing experiments beyond the initial $0.005/scan. Ship one price, observe, then iterate in a separate issue.

## Reasoning guidance

Think carefully and step-by-step before responding; this is a marketing bet with crypto-custody risk, and the wrong wallet architecture is hard to undo. Validate the Workers-runtime compatibility of the chosen x402 SDK *before* writing any integration code — if no Workers-compatible SDK exists, surface that and stop, don't shim around it.

## Cross-references

- isitagentready.com scoring methodology (commerce category): https://isitagentready.com/dmarc.mx
- Existing agent-discovery work: https://github.com/schmug/dmarcheck/issues/181 (MCP server tracker, mentioned in CLAUDE.md)

body:
## Problem

The cross-model consensus / cross-family red-team gate is meant to be a **$0 token-saver** (fleet +
free-cloud raters instead of paid review). In practice each run incurs heavy **operator
troubleshooting overhead** that eats the savings — observed live on the #3125 consensus run
(2026-06-19):

- **Provider-name drift**: `google-ai-studio`/`github-models` were wrong keys vs the actual
  `gemini`/`github-models` registry entries; one rater silently failed as `unknown_provider`.
- **Dead free endpoints**: OpenRouter retired free DeepSeek/Qwen/Llama-4 ("use paid slug", HTTP
  404); Google AI Studio key returns HTTP 429 "credits depleted" (the real root cause of the
  long-standing "gemini flakes empty").
- **Fleet reached only via the LiteLLM gateway**: `cascade-dispatch` probed `:4000` (gateway
  unhealthy) and failed straight to free-cloud, never trying the **direct Tailscale Ollama hosts**
  (`100.91.113.16:11434` = qwen3:32b/qwen2.5-coder:32b; `100.78.22.13:11434` = deepseek/granite) —
  so the best $0 cross-family substrate was skipped.
- **Host overload**: 4 large models dispatched in parallel (2 per host) all aborted — Ollama
  serializes per host; needs sequential scheduling + cold-load budgeting.
- **Model-capability blind spots**: qwen3:32b is a *thinking* model (empty content at low
  num_predict) and runs ~1.5 tok/s with a 64s cold-load — no registry told the dispatcher to set
  `think:false` or budget the latency.
- **Numeric-gate unreachability**: when the free panel collapses to a correlated Llama-70B trio +
  Mistral, scores anchor at 82 and a `>93` gate is structurally unreachable — yet the loop has no
  "consensus-max on available panel" honest-stop, so it burns iterations.

Net: the savings are real but the per-run overhead (operator time + tokens spent troubleshooting +
wasted dispatches) frequently exceeds them. Filed incident:
`freecloud-rater-panel-collapsed-to-anchored-pair`.

## Goal

Make the cross-model consensus workflow **low-overhead and self-healing**, so the $0 savings are
net-positive without operator babysitting. Keep it LEAN (no new paid infra; no new heavy framework).

## Acceptance criteria (Epic-level)

- AC1: A **preflight** that, in one cheap call, reports each rater's reachability + key validity +
  family, and emits the usable panel BEFORE a run (no mid-run `unknown_provider`/`no_key`/`429`
  surprises).
- AC2: **Direct fleet dispatch** — the dispatcher tries the Tailscale Ollama hosts directly (not only
  the LiteLLM gateway), with per-host **sequential scheduling** + cold-load budgeting.
- AC3: A small **model-capability registry** (family, size, thinking-flag, rough tok/s, default
  timeout) consumed by the dispatcher (sets `think:false`, sizes timeouts, discounts small models).
- AC4: **Graceful degradation + honest reporting** — when the panel cannot reach the gate (too few
  independent families), emit `consensus-max=<N> on <families>` and stop, not infinite iteration.
- AC5: **Telemetry** proving net savings — per-run overhead (failed dispatches, retries, wall-time)
  vs paid-review cost avoided, so the workflow's own ROI is auditable.

## Constraints / goal-lens

G3 (the point): never let troubleshooting overhead exceed the savings. G6 resilience: degrade, never
hang. G5: no user-specific coupling (host list settings-driven). G1: still cross-family (no Anthropic
rater); honest gate (no gaming the score).

## Relation
Sibling to Epic #3124 (memory/doc retention). This Epic optimizes the *review substrate* that #3124
(and all governed work) depends on. Evidence source: #3125.
title: Optimize the cross-model consensus workflow to cut troubleshooting overhead

## Summary

A reservoir-style Lean 4 library that lets contract authors and auditors
formally verify safety properties of FunC source and TVM bytecode using
machine-checked proofs.  Pitched as a Mi-Cho-Coq sibling for TON:
public, lakefile-installable, dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.

**Repo:** https://github.com/MavenRain/tvm-lean4
**Status:** Scaffold pushed, `lake build` green (23 modules), no proofs yet.

## Problem

TON's smart contract auditing landscape is empirically nascent.  Yanovich
et al. (arXiv 2509.10823, revised 2026-04-16) catalog 233 real-world
vulnerabilities across 34 audit reports and observe that TON-specific
concerns, asynchronous message handling chief among them, do not map
cleanly onto Ethereum auditing patterns.

CertiK formally verified TON's masterchain `elector` and `config`
contracts ahead of mainnet by manually translating FunC into Coq and
proving safety properties by hand.  The effort caught two concrete bugs
including a validator-fund-loss issue, but was never released as a
reusable tool.  No public, package-manager-installable formal
verification framework exists for TVM bytecode or FunC source.

The closest existing TON-side tool in this category is `TonAudit AI`
(#1213), which uses an LLM-prompted vulnerability scanner.  That tool is
complementary to but categorically different from a deductive formal
verification framework: LLM scanning gives a probabilistic finding with
no guarantee, while a machine-checked Lean 4 proof gives a permanent
mathematical certificate.

## Solution

`tvm-lean4` is a Lean 4 library structured as a reusable lakefile
dependency.  The framework provides:

1. A small-step semantics for the TVM instruction set, modeled as a
   relation on `(Stack, Cell, ControlState)` triples.
2. A FunC frontend that lowers source AST to TVM bytecode, with a
   Lean-checked correctness theorem stating the lowering preserves
   semantics for well-typed programs.
3. An asynchronous-message envelope model (`InternalMessage`,
   `BounceFlag`, `Address`) so that contract specifications can quantify
   over inter-shard delivery and bounce-on-failure.
4. A specification language inspired by Mi-Cho-Coq's Hoare-triple
   encoding, letting authors state pre/post conditions about a
   contract's storage and outgoing messages.

Downstream users add `require «tvm-lean4» from git ...` to their own
lakefile and write proofs about contracts they have written.

## What's already built

A scaffold of the five core modules, with the build green:

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| `TvmLean4.Word` | `Int257` 257-bit signed integer with bounded-range proof witness and a smart constructor `ofInt?` |
| `TvmLean4.Cell` | `Cell` inductive type, `maxBits = 1023`, `maxRefs = 4`, shallow `WellFormed` |
| `TvmLean4.Slice` | `Slice` read cursor into a cell, shallow `WellFormed` |
| `TvmLean4.Stack` | `StackValue` sum (int / cell / slice / builder / tuple / cont / null), `Stack` abbrev |
| `TvmLean4.Message` | `InternalMessage` envelope, `BounceFlag`, `Address` |

Build:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/MavenRain/tvm-lean4
cd tvm-lean4
lake update
lake build
```

Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc1`.  `kan-tactics` pinned by
SHA in `lakefile.lean`.

## Roadmap

### Milestone 1: TVM step relation for the contract-relevant instruction core ($1.5K)

Formalize the small-step semantics for around 50 TVM instructions
covering stack manipulation (`PUSH`, `POP`, `DUP`, `SWAP`, `ROT`),
arithmetic (`ADD`, `SUB`, `MUL`, `DIV`, `MOD`, comparisons), control
flow (`IFRET`, `CALLREF`, `JMPREF`), and cell operations (`NEWC`,
`ENDC`, `STX`, `CTOS`, `LDX`).  This is the instruction subset that
covers the standard Jetton minter, Jetton wallet, and NFT collection
contracts.

Lean-checked theorems delivered:

* `step_deterministic`: at most one successor state for any given
  current state.
* `step_preserves_well_formed`: well-formed states step to well-formed
  states.

### Milestone 2: FunC frontend and bytecode lowering ($1.5K)

A FunC AST in Lean and a lowering function from FunC source to TVM
bytecode covering the M1 instruction subset.  Lean-checked theorem:
`lowering_preserves_semantics`, the source-level evaluator and the
bytecode evaluator agree on terminating well-typed programs.

This is the reusable, machine-checked analogue of the manual translation
CertiK performed for `elector` and `config`.

### Milestone 3: Worked example: Jetton minter total-supply conservation ($2K)

End-to-end demonstration: the Jetton minter contract is verified to
preserve total supply across `mint` and `burn`, including the
bounce-on-failure case where a mint message bounces back to the
minter and the supply must be decremented.

This proof exercises every layer of the framework (Word arithmetic,
Cell encoding, Stack manipulation, async Message handling) and
produces a public, replayable Lean proof object that downstream users
can study as a template.

## Requested funding

Total: **$5,000 USDT**, paid per milestone.

Milestone 1: $1,500
Milestone 2: $1,500
Milestone 3: $2,000

Funding pays for the development time required to bring the framework
from architectural scaffold to a working end-to-end FV pipeline with
one canonical verified contract.

## Relevant links

* Repo: https://github.com/MavenRain/tvm-lean4
* Mi-Cho-Coq (the Tezos analogue this work is modeled on):
  https://gitlab.com/nomadic-labs/mi-cho-coq
* `kan-tactics`, the proof-tactic library used throughout:
  https://github.com/MavenRain/kan-tactics
* CertiK formal verification of TON masterchain `elector` and `config`:
  https://www.certik.com/resources/blog/formal-verification-of-ton-master-chain-contracts
* Yanovich et al. on the TON audit landscape:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10823

## License

Dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.  Public goods.
title: tvm-lean4 — Lean 4 Formal Verification Framework for TVM and FunC
