## Summary `gitnexus analyze --skills` (and `gitnexus setup`) inject a ~101-line **"GitNexus — Code Intelligence"** block, *identically*, into both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. This is **invasive**: it mutates the user's checked-in instruction files and dominates them (CLAUDE.md ≈ 66% injected, AGENTS.md ≈ 50%), spending always-on context every turn of every session. Most of the block **duplicates guidance the agent already receives through cheaper channels GitNexus already ships**: on-demand **skills**, **MCP tool descriptions**, **MCP per-response hints**, and **hooks** (grep-augment + post-commit staleness). This is an *altitude* problem — the heavy manual sits in the most expensive tier (always-on repo files) when it belongs in cheaper, demand-driven tiers. **Goal:** shrink the always-on, repo-file footprint by ~90% to a small, stable pointer; push the manual to per-session / on-demand channels GitNexus already owns; add a clean opt-out — without losing the behavioral enforcement that makes GitNexus useful. ## Current state (findings) **Injection mechanism** — `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts` - `generateGitNexusContent()` (L41–151): single hardcoded template literal; interpolates **volatile stats** (`nodes`/`edges`/`processes`) + project name → this is what makes the block churn on re-index. - `upsertGitNexusSection()` (L172–202): marker-based (`` / `:end`) create/replace/append. **Re-runs cleanly replace the block** → slimming the template auto-migrates existing files. - `generateAIContextFiles()` (L283–310): writes the **same content to both** `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, then `installSkills()` lays down 6 skills. - Triggered by `gitnexus setup` (always) and `gitnexus analyze --skills` (opt-in). Plain `analyze` deliberately skips it (avoids stat churn, see `scaffold.ts` header + #108). **No flag / env var / config key disables it today.** **Footprint** — ~101 lines / ~1.6k tokens **per file**, written into **both** → ~3.2k always-on tokens, 100% duplicated across the two files. Sections: Always Do / When Debugging / When Refactoring / Never Do / Tools Quick-Reference table / Impact Risk Levels table / Resources table / Self-Check checklist / Keeping-the-Index-Fresh prose / CLI skill table. **Redundancy** — ~40% of the block duplicates content available elsewhere: | Guidance | Also lives in | |----------|---------------| | Tools quick-reference | MCP tool descriptions (`mcp/tools.ts`) | | Impact risk levels (d=1/2/3) | `gitnexus-impact-analysis` + `gitnexus-guide` skills; `impact()` output | | Resources list | `gitnexus-guide` skill; tool descriptions | | Debugging / Refactoring workflows | full versions in the respective skills | | Keep-index-fresh | PostToolUse staleness hook + `gitnexus-cli` skill | **Unused lever** — `gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts` constructs `Server` (L87–99) **without an `instructions` field**. MCP server `instructions` are loaded once per session by clients on connect (how serena/context7 instructions appear in-session) — the natural, repo-file-free home for the manual, present only for agents actually using the tools. ## Design — deliver each tier of guidance at the right altitude ```mermaid graph TD subgraph T1["Tier 1 - ALWAYS-ON (repo files) - keep tiny + stable"] P["~10-line pointer in CLAUDE.md & AGENTS.md
capability + 1 behavioral nudge + where-to-look
NO stats, NO tables, NO workflows"] end subgraph T2["Tier 2 - PER-SESSION (no repo mutation)"] MCP["MCP server instructions field (NEW in server.ts)
tools ref - risk levels - Always/Never - condensed workflows - resources"] SK["Skills (.claude/skills/gitnexus/*) - deep workflows, on-demand"] end subgraph T3["Tier 3 - JUST-IN-TIME (hooks + response hints)"] H1["PostToolUse: post-commit staleness (exists)"] H2["PreToolUse: grep/glob graph-augment (exists)"] H3["PreToolUse on Edit/Write: impact reminder (NEW)"] HINT["MCP per-response next-step hints (exists)"] end P -.points to.-> MCP P -.points to.-> SK AG["gitnexus analyze --skills / setup"] --> P AG --> SK ``` **Content re-allocation:** - **Tier 1 (repo files), slimmed to ~10 lines, content-stable:** "Repo indexed by GitNexus — use its MCP tools + skills for impact analysis, safe rename, execution-flow search. Run impact analysis before editing indexed symbols; prefer graph `query` over grep. Deep workflows: `.claude/skills/gitnexus/`." **Drop volatile stats** (move to MCP instructions / `…/context` resource) so the block no longer churns — meaning it can safely be written even on plain `analyze`. - **Tier 2 (MCP `instructions`, NEW):** the migrated manual — tools quick-reference, impact risk levels, Always/Never rules, condensed debug/refactor sequences, resources. Lives in the server, not the repo. ~700–900 tokens, paid once per session, only when the gitnexus MCP is connected. - **Tier 2 skills:** unchanged (already installed); they remain the authoritative deep references the pointer links to. - **Tier 3 hooks/hints:** keep existing; the post-commit staleness hook makes the "Keeping the Index Fresh" prose redundant → drop it from Tier 1. **Add** a non-blocking PreToolUse hook on `Edit|Write`: when `.gitnexus/` exists in the tree, emit a one-line `additionalContext` reminder to run `gitnexus_impact` on the symbols being changed (file-level reminder — the agent names the symbol). Strongest enforcement of the #1 rule, delivered exactly when relevant, at zero always-on cost. Never blocks; no-op outside indexed repos; **deduped per-file-per-session** so it doesn't repeat on every edit to the same file. **Governance / opt-out (NEW):** an `agentFiles` config (`mode: "lean" | "full" | "off"`, default `lean`; optional `targets`). `lean` = the pointer; `full` = today's block (back-compat); `off` = no repo-file mutation at all (pure MCP + skills + hooks). Read from repo-level `.gitnexus/config.json` (preferred) with global `~/.gitnexus/config.json` fallback. Directly answers the "invasive" complaint with a one-setting escape hatch. ## Implementation tasks - [ ] **`gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts`** — Replace `generateGitNexusContent()` body with a **lean pointer template** (no stats interpolation). Keep the markers + `upsertGitNexusSection()` as-is (auto-migrates existing blocks). Add a `mode` parameter threaded from config; `full` keeps the current text (extract current template into `generateFullContent()` for back-compat); `off` short-circuits `generateAIContextFiles()` to skip the two `upsert` calls (still install skills). - [ ] **`gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts`** — Add `instructions: GITNEXUS_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS` to the `Server(...)` options (L87–99). Define the constant in a new small module (e.g. `mcp/instructions.ts`) holding the migrated manual. *(Verify the MCP SDK `ServerOptions.instructions` field name against the installed `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` version.)* - [ ] **Config** — Extend the GitNexus `CLIConfig` (`repo-manager.ts`, ~L346–352, currently LLM-only) with an `agentFiles` block (`mode` default `lean`, optional `targets`). Resolve repo-level `.gitnexus/config.json` over global `~/.gitnexus/config.json`. Thread `mode` through `scaffold.ts` (`scaffoldAIContextForIndexedRepos` → `generateAIContextFiles`). - [ ] **Hook** — In the bundled hook template the CLI ships (installed to `~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs`), add a PreToolUse `Edit|Write` branch alongside the existing grep-augment branch (`handlePreToolUse`): if `findGitNexusDir(cwd)` resolves, emit a one-line non-blocking `additionalContext` impact reminder via `sendHookResponse`; dedupe per-file-per-session (e.g. marker file under the OS temp dir keyed by session id + file path); no-op / fast otherwise; never blocks. - [ ] **`docs/adr/ADR-001-lean-gitnexus-agent-file-injection.md`** — Record the decision (see ADR summary below); create `docs/adr/` if absent. ## Fitness functions (guard against re-bloat) Add unit tests in the gitnexus package: 1. **Tier-1 size cap:** `lean` block ≤ ~20 lines / ≤ ~400 tokens. 2. **Stability invariant:** generating the `lean` block with two different `stats` objects yields **identical** output (no volatile content → no git churn). 3. **MCP instructions present:** `createMCPServer` exposes a non-empty `instructions` containing the tools/risk-level reference. 4. **Mode behavior:** `off` writes neither file; `full` reproduces the legacy block (back-compat). ## Verification (end-to-end) 1. `cd gitnexus && npm run build && npm test` — new fitness tests pass; existing suite green. 2. Scratch repo: `npx gitnexus analyze --skills` (default `lean`) → `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` get the ~10-line pointer, no stats, no churn on a second run (`git diff` empty after re-analyze). 3. `mode: "off"` → re-run → no marker block written, skills still installed. 4. Connect the MCP server (or inspect the `initialize` response) → `instructions` carries the manual. 5. Trigger an `Edit` in a `.gitnexus` repo → the non-blocking impact reminder appears and does not block the edit. ## ADR summary (to be written to `docs/adr/ADR-001-…`) - **Context:** Always-on injection of a ~101-line manual into two tracked agent files duplicates guidance available through cheaper, demand-driven channels GitNexus already ships; it taxes every session and clutters user-owned files. - **Decision:** Deliver guidance at the right altitude. Tier 1 (repo files) keeps only a ~10-line, stat-free, content-stable pointer. The manual moves to the MCP server `instructions` field (per-session, repo-file-free) plus existing skills. Behavioral enforcement of impact-before-edit moves to a just-in-time, non-blocking PreToolUse `Edit|Write` hook. A `mode: lean|full|off` config gives a clean opt-out. - **Consequences — positive:** ~90% cut in always-on repo-file tokens; pointer no longer churns on re-index (safe to write even on plain `analyze`); single source of truth per tier; users can opt out. **Negative / risks:** MCP-instructions manual is absent for agents that read the files but don't connect the MCP server (mitigated by `full` mode + skills); the Edit/Write hook adds a hook-maintenance surface (mitigated by dedupe + no-op-when-uninstalled + never-block). - **Fitness functions:** the four tests above are the regression guards. ## Decisions confirmed Tiered (lean pointer + MCP `instructions`) · ship the non-blocking Edit/Write impact hook · ship the `mode: lean|full|off` config (default `lean`). --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Lean GitNexus agent-file injection: stop bloating CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, move the manual to MCP instructions + hooks

## Summary

Design the data model and storage approach for the job-application tracker. The app is a **generic personal job-application tracker** (RAV submission itself is handled by the official RAV web portal, so there is **no need** to replicate RAV form 716.007 or generate a PDF). The focus is on monitoring every application through its full lifecycle, with a detailed timeline and file attachments.

## Goals

- Track each job application from **exploring** (not submitted yet) all the way to a terminal outcome.
- Monitor **every step**, including on-hold periods and inbound contact (e.g. "they wrote to schedule an interview").
- Attach evidence to steps: emails, screenshots, images, PDFs.
- Keep it lean; avoid infrastructure that could generate surprise bills.

## Data model

### `application` — the opportunity
One row per job applied to. Carries a **current status** for a quick pipeline/Kanban view.

Fields:
- `company` (employer) + **agency or direct** (`agency_id` null = applied directly)
- `role` / position
- `location` (+ remote flag)
- **contract type** — TBD: employment type (permanent / fixed-term / freelance / internship) and/or workload (full-time / part-time)
- `posting_url`
- `applied_on` (anchors the application in time)
- `status` (current snapshot — see lifecycle below)

### Status lifecycle (pipeline)
- `EXPLORING` — found it, interested, not submitted yet
- `APPLIED` — submitted
- `INTERVIEWING` — in the interview process
- `OFFER` — they made an offer
- `REJECTED` — they said no
- `WITHDRAWN` — I pulled out / turned them down

Open question: model **on-hold** as an orthogonal flag/pause (can happen at any stage) rather than a pipeline stage, so we don't lose track of where the application actually is.

### `application_event` — the timeline (the core content)
A dated journal of everything that happens to an application. Each entry has a type, a date, and an optional note. Types e.g.: applied, reply received, interview scheduled, interview done, on hold, offer, rejected, withdrawn, note.

- **Current status** = derived from / kept in sync with the latest status-changing event.
- **Timeline** = the full event history ("how did this one unfold").
- Every status change is itself a dated event, so "did they reply?" is captured for free.

### `attachment` — evidence on events
Files linked to a timeline event (email, screenshot, image, PDF). DB stores metadata + a storage reference; bytes live in the storage backend (below).

## Storage approach

Put file storage behind a small **`StorageService`** interface (`store` / `retrieve` / `delete`) so the backend is swappable and, eventually, **per-user selectable**.

- **v1:** `LocalFilesystemStorageService` writing to a **Hetzner Volume** (durable block storage, snapshot-backed) — not the VM root disk. Optionally Hetzner S3-compatible Object Storage later.
- **Later (per-user backends):** resolve the implementation from a per-user setting:
  - Free tier → server storage (shared quota)
  - "Link my own Google Drive" → per-user OAuth, files land in their Drive (zero cost to us)
  - Paid tier → managed object storage (e.g. Azure Blob)

## Cost safety (avoid surprise bills)

Metered/paid features must be **off by default, gated per user, and capped at the provider**:

1. **Free default path touches zero metered services** (local FS / user's own Drive).
2. **Per-user entitlement** — a `plan` (`FREE`/`PRO`) or simple allowlist flag on `app_user`; expensive features check it and refuse otherwise. Additive — can be added the day the first paid backend lands.
3. **Hard caps at the provider** — Azure budget/spending limit, Anthropic API monthly spend cap + per-user token budgets, and in-app per-user quotas/rate limits enforced before calling any paid service.

## Non-goals / decisions made

- ❌ No RAV form 716.007 replication or PDF export (RAV web portal handles submission).
- ✅ Ownership designed in from day one (`app_user` + `user_id` FK); auth (Keycloak) deferred.
- ✅ Tables/columns in English.

## Open questions

- [ ] "Contract type": employment type, workload, or both?
- [ ] "On hold": orthogonal flag vs. pipeline status?
- [ ] Interview rounds: distinguish phone screen / on-site / final, or one `INTERVIEWING` bucket with details in the note?
- [ ] `status` denormalized on `application` vs. purely derived from latest event?
- [ ] Hetzner Volume (plain FS) vs. Hetzner Object Storage for v1.
title: Design: application lifecycle tracking, timeline with attachments, and swappable storage

## Problem

The `note` field is the single largest item in claim payloads — real-world notes run 1000+ chars. Because MCP tool results stay in the model's context for the rest of the session, and every `get_claims` / `register_agent` call re-emits the full claim array, other agents' full notes are paid for on every poll, repeatedly, for the whole session.

This is the largest remaining contributor to dibs MCP context usage after the payload-slimming and compact-JSON work (slimming the structural fields already landed; notes are user/agent-authored content that can't simply be dropped).

## Options to consider

- **Truncate in list views**: return notes truncated (e.g. first ~200 chars + ellipsis) from `get_claims` / `register_agent`, and only the full note when a claim is fetched directly or filtered by `path`.
- **Hard cap note length** at write time (`create_claim` / `update_claim`).
- **Separate "summary" vs "detail"**: a short `title` is already required; lean on it for list views and make full notes opt-in.

## Trade-off

This trades coordination richness for tokens — agents currently use long notes to explain scope/intent to each other. Truncation in list views (full note on direct fetch) seems like the best balance, but it's a product decision.

## Context

Surfaced while optimizing dibs MCP token usage (it was ~39% of one session's context). Structural slimming + compact JSON already cut ~22% per `get_claims` call; this is the next lever but needs a judgment call.
title: Cap or truncate claim notes in list views to cut persistent MCP context cost

Goal: leave Next.js/OpenNext for a Cloudflare-native stack so the app fits the **free Workers plan** (the OpenNext worker is 4.49 MiB gzipped vs the 3 MiB free cap; see #95 thread) and drops the Vercel dependency entirely. Data layer (D1/R2) and auth (better-auth on D1) are already CF-native and migrated — this is a **frontend/runtime** rewrite, not a data one.

## Why it fits free Workers
A Hono worker + React SPA served via **Workers Static Assets** keeps the *worker script* tiny (hundreds of KB); the React bundle ships as **assets, which are not counted against the 3 MiB script limit**. No paid plan needed.

## Target stack
- **Hono** on Workers — routing + serving + API (de-facto CF standard, tiny).
- **Vite + React** SPA — reuse existing client components; client-side router (react-router/TanStack Router).
- **Workers Static Assets** for the SPA bundle.
- **better-auth** (kysely/D1 path, already working) mounted in Hono.
- **D1 + R2** bindings — unchanged.
- **intlayer** via its Vite/React integration (`react-intlayer`) — keep the 16 content files, avoid an i18n rewrite.
- **Prerender** landing + blog routes to static HTML for SEO (Vite SSG / small prerender step).

## Reuse as-is (no rewrite)
D1/R2 repos (`lib/repos`, `lib/d1`), better-auth setup, FSRS core (`app/fsrs.ts` logic), AI integrations (fetch-based), the Tampermonkey userscript (framework-agnostic), most of the **36 `use client` components**, the 16 intlayer dictionaries.

## Must rebuild
- Routing: Next App Router (24 pages) → Hono routes + client router.
- SSR/RSC → SPA (+ prerender for landing/blog/SEO pages).
- 29 `app/api/*/route.ts` → Hono route handlers (mechanical; reuse the lib logic).
- Build/deploy: Next/OpenNext → Vite + wrangler.

## Inventory (current)
24 pages/layouts · 29 API routes · 61 React components (36 client) · 16 intlayer content files.

## Phases (incremental, on a branch; Vercel stays prod throughout)
1. **Scaffold** — Hono worker + Vite React SPA + Workers Assets; wire DB/BLOBS/auth bindings; deploy a hello-world to confirm free-plan size + workers.dev.
2. **Backend parity** — port all 29 routes to Hono; validate with the existing API/sync test suites.
3. **App shell + core flow** — SPA shell, client router, intlayer; port the main review flow (`/list`, add-note, review) reusing client components.
4. **Remaining features** — roadmap, read, polyglot, ai-vocab, import, membership, preferences, profile, contact.
5. **Auth UI** — sign-in, OAuth callbacks (register workers.dev + lianki.com redirect URIs), logout, membership gating.
6. **SEO** — prerender landing + blog.
7. **Parity QA** — port qa:all suites; full feature walkthrough vs current prod.
8. **Cutover** — deploy (now fits free plan), smoke-test workers.dev, point `lianki.com` at the Worker; keep Vercel as instant DNS rollback until soaked.

## Risks / decisions
- SSR/SEO loss on app pages (fine — they're behind auth) ; landing/blog need prerender.
- intlayer's Vite integration parity with its Next integration — validate early in Phase 1.
- OAuth redirect URIs must be added for the new origin(s).
- Long tail of 24 pages — effort is **weeks**, not days. Keep prod on Vercel the whole time.

## Tradeoff (recorded)
This is a multi-week rewrite whose immediate trigger is avoiding a $5/mo Workers Paid plan — but it also yields a leaner, single-platform, Vercel-free app with no OpenNext complexity. If timeline matters more than platform purity, Workers Paid unblocks the existing app today with zero code change (everything else for that path is already staged).
title: Rewrite Lianki as a CF-native app (Hono + Vite/React SPA + Workers Assets), retire Next.js

Research findings from a `/deep-research` run (2026-07-02) on **how to use Claude to generate
high-quality, stylistically-consistent assets** across all four categories: visual/game art, audio,
store/marketing, and in-game text/narrative. Priority was **quality & consistency across a large asset
set**, with Claude orchestrating paid AI tools (Midjourney/Flux/ElevenLabs) where useful.

Filed to pursue later — this is a **backlog/research** issue, not a scoped code change. No production
code is touched by filing it.

**Method:** 5 search angles → ~15 sources fetched → claims extracted → **3-vote adversarial
verification** per claim (2/3 refutes kills it) → synthesis. **20 claims survived, 5 refuted.** Every
finding below carries its source + confidence; refuted claims are listed at the end so we don't act on
them. Time-sensitive items (2025–26 tool behaviour) are flagged for re-verification at implementation.

---

## Headline insight (reframes the whole approach)

**The battle renderer already draws 100% procedurally in Kotlin/Canvas — zero raster sprites.** Verified
against our own code: enemies are `drawRect` (`EnemyEntity.kt:130`), projectiles/orbs are `drawCircle`,
the ziggurat is stacked `drawRect` layers (`ZigguratEntity.kt:108`), biome skies are `LinearGradient`
shaders (`BackgroundRenderer.kt`), HP bars/floating text via `drawRect`/`drawText`; **no `drawBitmap` in
main**. [Confidence: **high** — primary Android docs + our codebase]

Consequence for the #1 goal (consistency): **code-drawn art is deterministic and governed by a single
source of truth** — a stochastic image generator fights consistency, a Kotlin function does not. So split
the asset problem in two:

- **Code-drawable** (in-battle entities, projectiles, particles, biome backgrounds, many UI shapes) →
  **Claude writes/refactors Kotlin.** Perfect consistency, free, version-controlled, no licensing questions.
- **Raster-only** (app icon, Play feature graphic, marketing art, detailed illustrated UI icons) →
  **Claude orchestrates Midjourney/Flux** with the consistency techniques below.

---

## 1) Visual / game art

**Procedural (default for in-battle visuals):**
- Canvas primitives cover a large class of needs — `drawText`, `drawRect`/`drawOval`/`drawArc`,
  `Path`/`drawPath`, `LinearGradient`+`setShader`, `drawBitmap`. UI icons, projectiles, biome background
  elements can be generated in code. [primary: Android custom-drawing docs + codebase; **high**]
- Particles: **one config governs the whole visual style** (a code-parameterized emitter with `colors`,
  `particleShapes`, `blendMode`, physics) → consistency by construction. [primary: PiotrPrus/ParticleEmitter
  README; **high**]. ⚠️ The "1,000+ particles high-performance" perf claim for that library was **refuted** —
  benchmark on-device, don't rely on the number.
  - *Claude's role:* author per-biome/effect particle configs + the Kotlin that consumes them (feeds
    `EffectEngine`/`ParticlePool`).

**Raster (app icon, marketing, illustrated assets):**
- **Midjourney `--sref`** transfers visual vibe (colors/medium/textures/lighting) without copying
  objects — core batch-consistency mechanism. [primary: MJ docs; **medium**]. ⚠️ separation isn't perfect
  ("subject leakage"); it's for *style*, not character identity.
- **`--sref <code>`** numeric style codes → **reusable, repeatable** aesthetic anchor across many assets.
  [primary: MJ docs, 3-0; **high**]. ⚠️ produces a consistent *aesthetic*, **not identical images**; shifts
  with MJ version, seed, `--sw` (0–1000, default 100).
- **Character consistency:** `--cref` recreates a character (hair/clothes/face) across images; `--cw` dial
  (`100` = full detail incl. clothing/hair, `0` = face only). [primary: MJ docs, 3-0; **high**].
  ⚠️ **Currency:** `--cref` is pre-V7; on **V7 (2025–26) docs steer to Omni Reference (`--oref`/`--ow`)** —
  use Omni Reference if on V7.
- **Best consistency:** seed the reference with a **Midjourney-created single-character image**; real-photo
  refs "won't look exactly like them," fine details (freckles/logos) won't reproduce. [primary: MJ docs, 3-0; **high**]
- **Flux route (stronger identity locking):** ready-made **`gokaygokay/Flux-Game-Assets-LoRA-v2`**
  (FLUX.1-dev, Apache-2.0) → game props/icons (castles, crowns, shields, swords, chests, warriors/wizards)
  on white background. Style anchored by required trigger **`wbgmsst`** + fixed template
  (`wbgmsst, <prompt>, white background`). [primary: HF model card, 3-0; **high**]. Good fit for UW/upgrade
  icon batches.
- **Max character-identity locking:** train a subject-specific Flux LoRA + prompt constraints → one
  character consistent across wildly different environments. [blog + corroborating 2025–26 sources, 3-0;
  **medium** — lead source was a personal blog]. Needs tuning (strength ~0.75–0.85; 10–20 test gens; too high
  bleeds into background).

**Recommended raster consistency stack:** (1) Claude authors a **style bible** (hex palette, line weight,
lighting, Babylonian-ziggurat descriptors, per-biome mood). (2) Lock **one `--sref` code / LoRA / Omni
Reference** as the anchor on *all* prompts. (3) Claude generates the **batch of prompts** (6 enemies × states,
5 biomes, UW icons) from the bible. (4) Claude as **art-director critic** — paste generations back, it flags
off-palette/off-style and rewrites the prompt.

## 2) Audio

- **ElevenLabs Sound Effects** — text→SFX, 4 samples in seconds, upscale/regenerate; explicitly positioned
  for **video game development** (Weapon/Bullet/Laser/UI/Ambience tags → combat SFX, UI sounds, ambience).
  [primary: elevenlabs.io/sound-effects, 3-0; **high**]. *Claude's role:* author the batch prompt list for the
  whole SFX set and iterate on misses.
- **ElevenLabs Music** (launched **2025-08-05**) — generates music the company says is **cleared for
  commercial use**, trained on licensed data → per-biome tracks. [secondary: TechCrunch + primary product page,
  3-0; **high**]
- ⚠️ **Licensing gate #1:** SFX/music are royalty-free for commercial use **only on a paid account**;
  free-tier output is **non-commercial only**. A monetized Play game is commercial → **paid plan required.**
  [primary: product page + binding Terms of Use, 3-0; **high**]
- ⚠️ **Licensing gate #2 (music):** Self-Serve plans permit commercial use *"except for film, TV, and Studio
  Games."* The **"Studio Games" carve-out may capture a mobile game** — **verify the specific plan before
  shipping ElevenLabs music.** [primary product page; **high**]

## 3) Store & marketing — Play asset specs (verified)

- **App icon:** exactly **512×512 px, 32-bit PNG with alpha, ≤1024 KB**. [primary: Google Play support, 3-0; **high**]
- **Feature graphic:** exactly **1024×500 px, JPEG or 24-bit PNG (no alpha)**. Fixed ratio + no-alpha
  constrains composition/export. [primary: Google Play support, 3-0; **high**]
- ⚠️ **Do NOT trust the surfaced screenshot spec** (claim of "≥3 @ 1920×1080 / 1080×1920, up to 8/device"
  was **refuted 0-3**) — pull current screenshot requirements straight from Play Console at release time.
  - *Claude's role:* draft listing copy + ASO keyword clusters + screenshot captions; author the
    feature-graphic prompt to the 1024×500 no-alpha constraint; generate an export/resize script
    (ImageMagick/`cwebp`) that conforms every AI output to spec.

## 4) In-game text / narrative

Claude's home turf, no external tool needed. Consistency mechanism mirrors the art one: Claude authors a
**tone bible** (mythic-Babylonian voice, register, reading level, forbidden words) once, generates every
string against it, self-reviews for drift, and emits Android string resources directly
(`strings.xml` + per-locale `values-xx/`), keeping keys/placeholders consistent across locales.

---

## Google Play AI-content compliance — likely a non-issue

- Play's AI-Generated Content policy requires an **in-app report/flag mechanism** for offensive AI content —
  **but only for apps that generate content at runtime from user prompts** (chatbots, text-to-image apps).
  [primary: Google policy, 3-0; **high**]
- The policy **scopes "AI-generated content" to runtime generation from user prompts**; the sibling Generative
  AI policy **explicitly excludes apps that can't create content using AI at runtime.** [primary: Google policy, 3-0; **high**]
- **Implication:** we bake AI-assisted assets at **build time** with no runtime generative feature →
  the policy **likely does not apply.** Just confirm nothing in the build adds a runtime generator.

## Asset-licensing / ownership (verify per tool)

- **Stability AI (if we use Stable Diffusion/SD3.5):** Community License **free under $1M annual revenue**,
  **you own outputs** — but **auto-terminates above $1M**, requires **free commercial registration**, and
  ownership holds only **"to the extent permitted by applicable law."** [primary: Stability license + agreement,
  3-0; **high**]. ⚠️ **US Copyright Office position: purely AI-generated output may not be copyrightable** — the
  blanket "ship anything commercially" claim was **refuted 1-2**; human editing strengthens the position.
- **Midjourney / ElevenLabs / OpenAI image:** each has its own terms; pattern is **commercial rights require a
  paid tier**. Have Claude build a one-page license matrix per tool before committing.

---

## Concrete build order (Claude's role each step)

1. **Style bible + tone bible** — Claude authors both from the GDD (palette, ziggurat/biome descriptors,
   voice). *Single most important consistency artifact.*
2. **In-battle visuals** — Claude refactors/extends Canvas code to a shared palette + shape vocabulary across
   all 6 enemies + 5 biomes. Highest consistency, free, no licensing.
3. **Particle/effect configs** — Claude writes per-biome emitter configs.
4. **Raster assets** (app icon, feature graphic, illustrated UI/UW icons) — Claude authors batch prompts
   anchored to one `--sref` code / Omni Reference / trained Flux LoRA; critiques returns; writes export-to-spec script.
5. **Audio** — Claude writes the ElevenLabs prompt batch (paid plan; verify the "Studio Games" music clause).
6. **Text & localization** — Claude generates strings + `values-xx/` from the tone bible.
7. **Compliance pass** — Claude assembles the per-tool license matrix; confirms no runtime generative feature
   triggers Play's AI policy.

## Caveats, weak evidence & open questions

- **Weakest evidence:** trained-LoRA character-locking leaned on a personal blog (corroborated, not primary);
  ElevenLabs "upscale" wording was vendor-only. Play-spec + licensing findings are all primary-sourced/strong.
- **Time-sensitive (re-verify at implementation):** MJ `--cref`→Omni Reference (V7) shift; ElevenLabs music
  "Studio Games" clause.
- **Open questions:** (1) current exact Play *screenshot* requirements (surfaced numbers refuted — check Play
  Console); (2) whether "Studio Games" captures a mobile idle game on our intended plan tier; (3)
  copyrightability of our specific AI-art workflow given the US Copyright Office stance (legal check if IP
  protection matters).

## Refuted claims (do NOT act on — failed adversarial verification)

- Play screenshot spec "≥3 @ 1920×1080 / 1080×1920, up to 8/device" — **0-3**.
- "Commercial use of Stability outputs permitted, so ship anything" — **1-2** (copyrightability caveat).
- Kubriko "no procedural Canvas drawing" characterization — **0-3**.
- ElevenLabs music clearance "rests on Merlin/Kobalt deals" framing — **0-3**.
- PiotrPrus/ParticleEmitter "1,000+ particles high-performance" perf claim — **1-2**.

---

_Source: `/deep-research` workflow run `wf_e95c3988-d17` (2026-07-02). Full verifier evidence per claim
retained in that run's transcripts. Suggested labels: quality/consistency is the throughline; treat as a
research/backlog epic to decompose into per-category tasks when picked up._

body:
## Summary

Mentors currently appear on `/explore` regardless of how complete or active their profile is, sorted oldest-first (`created_at ASC`). This rewards incumbency and surfaces half-built or dormant profiles to mentees. This spec introduces a **visibility & ranking system** that gates *exposure* (not entry) and orders mentors by signals we already collect.

**Principle:** Anyone can sign up as a mentor. But to *appear* in discovery, a profile must clear a completeness bar; among those that qualify, ordering reflects quality, activity, and fairness.

## Goals

- Hide half-built mentor profiles from `/explore` until they meet a completeness bar
- Replace oldest-first sorting with a composite ranking that reflects real quality + activity
- Nudge mentors to complete their profile via a transparent checklist
- Keep the system fair (anti-incumbency rotation) and kind to volunteers (no public star averages)

## Non-Goals

- No hard entry gate — anyone can still create a mentor profile
- No public star-rating badges — `avgRating` stays a private, invisible ranking input (existing product decision)
- No admin review queue or invite-only flow in this scope
- No paid/tiered/featured-for-money placement (platform is free forever)

## Context: what already exists (reuse, do not rebuild)

| Capability | Location |
|---|---|
| `sessionFeedback` table (1–5 rating + comment) | `src/lib/db/schema.ts` |
| `getMentorStats()` → `avgRating`, `completedSessions`, `uniqueMentees`, `goalsHelped` | `src/core/dashboard/queries.ts` |
| Feedback API + post-session nudge cron | `src/app/api/feedback/*` |
| Session state machine + auto-complete cron (no-show handling) | `src/app/api/sessions/*` |
| Goal attribution to mentors + public "Impact" section | `src/modules/goals/queries.ts`, mentor page |
| `getLastSessionByMentor()` (recency), `getCompletedSessionCount()` | `src/core/booking/queries.ts` |

**Key existing decision:** `avgRating` is shown only on the mentor's own dashboard, never publicly. This spec honors that — rating feeds ranking invisibly.

## Current gap

- No completeness/readiness scoring anywhere
- No `/explore` gate — incomplete mentors still appear
- `/explore` sorts `created_at ASC` only (incumbency + staleness)
- No profile-strength nudge on `/profile`
- Filters minimal: search + available checkbox (no expertise dropdown, no sort control)
- Sessions have no `respondedAt`/`confirmedAt` timestamp → response-time not measurable

---

## Phase 1 — Completeness Gate + Profile-Strength Nudge

Compute a completeness score (0–100) from profile fields. Hide mentors below threshold from `/explore`; show every mentor a checklist of what's missing.

| Signal | Points |
|---|---|
| Has headline | 15 |
| Has bio (≥50 chars) | 15 |
| Has ≥3 expertise tags | 15 |
| Has ≥1 link | 10 |
| Has avatar (`user.image`) | 10 |
| `experienceYears` ≥ 2 | 10 |
| `available` = true | 15 |
| Has ≥1 availability window | 10 |

**Threshold to appear: 40.** Computed at query time — no schema change.

**Work:**
1. Add `computeCompleteness(profile, user, hasAvailability)` in `src/core/profiles/queries.ts`
2. Update `getMentors()` to check availability and filter below threshold
3. Add a checklist card to `src/app/(platform)/profile/page.tsx` ("Complete these to appear in search"); return breakdown from `GET /api/profile`

**Acceptance:**
- Incomplete mentor is absent from `/explore`; completing past threshold makes them appear
- `/profile` checklist accurately reflects missing items
- Existing search/available/expertise filters still work alongside the gate

## Phase 2 — Composite Ranking + Rotation

Replace `ORDER BY created_at` with a composite score over already-qualified mentors. Reuses existing signals — no new tables.

| Input | Source | Intent |
|---|---|---|
| Completeness | Phase 1 | baseline |
| `avgRating` | `getMentorStats` | quality (invisible) |
| `completedSessions` | `getCompletedSessionCount` | credibility (log-scaled) |
| Recency of last session | `getLastSessionByMentor` | freshness |
| Goals helped | `getMentorStats.goalsHelped` | outcomes |

Plus **anti-incumbency rotation** (daily-seeded shuffle among similarly-ranked mentors) and **recency weighting** (active-this-week outranks dormant-but-decorated).

**Work:**
1. Add `rankMentors()` that blends inputs into one sort key (batch-fetch stats to avoid N+1)
2. Add a sort control to `explore/filters.tsx` (Recommended | Newest | Most active); default Recommended

**Acceptance:**
- Recommended sort orders by composite, not `created_at`; rotation visibly varies day-to-day
- `avgRating` never rendered on public surfaces (verify mentor page + explore card)
- No N+1 in the ranking path

## Phase 3 — Behavioral Signals (requires migration)

The one genuinely missing data point is **response time** (sessions only have `createdAt`).

**Work:**
1. Migration: add `respondedAt timestamp` to `sessions`; set on confirm/decline (PATCH + one-click action route)
2. Derive avg response time + decline/cancel rate per mentor
3. Feed into ranking (penalize slow responders); show "Usually responds within X" on cards
4. Soft-deactivate / nudge dormant mentors (>45 days) via existing email infra

## Phase 4 — Matching (mentee-side intent)

Move `/explore` from discovery to matching.

- Capture lightweight mentee intent (goal area, level, what they want); reuse `goals` where present
- `matchScore` = expertise overlap + availability/timezone fit + capacity headroom
- "Suggested for you" row on dashboard (top 3) to fight choice overload
- Mentor-stated capacity ("how many mentees this month") → pre-commitment nudge + ranking input
- Optional mentor "who I best help" field for two-way fit

---

## Open Questions

1. **Threshold** — 40, or 30 to avoid an empty `/explore` early? (Lean 40, auto-relax if <5 pass.)
2. **Strength UX** — numeric score vs. plain checklist? (Lean checklist; numbers invite gaming.)
3. **Keep rating private?** — confirm `avgRating` stays invisible, ranking-only. (Lean yes.)
4. **Rotation cadence** — daily seed vs. per-request random? (Lean daily seed.)
5. **Phase 3 timing** — worth a migration before booking volume exists? (Lean defer until ≥20 active mentors.)

## Suggested sequencing

Ship **Phase 1** (schema-free, high-value, standalone), then **Phase 2** (schema-free). Defer **Phase 3** (migration) and **Phase 4** (larger) until there's mentor/booking volume.

## Decisions

- Reuse existing rating/session/goal signals — do not rebuild feedback
- Score computed at query time for Phases 1–2 (no storage, no staleness)
- Rating remains a private, invisible ranking input — no public star badges
- Gate is visibility-only; entry stays open
- Only Phase 3 requires a migration (`respondedAt`)
title: Mentor visibility & ranking system (explore gate + composite ranking)

body:
## Context

Maintainer review of the live site (2026-07-06): layout and tone are right — simple, plain, keep that character. But the page should make the *why use this* case harder. Full gap analysis against the maintainer's USP list exists (session work, 2026-07-06); the measured facts below are verified.

## The four gaps to close

1. **Cost framing.** "Pay for usage, not a subscription" exists as a reason, but the numbers are buried and the subscription contrast is missing. Target framing (measured, honest): subscription dictation tools run ~$12–15/month (no competitor named on the page); the maintainer's all-day heavy use — ~25 h of audio/month, measured over the last 6 months from the local archive — costs about **$3/month** at Soniox's $0.12/h; lighter regular use lands around a dollar; the Groq path is free.
2. **Python-script transparency.** The word "Python" does not appear on the page. State it plainly: a single Python script, not an installed product — lean, fully readable, easy to modify (see 4); trade-off is a terminal window instead of a GUI (a VISION non-goal anyway). Natural spot: the get-started/audience block, or a sixth reason.
3. **Feature breadth.** There is no features section, so the "this actually does a lot" impression never forms. Add ONE compact section (after the lineup, before privacy): verbatim/polished modes, runtime API switching, recognition vocabulary, push-to-talk (currently mentioned nowhere), history archive of every recording + transcript, retry + crash-safety net, "extend it by telling your AI coding agent".
4. **Free path from "try" to "use".** Groq's free tier is generous and permanent (2,000 requests/day, up to 8 h audio/day — verified 2026-07-06). It can be framed as a real way to *run* the tool, keeping the honest asterisk that the German-quality anchor is the paid Soniox default.

## Hard constraints

- **Docs-first rule stands** (#75: every statement traces to README/VISION/CHANGELOG, no invented numbers). The cost figures above must land in README **first** (as measured maintainer experience with prices per provider pricing pages, dated), then on the page. Same for push-to-talk phrasing etc. — page follows docs.
- **Vocabulary, not "replacements".** The tool has a recognition vocabulary (context terms that improve recognition upstream). It has NO post-hoc find-and-replace — verified in code 2026-07-06. The page must name it truthfully.
- Soniox note worth reflecting in setup-facing text: free starting credits for new signups were discontinued (Oct 2025) — Soniox is pay-as-you-go from the first minute; the free path is Groq.
- Keep the page's simple character: densify existing sections, at most one new section (features).

## Optional block

A screenshot of the running tool. Open dependency: the maintainer may want the terminal appearance polished first — decide at implementation time or ship without and add later. (A demo video is a separate issue.)

Relates: #75 (shipped v1 of the page), #88 (README linking — should follow this), #89.

body:
## Goal
Make Brain Gym deployable to a free hosting provider so it can be used from a phone browser, and ensure it works correctly and looks good on mobile. The app must remain runnable locally exactly as before (`python app.py` / `run.bat`).

## Tasks
1. **Production-ready serving.** Add a production WSGI setup (e.g., `gunicorn`) and the config to run the Flask app in production. Bind to `0.0.0.0` and read the port from the `PORT` environment variable (fall back to 5000 locally). Keep `debug=True` only for local dev.
2. **Deployment config for a free host.** Add config to deploy on a free, GitHub-integrated platform — prefer **Render** (`render.yaml`) and also include a **`Dockerfile`** + **`Procfile`** so the repo is portable to Railway/Fly.io/etc. Pin dependencies in `requirements.txt`.
3. **Fix progress persistence for ephemeral hosting.** Free hosts reset the filesystem on redeploy/sleep, which would wipe `data/progress.json` and the user's streak. Move user progress (streak, completed days, saved answers) to **browser `localStorage`** so it survives on the client, OR use a free persistent store. The local single-user experience and existing API behavior should still work; migrate gracefully and document the choice.
4. **Verify mobile responsiveness.** Confirm the UI is fully usable on a phone-sized viewport (buttons, textarea, hints, history drawer, and any new charts). Fix any overflow/tap-target issues. The layout already has some `@media` rules in `static/style.css` — build on those.
5. **Document deployment.** Add a clear "Deploy it (use from your phone)" section to the README with step-by-step instructions: connect the repo to the host, what to click, expected URL, and any environment variables. Keep it beginner-friendly.

## Constraints
- Do not break local development or existing endpoints.
- No paid services; free tiers only.
- Keep dependencies lean and pinned.
- Coordinate with the changes in #1 if both are in flight (this issue focuses on deployment + mobile + persistence; #1 focuses on features + tests).

body:
## Summary

In Docker grading mode, `state_checks.jsonpaths` assertions using `path:` (JSONPath
into the env-state DB, e.g. `$.db.orders[0].id`) are **not evaluated by the
grader**. Only `path_glob:` (filesystem glob) assertions are. Authors who write
careful `path:` assertions get them silently ignored — verdicts are driven entirely
by other grading components (hash, transcript), with the JSONPath assertions
producing 0 contribution regardless of state.

After PR #66 these assertions now produce a clear `FAIL: ... graded host-side` in
the reasons text, so the symptom is *visible*. But the underlying gap remains: the
assertions still don't actually evaluate the state they describe.

## Root cause: two parallel grading evaluators that don't speak the same language

- **Host-side** (`tolokaforge/core/grading/state_checks.py`,
  `StateChecker.check_jsonpaths`): understands both shapes — `path:` (JSONPath into
  env-state) AND `path_glob:` (filesystem glob). Has `jsonpath_ng` + the
  `equals` / `equals_ci` / `contains` / `contains_ci` operator logic.
- **Runner-side** (`tolokaforge/runner/grading.py`,
  `evaluate_jsonpath_file_checks`): only understands `path_glob:` + `contains_ci:`
  on the container filesystem. Has no JSONPath engine.

In Docker mode the orchestrator delegates grading to the runner (it owns the
env-state DB at grade time). The runner receives the full `state_checks.jsonpaths`
list — including any `path:` assertions — and silently skips everything it can't
evaluate. PR #66 makes that skip loud, but the assertions still don't run.

## Repro (deterministic, no LLM)

Write a task with mixed-shape jsonpaths:

```yaml
state_checks:
  jsonpaths:
    - path: "$.db.orders[0].status"
      equals: "paid"
      description: "Order status is paid"
    - path_glob: "/env/fs/agent-visible/notes/*"
      contains_ci: "shipped"
      description: "Notes mention shipping"
```

Run under Docker grading. The `path:` assertion will report
`FAIL: assertion uses 'path' ... graded host-side` even when `$.db.orders[0].status`
is genuinely `"paid"` in the runner's env-state. The `path_glob:` assertion
evaluates correctly.

## Impact

- Task authors ship grading.yaml configs that read as strict but evaluate as
  no-ops for any `path:`-style assertion. Tested via PR #66's diagnostic surface;
  every `path:` assertion across the repos is currently a no-op under Docker mode.
- Verdicts can be misleading: a task may pass on hash + transcript while its
  `path:`-jsonpath section reports 0/N — looking failed but contributing nothing
  meaningful.
- The "use jsonpaths for partial credit and debugging when the hash doesn't
  match" pattern documented in some `grading.yaml` files (e.g. "human-readable
  individual field assertions for partial credit") is **broken** in Docker mode.

## Proposed designs (non-binding)

### Option A — bring the JSONPath engine to the runner
Add `jsonpath_ng` + the operator comparison logic into `runner/grading.py`. The
runner already owns the env-state at grade time; it just needs the evaluator code.

- Pros: smallest concrete change, no new gRPC contract, no cross-process state
  shuffling.
- Cons: duplicates evaluator logic across `core/grading/` and `runner/grading.py`.

### Option B — share one evaluator
Extract the JSONPath/operator evaluator into a small shared module imported by
both `core/grading/` and `runner/grading.py`. Single source of truth.

- Pros: no duplication; same operator behaviour everywhere by construction.
- Cons: bigger refactor; the host and runner test suites both need to exercise it.

### Option C — route `path:` assertions back to the host
Have the runner return the relevant env-state slice (or the full state) and the
orchestrator evaluate `path:` assertions host-side via the existing
`StateChecker.check_jsonpaths`. Runner keeps only `path_glob:`.

- Pros: leverages the existing host evaluator; clear separation of concerns.
- Cons: gRPC round-trip; state crosses the boundary; mismatch potential between
  what the runner sees and what the host evaluates.

Author's lean: **Option A** for simplicity, with a note that B is the cleaner
long-term shape if a third caller ever needs the evaluator.

## Acceptance

- A task that ships `path:`-style jsonpath assertions (`$.db.x`, with `equals` /
  `contains` / etc.) graded **under Docker mode** produces the **same verdict** it
  would under host-side grading on the same final env-state.
- A regression test pinning the contract: an integration-style test exercising the
  runner-side grading RPC with a mixed `path:` + `path_glob:` config, asserting
  both shapes evaluate.

## Honest caveat

Fixing this **changes verdicts** for any task currently shipping `path:`
assertions. Those assertions were no-ops; after the fix they actually run. So:
- The change must land **behind the golden grading coverage** (already on `main`),
  so the verdict diffs are visible and intentional.
- Authors should expect to update goldens for affected tasks, the same way the
  fix-loud silent-pass change (PR #66) updated two snapshots.

## Links

- Discovered while validating PR https://github.com/Toloka/tolokaforge/pull/66.
- Related closed issues: jsonpath silent-operator-pass (#58), nondeterministic
  reasons (#59) — same family of "silent skip in grading" bugs.
title: Grading: `path:`-style jsonpath assertions are not evaluated in Docker mode (runner has no JSONPath engine)

## Purpose

Living home for Wardnet's **go-to-market and monetization strategy**. This is a tracking/discussion issue, not a code task — it captures the durable commitments and the evolving execution plan. The engineering work it implies is tracked in #609 (premium tier + entitlement) and #610 (bridge decoupling).

## Durable commitments (decided — see `docs/adr-premium-tier-and-entitlement.md`)

- **Free tier is the growth engine and is permanently free.** Self-host + bring-your-own-domain = full features, zero cost to us. Premium never gates the self-hostable product.
- **Premium gates a real cost centre** (DDNS + Tunneler run on our infra), so it is paid **from public availability** — never given away free and later charged for (clawback is the cardinal sin).
- **Beta is free but explicitly labelled** "free during beta → premium at GA, with advance notice." Never silently free.
- **Stripe-native trial at GA.** Stripe is the payment processor only; the account master record is ours (tenant management).
- **Positioning: transparent-but-quiet.** Free/self-hostable product and the mission are the hero; premium is an honest, secondary "supports the project" tier. The solo-OSS identity is a trust asset, leaned into — not a slick SaaS launch.

## Open / evolving (use this issue to iterate)

- [ ] Launch copy + the explicit beta-pricing notice wording
- [ ] Pricing (amount, monthly/annual, trial length) — defer until closer to GA
- [ ] Channels / community launch plan (privacy + self-hosting communities)
- [ ] GA cutover plan: beta → premium transition, advance-notice mechanics
- [ ] Decide where the "manage subscription" surface lives (Stripe Customer Portal vs in-app)

## Why an issue, not a Discussion

Solo + pre-launch: Discussions earn their keep when there's a community conversing. This repo standardized on issues (impl-docs retired in favour of issues, d8ed6c83), so a long-lived `strategy`-labelled issue is the idiomatic home. Revisit if/when a public community forms.

## Problem

**1. Session heartbeats are write-only.** `src/telemetry.ts:376-378`'s `heartbeat(sessionId)` is emitted every 30s (`src/index.ts:1782-1790`), but `grep` for non-test consumers of the `'heartbeat'` event returns nothing — the data is paid for and never read. `/swarm status` reports lane counts only ("N/M lanes active") with no notion of *when* each lane last did anything, so a wedged run and a healthy run look identical. Note: heartbeats are keyed by `sessionID` from the chat hook, **not** by lane — per-lane attribution would require correlating lane session IDs from lean-turbo run state, which is a real, separate correlation problem, not included here.

**2. `getTelemetrySummary` (context-capsule aggregation: token estimates, cache hit/miss, stale-summary counts) has zero production callers.** `src/context-map/telemetry.ts:225` — confirmed by grep, the only references are the defining module, its own test, and `docs/context-map.md`, which explicitly tells users this data exists "for user inspection" with no command surface to inspect it from. This is a shipped feature (FR-007) missing only its last mile.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Phase 1 only** (per-lane attribution deferred to a future issue if demand appears): add a session-level "Last activity: Xs ago" line to `/swarm status`, plus a "possibly stalled (no activity > N min)" annotation, sourced from existing heartbeat data.
2. Surface `getTelemetrySummary` via a `/swarm context-map stats` subcommand (or a conditional "Capsules: N delegations, X% cache hit, ~Y tokens/capsule, Z% success" status line when `total_delegations > 0`). Update `docs/context-map.md:145` to point at the new command instead of the bare function.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/swarm status` shows session-level last-activity staleness.
- A new command/status line surfaces `getTelemetrySummary`'s existing aggregation.
- `docs/context-map.md` points users at the new surface.

## Effort / Dependencies
Effort: S for both. No dependency.

## Source
opencode-swarm enhancement audit, Track G, run `20260702T035413Z`. Candidates ENH-G011-5 (critic: REFINED — per-lane attribution cut, session-level kept), ENH-G011-6 (UPHELD_MEDIUM_VALUE — "best value/effort ratio in the batch"). Roadmap: `docs/proposals/v8-feature-roadmap.md`.
title: Surface heartbeat staleness in /swarm status + wire the dark getTelemetrySummary (context capsule stats) into a command

## Context

PR #1730 (issue #1729) paid down the bulk of the CI quarantine debt — fixing the production `save_plan` projection bug, resolving ~40 cross-platform test failures, and driving 3 of 4 quarantine lists to zero. However, **11 entries remain across 3 lists**, and the effort exposed systemic gaps that allowed the debt to accumulate undetected for months. This issue tracks both the remaining debt and the structural fixes needed to prevent recurrence.

## Current quarantine state (on main post-#1730)

| List | Active entries | Root cause category |
|---|---|---|
| quarantined-tests.txt | 5 | Knowledge-system test failures (pre-existing, unrelated to #1729) |
| quarantined-tests-macos.txt | 4 | Lean-turbo worktree provisioning — macOS-only lane mock issue |
| quarantined-tests-windows.txt | 0 | Clean |
| quarantined-integration-tests.txt | 2 | Ubuntu CI-only: read-only fs semantics + injection-budget shared-state |

---

## Part A — Diagnose and fix the 11 remaining quarantined tests

### A1. macOS lean-turbo worktree tests (4 files)

**Files:**
```
tests/unit/turbo/lean/integration-worktree.test.ts
tests/unit/turbo/lean/runner.test.ts
tests/unit/turbo/lean/runner.adversarial.test.ts
tests/unit/turbo/lean/retroactive-adversarial.test.ts
```

**Failure signature (from merge_group run 28806176287):**
```
expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)
Expected: > 0
Received: 0
```
The tests mock `provisionWorktree` via `_internals.bunSpawn` and assert it was called at least 1 time during `runPhase`. On macOS it's called **0 times** — `runPhase` takes a different code path. These tests pass on ubuntu and Windows.

**Suspected root causes to investigate:**
- `checkPathBudget` (src/worktree/core.ts:326) may behave differently on macOS, changing the provisioning path. It's Windows-only in intent but may short-circuit on non-Windows in an unexpected way.
- `git worktree add` porcelain output format or branch creation semantics may differ on the macOS runner's git version, causing the mock to not match.
- A race condition that only manifests on the macOS runner's slower I/O — the `provisionWorktree` call may be async and the mock may not be installed by the time it runs.
- The tests construct lane evidence files that feed `listLaneEvidence`; the sort added in #1730 made ordering deterministic, but the mock setup may still depend on filesystem timing.

**Blocker:** requires macOS environment access (or detailed merge_group log analysis across multiple runs). Cannot be diagnosed on Linux or Windows.

**Validation:** merge_group run with `unit (macos-latest, N)` all 4 shards passing these files.

### A2. Integration tests — ubuntu CI-only (2 files)

**Files:**
```
tests/integration/phase-complete-events.adversarial.test.ts
tests/integration/unified-injection-budget.test.ts
```

#### A2a. phase-complete-events.adversarial.test.ts:393 — read-only .swarm directory

**Failure signature:**
```
expect(parsed.success).toBe(true)
Expected: true
Received: false
```
The test makes `.swarm` read-only via `chmod 444` and expects `phase_complete` to still succeed (write failure should be non-blocking). On the ubuntu CI runner, `success` is `false`. Passes on Windows and macOS.

**Suspected root cause:** the ubuntu runner's uid/fs semantics — the runner user may be root (which bypasses read-only permissions), OR the `chmod 444` on `.swarm` doesn't prevent the specific write path the way the test expects. The test should use a more robust read-only simulation (e.g. `chmod 555` on the parent, or mock the write).

#### A2b. unified-injection-budget.test.ts:312 — SC-005 (Production bug #2)

**Failure signature:**
```
expect(kiInjected).toBeUndefined()
Received: { info: { role: "system" }, parts: [{ type: "text", text: "[[KNOWLEDGE-INJECTED]]..." }] }
```
When `system-enhancer` alone exceeds the unified injection ceiling, `knowledge-injector` should get **0** allocation and not inject. But it still injects on the ubuntu CI runner. This is the **real Production bug #2** from issue #1729 section 3.4.

**Critical note:** this test passes in isolation on Windows and in a clean `origin/main` worktree. It only fails in the ubuntu CI merge_group environment. The suspected cause is **test-ordering/shared-state contamination** — `getSystemEnhancerDemand(sessionID)` reads from a session-keyed map that may not be populated correctly when tests run in a specific order, or the session ID isn't unique between tests.

**Source locations to investigate:**
- src/hooks/knowledge-injector.ts:707-712 — `allocateInjectionBudget(seDemand, effectiveBudget, ...)` call
- src/hooks/system-enhancer.ts:684-691, 1645-1651, 2479-2485 — `resetUnifiedBudget` / demand recording
- Determine whether SE demand is actually recorded for the session before KI reads it in this test flow

**This may be a real production bug** (not just a test issue): if SE demand isn't recorded under certain session lifecycles, KI would inject beyond the unified budget in production too.

### A3. Base quarantine — knowledge-system tests (5 files, pre-existing)

**Files:**
```
tests/unit/commands/cleanup-drift.test.ts
tests/unit/commands/knowledge.adversarial.test.ts
tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-injector-drift-adversarial.test.ts
tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-floor-action.test.ts
tests/unit/tools/knowledge-recall.test.ts
```

These were quarantined before/during the #1729 effort (commits a5879ccb, f491360a) and are unrelated to the cross-platform work. They're knowledge-system failures likely related to the #1716/#1717 knowledge lifecycle changes. Triage separately — they may already be fixed by the knowledge PRs that landed (#1722, #1727, #1730's merge brought those in).

---

## Part B — Structural CI improvements to prevent recurrence

The #1729 effort took ~10 merge_group bounces over 2 days because the `pull_request` CI tier is ubuntu-only and cannot surface macOS/Windows/integration/coverage failures. These improvements would have caught every bounce before queuing:

### B1. Shared canonicalTmpDir() test helper + lint enforcement

~20 test files were individually fixed with `fs.realpathSync(os.tmpdir())` for the macOS /var to /private/var symlink. Without a shared helper, new tests will reintroduce the bug.

- Create `tests/helpers/tmpdir.ts` exporting `canonicalTmpDir()` and `canonicalMkdtemp(prefix)`.
- Add `scripts/check-test-tmpdir.sh` (modeled on `check-mock-cleanup.sh`) that flags raw `os.tmpdir()` / `mkdtemp` usage in test files without the realpath wrap.
- Wire into the `quality` CI job.

### B2. Bash portability lint for scripts/

`check-invariants.sh` used `declare -A` (bash 4+) which silently died on macOS bash 3.2 for months. A lint script would catch this class of failure:

- Create `scripts/check-bash-portability.sh` that flags bash-4+ constructs: `declare -A`, associative-array subscript syntax, `grep -P`, hex escapes like `\x27`, `coproc`, `mapfile`/`readarray`.
- Wire into the `quality` CI job.

### B3. Cross-OS PR-tier validation (the biggest gap)

The root cause of the entire backlog: `pull_request` CI runs ubuntu-only, so macOS/Windows-only failures are invisible until the merge queue bounces them.

**Option A — workflow_dispatch full-matrix trigger:** add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger to ci.yml that lets PR authors manually trigger the full 3-OS matrix + integration + coverage on their branch before queuing. Cost: GitHub Action minutes, but prevents queue bounces.

**Option B — "platform-sensitive" path filter:** run macOS + Windows unit shards on `pull_request` only when the diff touches platform-sensitive paths (src/worktree/**, src/sandbox/**, src/plan/**, scripts/**, .github/workflows/**). Use a `paths` filter or a `dorny/paths-filter` action.

**Option C — Previously-quarantined smoke job:** add a fast `pull_request` job that runs just the previously-quarantined files on all 3 OSes (a small subset, not the full 4-shard suite). This catches regressions in the files most likely to have cross-platform issues without the full cost.

### B4. Coverage-gate docs reconciliation

Coverage is already a required check (ruleset 17809658, added 2026-06-30), but the ci.yml comment at ~L245-249 still says "must happen AFTER this lands on main." Update the comment to reflect that coverage is enforced.

---

## Recommended order of attack

1. **A3** (base quarantine, 5 knowledge tests) — re-triage each; may already pass after the knowledge PRs merged. Lowest effort, highest chance of quick wins.
2. **B1 + B2** (shared helper + bash lint) — quick to implement, prevents the most common recurrence patterns. ~2-3 hrs each.
3. **A2b** (injection budget SC-005) — likely a real production bug. Reproduce by running the test file in the same bun process as the other integration tests (simulate the CI ordering). ~2-4 hrs.
4. **A2a** (read-only .swarm) — fix the read-only simulation to be uid-independent. ~1 hr.
5. **B3** (cross-OS PR-tier validation) — the systemic fix. ~3-5 hrs depending on option chosen.
6. **A1** (macOS lean worktree) — blocked on macOS access. ~2-4 hrs with a Mac.

## Definition of done

- [ ] All 4 quarantine lists at 0 active entries
- [ ] B1 (canonicalTmpdir helper + lint) implemented and wired into CI
- [ ] B2 (bash portability lint) implemented and wired into CI
- [ ] B3 (cross-OS PR-tier validation) implemented — at minimum Option A or C
- [ ] B4 (coverage docs reconciled)
- [ ] No test is green-by-not-running (verified by checking all 4 lists return empty for non-comment lines)

## Related

- Closes the residual debt from #1729 (PR #1730).
- Supersedes the quarantine tracking in #1705 (now closed).
- A2b traces to #1729 section 3.4 "Production bug #2" (unified injection budget).
title: Pay down remaining test quarantine debt + structural CI improvements to prevent recurrence

## Problem

The OCR engine lineup no longer reflects measured quality/cost on the owner's hardware and born-digital academic workload. Several engines are mis-ranked or dead weight:

## Measured winners (owner's 64GB Mac, real workload)

- `qwen3.5:cloud` (Ollama Cloud, no extra key): ~0.57, ~49s/page, only engine to clear all 3 hard page types → practical workhorse VLM.
- Gemini 3.x: best quality (0.60-0.64) but paid + occasional empty pages → edge escalation only.

body:
## Summary

Compiling a deeply-nested patch whose **clock is modulated by an oscillator**
(e.g. a through-zero flanger: an LFO sweeping a comb of `ModalVoice`s) is ~4×
slower to compile than a *larger* patch with static clocks. The emitted kernel
is correct and small — the cost is entirely a compile-time **build-then-dedup**
of a duplicated expression tree. The fix is to preserve sharing in the IR
(hash-consing) instead of recovering it late via CSE.

This surfaced during the fixed-point clock work (Phase 1), but it is **not a
flanger bug** — it will hit every clock-modulating effect on the roadmap
(chorus, PM/FM, per-oscillator-clock instruments), since they all place an
oscillator in a clock path.

## Reproduction

- `patches/flanger_probe.json` (`ThroughZeroFlangerProbe` → `ThroughZeroFlanger`
  → `ReversibleComb` → 3× `ModalVoice` → 4× `ClockPhasor` each), LFO-modulated
  delay.
- `time diffcli compile patches/flanger_probe.json` → **~7.0–7.25s**.
- Contrast `patches/reverse_reverb.json` (5× `ModalVoice`, **static** offset
  clocks) → **~1.9s**, despite *more* oscillators.

The only structural difference is that the flanger's tap clock is `clk ± d`
where `d` carries an oscillator (`Sin`∘`ClockPhasor`); the reverb's offset is a
constant.

## Root cause: tree-representing-a-graph

`ClockPhasor` reads its clock `clk` twice (the fixed-point split-multiply:
`thi = clk >> 32`, `tlo = clk & mask`). `ModalVoice` feeds the same `clk` to 4
partial `ClockPhasor`s → 8 uses of `clk` per voice. `ReversibleComb` passes a
**modulated** clock into 3 `ModalVoice`s. The whole patch is fully inlined
(`sessionInlineNested = true`), and inlining is *substitution*: each `clk`
use-site gets a **copy** of the modulated-clock expression, so the LFO subtree
(`Sin` polynomial + a phasor) is duplicated ~16×. The pre-CSE strata/partition
passes then walk that bloated tree; emit-time structural CSE collapses it back
to a small plan. So the denotation never duplicated anything (`clk` is one
value used many times) — the *tree* representation lost the sharing the meaning
always had.

## What was ruled out (with evidence)

- **Output / codegen volume** — the fused flanger plan (112KB) is *smaller*
  than the static reverb's (171KB). Not a codegen-size problem.
- **`structuralId` emit-CSE memo** — the TS emitter had a per-node `hashCache`
  (WeakMap node→id) that the Lean port intentionally dropped
  (`lean/Tropical/Ir/Emit.lean:29`). Restoring it (value-keyed `Std.HashMap
  CoreExpr Nat`) moved compile time 6.97s → 6.83s — negligible. The cost is
  **upstream of emit**: a strata/partition pass is superlinear on the
  duplicated tree (which pass exactly was not isolated; the fix is the same
  regardless).

## Benchmark: the inline-vs-fractal tradeoff

Compiling the same patch fused vs. fractal (`sessionInlineNested = false`),
runtime measured over 4.096M samples warm:

| realization | compile | runtime | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| fused (inlined) | 7.25s | **163 ns/sample** | — |
| fractal (per-instance) | **1.83s** | 193 ns/sample (**+18%**) | bit-identical (goldens pass) |

So **not-inlining is 4× faster to compile but ~18% slower at runtime** — a real
lost-fusion tax (registers → slots, no cross-instance optimization), paid on
exactly the expressive patches we want to ship. Correctness is unaffected
(fractal renders bit-identically; goldens green under both).

## Proposed solution: hash-cons the IR (preserve sharing)

Recover-late (current emit CSE) and not-inlining both have costs the benchmark
makes concrete. The principled fix is to **never lose the sharing**: intern
expression nodes so identical subtrees are one node with many parents (sharing
by *identity*), and make the strata/partition passes id-aware. Then the bloated
tree is never constructed → fast compile **and** full-inline fusion (the 163ns
runtime).

Why hash-consing specifically, over the alternatives:

- **Don't-inline modulated sources (operational patch)** — costs the measured
  18% runtime. Rejected as a permanent fix.
- **Let-insertion during inlining (Brady)** — bind multiply-used substitutions
  instead of copying. Correct in principle, but the post-strata `CoreExpr` is
  deliberately **let-free** (`arrayLower` unrolls all `bindingRef`s), so an
  inserted `let` is re-duplicated downstream. Doesn't survive the pipeline.
- **CSE during strata** — needs a sharing representation to express the dedup;
  same obstacle as let-insertion in a let-free IR.
- **Hash-consing** — sharing by node identity is *orthogonal to syntax*, so it
  is compatible with the flat, let-free IR as-is. It also speeds up **all**
  compilation, not just clock-modulated patches.

### Sketch / scope

- An interned expression store (analogous to the existing program `Arena` /
  `ProgramIdx`): nodes keyed by `(op, child-ids)`; construction returns an id;
  identical subtrees collapse to one entry.
- The substitution in `InlineInstances` produces shared ids instead of deep
  copies.
- `ArrayLower` / `IdentityElim` / `partitionKernel` / `Emit` operate over ids
  (DAG), not tree values.
- Equivalence gate is already in place: `tropicaltest` goldens +
  `tests/web/wasm_vs_jit` must stay bit-identical (output is unchanged — this is
  purely a representation/perf change).

This is a self-contained IR refactor that deserves its own runway. It is the
right principled fix and is justified by the +18% runtime cost of the
operational alternative.

## Workaround until then

Keep `sessionInlineNested = true` (fused) — runtime-optimal. The ~7s compile is
isolated to deeply-nested *modulated-clock* patches; static-clock patches and
single-oscillator reparameterizations (reverse `clk: -θ`, varispeed `clk: k·θ`)
compile fast.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Compile-time blowup for modulated-clock patches: inlining duplicates shared subtrees (hash-cons the IR)

### Problem
 
`app/services/ingestion/adapters/news.py` ships with `StubNewsProvider`, which produces nothing. The pipeline routes news through `IngestionPipeline._ingest_news_items` (line 399 of `pipeline.py`), which now has working dedup (2026-05-09 fix) but no real input.
 
Until a real news source is wired, the news path contributes zero events to scoring. The audit doc has flagged this as zero-impact-today.
 
### What to do — decision phase
 
Pick a provider. Options to evaluate:
 
- **GDELT 2.0** — free, broad coverage, noisy, requires aggressive filtering. Material attribution would lean heavily on the keyword + Haiku hybrid pattern landed for SEC EDGAR.
- **NewsAPI / Newsdata.io** — paid, cleaner, more focused. Per-call cost.
- **A purpose-built RSS aggregator** — curate ~20 industry feeds (Reuters Metals, Mining.com, S&P Platts, etc.). Highest signal, hardest to maintain.
- **Continue with stub** — accept zero news coverage at launch. Scoring works fine without it (all five pillars have other inputs).
The Tier 3 audit recommended Haiku attribution for any free-text source. For GDELT specifically, the keyword pre-filter from `MaterialCache` becomes essential — GDELT volume is too high for Haiku-on-everything.
 
### What to do — implementation phase (after provider selected)
 
1. Replace `StubNewsProvider` with the chosen adapter. Honor the existing `NewsAdapter` interface in `app/services/ingestion/adapters/news.py`.
2. Run `MaterialCache.detect` over `article.title + article.summary` per the Tier 1.3 cap (top-3 materials, drops >5).
3. When `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, run results through `MaterialClassifier.classify` per the Tier 3 pattern (see `app/services/ingestion/ingest_sec_edgar.py` around lines 382–460 for the reference implementation).
4. Persist via `pipeline._add_risk_event` — dedup is now handled there.
### Acceptance
 
- Decision documented in `docs/scoring-audit-2026-05-addendum.md`.
- If implemented: end-to-end synthetic test (mock provider response → events written → material junctions written → idempotent re-run).
- Cost ceiling documented (if paid provider).

## tl;dr

The teleprompter is a marketing wedge for [Astrlabe](https://github.com/kori-app/astrlabe), not a standalone revenue product. AI features should make it the **best free pitch teleprompter on the web** — and surface Astrlabe at the moments when AI obviously means "AI workflow", which is what Astrlabe does.

Don't build separate billing. Don't gate the core teleprompter. Gate AI features at a usage cap, route paid users through Astrlabe's existing auth (windsock) so the funnel is one product.

## Why this product, why now

Existing teleprompter tools are either:
- **Free + ugly** (random GitHub projects, web teleprompters with 2014-era UI)
- **Paid + ugly** ($10-20/mo SaaS apps that look like Office 2007)
- **Pro + expensive** (hardware teleprompters, $500+ apps)

Nobody is shipping a **modern, AI-native, beautiful, free** teleprompter. The wedge is real because:
1. Founders practicing pitches Google "online teleprompter" daily
2. The product naturally calls for AI features (write, time, coach, practice)
3. Once a founder uses it, they're 1 click away from "wait, you also have a workflow canvas?"

## The freemium tiers

### Free (forever, no signup)
- Everything in v0.x.0 today
- Visual polish (#1)
- Per-section pacing (#7)
- 5 AI generations / month (script writing, tone shift, translation) — unsigned, IP-rate-limited
- Open source — anyone can self-host

### Pro — $9/mo (signup via Astrlabe windsock)
- Unlimited AI generations
- Voice coaching (mic-driven feedback after each practice)
- Recording integration (screen + camera, exported MP4)
- Two-screen presenter mode
- Cloud sync across devices (script library)
- Custom fonts + brand kit
- Priority support

### Astrlabe Pro (existing tier) — bundles Teleprompter Pro
- Anyone paying for Astrlabe gets Teleprompter Pro free
- Reverse direction: Teleprompter Pro users see "Want this same canvas + agents to power your real workflows? → Astrlabe Free trial"

## The AI features (in priority order)

### Tier A — write & rewrite (low cost, broad appeal)
- [ ] **Generate script from prompt** — "60s pitch about X for Y audience" → structured script with `// timing` markers
- [ ] **Tone shift** — selection-based: "make this more punchy / casual / formal / shorter / longer"
- [ ] **Auto-section** — paste long monologue, AI inserts `// X-Ys · Label` markers based on rhythm

### Tier B — practice & coach (mic + signal processing)
- [ ] **Voice-driven scroll** — Web Speech API listens; teleprompter scrolls at your actual pace (no manual speed)
- [ ] **Practice analytics** — record session; AI analyses pace variance, filler words ("um", "like"), section drift
- [ ] **Pronunciation hints** — flag rare words, show inline phonetic on hover

### Tier C — pro / paid only
- [ ] **TTS preview** — generate audio of how the script sounds at target pace (helps refine word choice)
- [ ] **Cloud script library** — save/sync scripts across devices
- [ ] **Recording integration** — screen + camera recording, transcribed, with feedback overlay

## How it ties to Astrlabe

The killer feature is **also a demo of Astrlabe**:

> "Your pitch script is a workflow. Generate → Refine (LLM agent) → Practice (mic) → Analyze (sentiment + pace) → Coach (LLM feedback). The teleprompter you're using right now runs on the same engine that powers Astrlabe workflows."

Subtle plug, not pop-up. A `Powered by Astrlabe` link in the footer + an explicit "Built with Astrlabe — try the canvas →" in the AI generation modal.

## What NOT to do (yet)

- ❌ Separate billing system (Stripe checkout in teleprompter repo)
- ❌ Gate basic teleprompter features
- ❌ Server-side dependency for the free tier (must keep working offline)
- ❌ Force signup before first generation (3 free uses, then signup gate)
- ❌ Complex auth flows — reuse windsock OIDC for Pro

## Open questions

1. **AI inference**: call OpenAI directly from the browser with a per-IP rate-limited proxy on Astrlabe? Or require signup for ANY AI feature? Lean: per-IP free tier (5/month) → low friction, easy churn.
2. **Pricing**: $9/mo standalone vs $0 if you have Astrlabe? Need a price floor that doesn't make Astrlabe customers feel cheated. Lean: bundle in Astrlabe Pro, standalone $9/mo as the "I just want the teleprompter" persona.
3. **Self-host story**: package + AI proxy could be self-hosted by enterprise users. Charge for the hosted version, keep the package open source. Same model as Plausible / Cal.com.

## Next concrete step

Pick ONE AI feature to ship first as proof. **Recommendation: "Generate from prompt"** — easiest, most demo-able, generates the highest-leverage feedback ("wait, this just wrote me a pitch in 5 seconds").

That ships as v0.4.0 with:
- Modal `Generate script` button next to `Edit`
- Backend: Astrlabe-hosted proxy (`/api/teleprompter/generate`) — Anthropic or OpenAI call, structured output via JSON mode
- Free: 5/month/IP. Paid: unlimited via windsock token.

Comments, alternative proposals, "this is the wrong wedge" all welcome below.
title: RFC: AI Co-pilot + freemium positioning
