## Problem

`docs/spec.md` is a single 1269-line file covering 25 top-level sections, from the trust model through the Lua API to the build order. That makes it hard to navigate, hard to maintain (a visibility change is a diff against a 1269-line monolith), and hard to link into — issues cite line numbers that drift on every edit. It's also the one artifact every other change leans on, so the friction is paid constantly.

The proposal: split it into functional-area documents under `docs/`, with a single `overview.md` as the hub that frames the system and links out to each area. Future work and known limitations move out of the spec and into issues as part of the same pass.

## Proposed structure

A starting split for discussion — grouped by the system's functional areas, mapping the current sections:

- **`overview.md`** — Goals, Architectural principles, a high-level Trust model summary, and the TOC linking the area docs.
- **`trust-and-authority.md`** — Trust model (full detail), Clients and the server boundary.
- **`data-model.md`** — Data model, Naming conventions, Identity and participants.
- **`visibility.md`** — Visibility.
- **`conversations-and-briefs.md`** — Conversations and contexts, System prompt, Contextual briefs.
- **`events-and-storage.md`** — Event sourcing, Storage and materialization, Time.
- **`write-path.md`** — Write path and regeneration, Concurrency.
- **`agent-loop.md`** — Agent loop and tool protocol, Server API and turn lifecycle, Lua API.
- **`lifecycle.md`** — Initialization and lifecycle.
- **`observability-and-testing.md`** — Observability, Testability and abstraction boundaries, Validation and the eval harness.
- **`roadmap.md`** — Build order.

Each area doc is ~100-200 lines and self-contained enough to review in isolation.

## What leaves the spec

Two kinds of content move out of the spec as part of this split:

- **The visibility-regression appendix is removed.** Its scenarios are implemented as eval fixtures in `crates/eval/src/scenarios/` (`privacy.rs`, `compaction.rs`, `identity.rs`, and the rest), so the spec is duplicating the fixture inventory. The spec's job is to describe the architecture and *how* the system is evaluated, not enumerate the current tests. Before dropping, verify each appendix scenario has a code counterpart; any that don't get moved to code, not kept in the spec.
- **Known limitations and Future directions move to the issue tracker.** We're generally moving future work to issues so it's trackable and assignable rather than buried in a spec section that drifts. The split is the moment to triage each item into an issue (some already are — #15, #16) and replace the enumerated lists with a pointer to the labeled issues. `roadmap.md` keeps just the Build order.

## Migration concerns

- **Permalinks break.** Issues #15 and #16 reference `docs/spec.md` line anchors (`#L1050`, etc.); other issues and commits do too. Re-point every reference in the same PR that does the split, so there's no window where the links dangle.
- **Cross-references become inter-doc links.** The spec leans heavily on "see **Visibility**" / "(see §Storage)" — currently intra-document. After splitting these are relative markdown links to section anchors, which need a consistent scheme (and a convention for when a section is renamed). This is the bulk of the mechanical churn.
- **Fully split, no generated artifact.** A single-document read is just concatenating the area docs in overview order (the overview defines the order), so nothing needs to be maintained as a generated file. The one cost is that one-shot `grep docs/spec.md` becomes `grep -r docs/` — minor, and offset by per-file clarity.

## Verify docs ↔ code as part of the split

The split is a natural audit point: each area doc gets re-read against its implementation. As part of this work, verify that the docs correctly model the application and vice versa — every spec'd mechanism exists in code, and every load-bearing code behavior is described. Drift surfaced here gets filed as issues (the #15 and #16 findings are examples of the kind of thing this surfaces), not silently fixed in the prose.

## Proposed approach

One atomic move in a single PR: split the content into the structure above, rewrite every internal cross-reference as an inter-doc link, drop the appendix, triage Known limitations / Future directions into issues, and re-point the `docs/spec.md#L…` anchors in open issues and recent commits. A partial split leaves the repo half-migrated and the cross-refs inconsistent, so it's worth doing in one pass.
title: Split the spec into functional-area documents connected by an overview

body:
## Problem (the "So What?")
Maxwell's Daemon's headline promise is letting operators "swap MCP toolsets at invocation time" and "measure each change." But today a single MCP tool-call failure is **fatal to the whole run**. In `src/agent/default.rs`, the non-bash tool path propagates the provider error with `?` (`run_non_bash_tool(...).await?` at ~line 1456, which bubbles the `provider.call(...).await?` at ~line 2344). So a spawn failure, stdio timeout, malformed/missing JSON-RPC response, a protocol-version mismatch, or a server-reported tool error aborts the entire trajectory — even at step 40 of a long, paid SWE-bench run. This is an asymmetry: a failing **bash** command becomes a recoverable observation (non-zero exit code → the agent routes around it), and a failing **model** call has `fallback_models`, but a failing **MCP** call has neither. The exact capability operators are told to lean on (swappable toolsets) is the most fragile path in the loop.

## User Story
As an agent operator running long-horizon, paid trajectories with a swapped-in MCP toolset, I want a single flaky MCP tool call to be handed back to the model as a recoverable error observation, so that one server hiccup doesn't nuke an expensive run and corrupt my measurement of the toolset.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A failed MCP tool call — process spawn failure, stdio/timeout, malformed or missing JSON-RPC response, protocol-version mismatch, or a server-reported tool error — does **not** abort the run. It is surfaced to the model as a tool observation carrying a non-zero/error indication, and the agent loop continues to the next step.
- [ ] The failure observation names the failing tool and the MCP server (redacted via the existing redaction surfaces) and gives a concise reason, so the model can retry or route to another tool.
- [ ] Each MCP failure is tagged in the trajectory with a distinct per-step marker and reason — symmetric with how chaos-injected bash timeouts are tagged (`chaos_injected: true`) — so `bench inspect`/analysis can count MCP faults separately from model behavior.
- [ ] A run-level guard prevents pathological loops: after a configurable number of consecutive failures from the same MCP tool/server (sane small default; `0`/off preserves a default rather than infinite tolerance), the run aborts **deliberately** with a clear, distinct exit code and failure category — never an opaque crash.
- [ ] The run outcome / `failure_category` distinguishes a "recoverable MCP fault" from a "deliberate MCP give-up abort," so nightly-smoke and bench measurement do not misattribute a flaky toolset to model failure (relates to the harness-attributable-failure gating in #820).
- [ ] Behavior holds for the current stateless per-call spawn (fidelity mode) and is defined to also hold for the persistent-session mode proposed in #840.
- [ ] A deterministic MCP-fault injector (in the spirit of `--chaos-fail-every`) exists to exercise each failure class in tests.
- [ ] Documented in a new `docs/spec-*.md` and linked from MCP-related docs.

## Success Metric
With the deterministic MCP-fault injector exercising each failure class once per run: **0%** of single-fault trajectories abort with a fatal/opaque error (today: 100% abort on the first fault), and **≥99%** continue with the fault recorded as a recoverable observation. Operational corollary: MCP-attributable fatal aborts in nightly SWE-bench smoke trend to 0.

## Out of Scope
- Automatic restart / health-checking of long-lived MCP processes (persistent-session lifecycle is #840's concern).
- Transparent automatic retry-with-backoff of the same MCP call (this slice is graceful degradation into a recoverable observation; retry is a possible follow-up).
- Changes to MCP transport or protocol negotiation, and any new toolset config surface beyond the give-up threshold.
- Non-stdio (HTTP/SSE) MCP servers — the current implementation is stdio-only.

## Gap Analysis
Claude Code, Codex, and OpenHands return MCP tool errors to the model as a tool result with an error flag (e.g., `isError: true`), letting the agent recover in-loop, and they reconnect crashed servers. mini-swe-agent is bash-only, so its tool failures are *always* recoverable observations via the exit-code model. Our harness already does the right thing for bash (exit code → observation) and for provider faults (`fallback_models`) — MCP is the lone tool path that is fatal. Closing this asymmetry is what makes "swap MCP toolsets at invocation time" actually safe for paid, long-horizon runs, which is the project's stated reason to exist. Existing MCP work is adjacent but doesn't cover this: `bench tool-coverage` (#263) measures usage, `scriptability-check` probes servers *before* the run, and #840/#842/#845/#850/#852 address sessions/inventory/comparison/preview/preflight — none address the *in-loop runtime error path*.

## Complexity Tier
M — touches the agent step error path and trajectory recording, adds a fault injector and a give-up threshold to config, plus a spec doc and tests; no new subsystem.
title: Recover from MCP tool-call failures instead of aborting the run

body:
## Goal

When a sales order contains materials that come from suppliers, the platform should be able to **generate the corresponding purchase orders to those suppliers** (at our cost), so we can track what we owe, receive stock, and pay them — all linked end-to-end. This issue is the **design + plan**; it is not yet a build ticket. Lock the open decisions (bottom) before we start, so we don't paint ourselves into a corner.

Parent tracking: #72.

---

## Why now / what prompted this

From the order-window iteration we now have the building blocks for per-line supplier tracking, but **no automation** that turns a sales order's supplier-assigned lines into actual purchase orders. Today: per-line supplier + a "what we owe" rollup + supplier-attributed money-out exist; auto-creating the supplier PO / supplier bill does **not**.

---

## Already in place (building blocks — do NOT rebuild)

- `order_items.supplier_company_id` (per-line supplier; shows on every line, catalog or ad-hoc) + `products.supplier_company_id` (product default, auto-set on purchase receive).
- Purchase orders: `orders.order_type='purchase'` + `supplier_company_id`.
- `generate_supplier_bill_from_order(p_order)` (purchase order → supplier bill = real AP).
- `deliver_order_line` / `receive_order_into_warehouse` (stock-in + status).
- Finance → **Payables** (supplier bills + uninvoiced purchase orders, aged) and Finance → **Planning** (schedule outgoing payments, "Outgoing" filter, `planned_payments`).
- Per-order **"Suppliers on this order — what we owe"** rollup (line cost grouped by supplier − money paid out, with a Pay button) — `ordersService.getOrderSupplierExposure`.
- Pricing resolver `get_product_price_for_workspace` (shared by quotes/invoices/orders): sell price from `product_prices.list_price` − customer discount; cost from `_pricing_cost` → `products.cost`.

---

## Core design

### New RPC — `generate_purchase_orders_from_sales_order(p_sales_order)`
1. Take the sales order's lines that have a `supplier_company_id` **and** a cost, that we need to procure (scope = decision #1/#2 below).
2. **Group by supplier.** For each group create a **draft purchase order** to that supplier, copying lines (qty, `unit_price = unit_cost`, unit, **purchase VAT** — see gap A3), carry `project_id`.
3. **Link back:** new `orders.source_sales_order_id` (+ `order_items.source_order_item_id`) so the sales order shows "Linked purchase orders" and each PO knows its origin.
4. **No double-procurement:** track `order_items.procured_qty` on the source line; re-runs only cover the remainder / back-order.
5. Operator reviews drafts → **receive** (stock-in) → `generate_supplier_bill_from_order` → lands in **Payables** (real liability) → pay it (draws down AP). Loop closed.

### Schema additions
- `orders.source_sales_order_id uuid` (purchase → originating sales order).
- `order_items.source_order_item_id uuid` + `order_items.procured_qty numeric default 0`.
- (Possibly) `purchase order ↔ sales order` is 1:N via the column above; no link table needed.

### UI
- Sales-order **Actions → "Create supplier purchase orders"** → grouped **preview** (per supplier: lines, qty, cost, total, MOQ/lead-time warnings) → confirm → creates draft POs.
- **"Linked purchase orders"** section on the sales order (status of each PO, received/billed/paid).

---

## Gaps & considerations that MUST be folded in (these were missing from the first pass)

### A. Accounting correctness
- **A1 — Commitment vs. liability.** A PO is a *commitment*, not money owed. The real **liability (AP)** only exists at **goods-received / supplier-bill**. Keep the two distinct: commitment (PO) → liability (supplier bill) → paid. The current per-order "what we owe" rollup is a **commitment** view; label it as such, separate from booked Payables.
- **A2 — 3-way match.** PO ↔ goods received ↔ the supplier's *actual* invoice (which rarely equals our cost). Need a match/variance step (decision #5).
- **A3 — Purchase VAT + currency.** PO carries the supplier's **input VAT** (≠ the sale's VAT) and possibly a **different currency**. Must set VAT per PO line and handle FX, not just copy the sale line.

### B. Procurement realities
- **B1 — MOQ + lead time.** `product_prices.moq` and `lead_time_days` exist — "procure the shortfall" must round up to MOQ and surface lead time.
- **B2 — Multi-supplier sourcing.** Product has **one** `supplier_company_id` today; real buying compares suppliers per item. Single-source for v1, multi-source later (needs a supplier price-list model).
- **B3 — Non-stock / service lines.** e.g. transport, labour — have a *supplier* (carrier/contractor) but aren't warehouse stock. "Procure shortfall via warehouse" won't handle them; service POs are a separate shape.
- **B4 — Drop-ship vs stock-to-warehouse.** Supplier-ships-direct-to-customer (no stock movement) vs into our warehouse first — two flows (decision #1).

### C. Lifecycle & control
- **C1 — Edit/cancel reconciliation.** Change the sales-order qty or cancel it after POs exist → what happens to the linked draft POs? Partially handled by `procured_qty`; needs explicit rules.
- **C2 — Approval gate.** Creating POs commits money; optional PO-approval step (mirror the #227 pricing-approval pattern) (decision #4).
- **C3 — RBAC.** Who can create POs / pay suppliers.

### D. Prerequisites (hard dependencies)
- **D1 — Supplier must be a real CRM company** (`is_supplier`), not just a `factory_name` string on the product. Catalog-sourced products may need a products→CRM-supplier link first (the existing factory-name pin helps).
- **D2 — Cost source (blocks meaningful POs).** A PO price *is* the cost. If `products.cost` is empty but cost lives in `product_prices.cost_basis`, POs come out €0. **Add a `coalesce(products.cost, product_prices.cost_basis)` fallback in `_pricing_cost`** as a prerequisite. (Separate quick win, tracked here as a dependency.)

---

## Open decisions (need answers before finalizing)

- [ ] **#1 Drop-ship?** Do suppliers ever ship straight to the customer, or always into our warehouse first?
- [ ] **#2 MOQ / lead time** — must we respect supplier minimum order quantities?
- [ ] **#3 Multi-supplier** — source the same product from several suppliers (price comparison), or one-per-product for v1?
- [ ] **#4 Approval** — should creating supplier POs require approval, or just-do-it?
- [ ] **#5 Match strictness** — 3-way matching (PO↔receipt↔supplier invoice with variance), or "create PO → receive → bill" enough for v1?

---

## Proposed phasing

- **v1 (lean, safe):** single-supplier, warehouse-only, **manual** "Create supplier POs" with grouped preview + linkage + `procured_qty`, no auto-approval. Commitment vs. liability made explicit. Depends on **D2** (cost fallback).
- **v2:** shortfall-only procurement using `warehouse_items.reorder_point`/`qty_on_hand`; MOQ + lead-time (B1); service/non-stock POs (B3); edit/cancel reconciliation (C1); optional approval (C2).
- **v3:** drop-ship (B4); multi-supplier sourcing + supplier price lists (B2); 3-way matching + variance (A2); purchase-VAT/FX hardening (A3).

---

## Attach to more workflows (beyond per-sales-order)

- **Low-stock replenishment run** — create POs for any product under `warehouse_items.reorder_point`, grouped by supplier (procurement isn't only sales-order driven; this is the bigger recurring win).
- **Quote → accepted → order → suggest procurement.**
- **Flows engine** — emit a `procurement_needed` event → notify purchasing / optional auto-create (follow the existing TriggerType + system-default-flow pattern).
- **Project BOM → POs** for project-based buying (carry `project_id`).

---

## Related, deliberately out of scope here

- **Supplier portal** (a supplier logs in to see payments to them + what we owe; v2 cross-tenant "owed to me across the network" gated by per-workspace opt-in + VAT-verified identity). Tracked separately if we proceed.
- **Supplier opening balances** — decided **not** to build (use a supplier bill if ever needed).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Supplier procurement automation — generate purchase orders from sales orders (design + plan)

On physical iOS devices, 'fdb native-tap --at x,y' currently fails with 'Target doesn't conform to FBSimulatorLifecycleCommands protocol' because idb's 'ui tap' is simulator-only (idb issue #853 has been open since Oct 2023, no fix planned).

RESEARCH FINDINGS (mid-2026):

There is NO out-of-process, zero-setup tap injection path for physical iOS devices. Apple has never exposed HID injection through lockdownd. xcrun devicectl has no tap command. idb physical-device support is broken since iOS 17.

The de-facto standard used by Appium, pymobiledevice3, go-ios, tidevice, etc. is WebDriverAgent (WDA): a signed XCUITest runner IPA installed once on the device, exposing an HTTP server at port 8100 that accepts W3C WebDriver Actions for taps.

PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION:

Use pymobiledevice3 (already installed by users who've patched it for Python 3.14 — same dependency we already lean on for sim native-tap was idb, which itself depends on pymobiledevice-style protocols). Specifically:

1. User one-time setup:
   - Build/sign WDA (Appium publishes pre-built IPAs at github.com/appium/WebDriverAgent/releases)
   - Install on device once (paid Apple Developer account: cert valid 1 year; free account: 7 days)

2. fdb native-tap on physical iOS:
   - Use 'pymobiledevice3 developer wda --xctrunner' to start WDA, run a tap via W3C Actions HTTP POST, stop WDA
   - OR talk to WDA HTTP directly from Dart (port-forward over usbmux), assuming WDA is already running

INVESTIGATION REQUIRED before implementing:

1. Confirm which user setup is least painful. The 7-day free-account cert expiry is bad UX for a debug tool. The paid account requirement may push fdb native-tap on physical iOS into 'power user' territory.
2. Confirm pymobiledevice3 CLI exposes a raw-coordinate tap (not just 'tap by accessibility ID'). The research showed swipe accepts coords; raw-coord tap may require talking to WDA's HTTP /actions endpoint directly.
3. Decide whether fdb should manage WDA lifecycle (auto-launch, auto-stop) or assume user starts WDA themselves.
4. Test on iOS 26.x — go-ios issue #613 reported WDA launch regression on iOS 18.5; iOS 26 compatibility unconfirmed in research.

SOURCES:
- idb #853 (sim-only ui tap): https://github.com/facebook/idb/issues/853
- pymobiledevice3 WDA CLI: https://github.com/doronz88/pymobiledevice3/blob/master/pymobiledevice3/cli/developer/wda.py
- Appium WDA pre-built IPAs: https://github.com/appium/WebDriverAgent/releases
- Appium pre-installed WDA guide: https://appium.github.io/appium-xcuitest-driver/7.1/guides/run-preinstalled-wda/

NOTE: the in-process 'fdb tap --at' (via fdb_helper Pigeon) DOES work on physical iOS for any in-app coordinates including UIAlertController. This ticket is only about out-of-process native-tap, which is needed for system-level dialogs (iOS permission prompts) that appear before/outside the app's UIWindow.
title: fdb native-tap: implement physical iOS support via WebDriverAgent

Backlog of **missing-coverage suggestions** surfaced during the Quarto slide overhaul (#5). Each rebuilt deck's `coverage-notes.md` recorded concrete gaps on its broad themes; this issue rolls them up so they aren't lost in per-deck notes. These are **deliberate future editing passes**, not part of the migration (which is shipped) and **not** the annual current-events refresh (that's a separate surgical pass per `docs/slides/TEMPLATE.md`).

Scope note: some hands-on items overlap with #3 (Enhance Hands-On Activities) and several "link to Ch. 4 / DSA" items are about cross-referencing decks that already exist. Source deck is noted in each item.

## 1. New or substantially expanded decks (largest gaps)

- [ ] **Disinformation / propaganda depth** — the four behavioral signatures (volume, retweet ratio, retweet speed, collusion), Benkler's *Network Propaganda* finding, CIB detection (Meta/Graphika/Stanford IO), election deepfakes (Jan 2024 NH Biden robocall). *(03-Platform/01-Platform, 02-Propaganda)*
- [ ] **Content moderation as its own treatment** (book §3.6) — currently only previewed; GIFCT shared-hash terrorism database as a "centralization = takedown risk, no appeal" case study. *(03-Platform/01-Platform)*
- [ ] **Age-gating / youth bans** — Australia's under-16 social-media ban (effective Dec 10, 2025) as categorical exclusion + an age-verification/privacy problem; could be its own short deck. *(04-Legal/01-Legal)*
- [ ] **Standalone internet-governance deck** — the conclusion currently absorbs governance; if it grows (Oversight Board, Bluesky composable moderation, Mastodon federation, data-localization economics), split it into its own `07-` section deck. *(07-Conclusion)*

## 2. Cross-cutting threads (recur across multiple decks — handle consistently)

- [ ] **Encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT) + ECH/Encrypted ClientHello** as both a censorship target and a circumvention layer — gestured at in three decks; deserves coherent treatment spanning Technical/Measurement/Circumvention (Iran 2022 Mahsa Amini, Russia post-2022, a "state of SNI encryption in 2026" slide). *(02-Technical/01-Protocols, 02-DoS, 06-Circumvention)*
- [ ] **Section 230 / intermediary liability ↔ DSA** explicit cross-links — central to Platform + Legal; state pressure leverages safe-harbor. Add forward/back pointers between the Intro, Platform, and Legal decks. *(01-Overview, 03-Platform/01-Platform, 02-Propaganda)*
- [ ] **"Up the stack" economic controls** — app-store/payment-rail prioritization, CDN/cloud free-tier effects, AI paid-vs-free tiers as a "tax on access" parallel to zero rating. Ties §4.3 to the platform chapter. *(03-Platform/01-Platform, 04-Legal/03-PaidPrioritization)*
- [ ] **Shared vocabulary / Roberts's taxonomy as a recurring reference** — promote censor / point-of-control / fear-friction-flooding / porous to a reusable slide for continuity across decks. *(01-Overview)*
- [ ] **Botnet thread continuity** — book defers botnet mechanics; ensure the Platform/abuse material picks up Mirai-style IoT botnets so the thread isn't dropped between Ch. 2 and Ch. 3. *(02-DoS)*

## 3. Per-deck content additions

- [ ] **Intro:** globalization (§1.3) slide — spread of centralized filtering infrastructure / China's model as export. *(01-Overview)*
- [ ] **Protocols:** Iran's June 2025 "stealth blackout" (arXiv 2507.14183) as a case study contrasting Egypt-style BGP withdrawal; QUIC/HTTP-3 (UDP) filtering slide. *(02-Technical/01-Protocols)*
- [ ] **DoS:** low-rate / Layer-7 application DoS (Cloudflare: ~93% of attacks on journalism orgs are L7); RuNet selective-throttling case study (2021 Twitter, 2025 call interruptions). *(02-DoS)*
- [ ] **Platform:** generative AI as a moderation *target* not just moderator (Grok NCII-deepfake + Ofcom/EU Online Safety Act responses) — revisit when per-regulator dates firm up. *(03-Platform/01-Platform)*
- [ ] **Propaganda:** China's 50-cent army with King/Pan/Roberts (2017) data (distraction, not rebuttal); a downstream-effects-skepticism slide (exposure ≠ persuasion, e.g. Eady et al. 2023). *(03-Platform/02-Propaganda)*
- [ ] **Personalization:** generative-AI/chatbots as the new personalization surface (data voids); YouTube recommendation-radicalization research; US-side "addictive feed" laws to balance the EU/DSA lean. *(03-Platform/03-Personalization)*
- [ ] **Legal:** CFAA + researcher chilling effects (Sandvig v. Barr, Van Buren 2021 — relevant to our own Ch. 5 measurement work); DMCA §1201 anti-circumvention vs. §512; global intermediary-liability comparison (India IT Rules, NetzDG, Brazil); state laws in depth (TX HB20, FL SB7072). *(04-Legal/01-Legal)*
- [ ] **Net Neutrality:** end-to-end / common-carriage lineage (telegraph→telephone→broadband); no-competition last-mile as the structural argument; EU BEREC as a statute-backed contrast to US ping-pong. *(04-Legal/02-NetNeutrality)*
- [ ] **Paid Prioritization:** India 2016 Free Basics / TRAI differential-pricing ban as developing-world precedent; sponsored-data / 5G network-slicing as the next form. *(04-Legal/03-PaidPrioritization)*
- [ ] **Measurement:** modern GFW / Iran multi-layer filtering / Kazakhstan state HTTPS interception (rogue root CA); Censored Planet methodology depth (Satellite/Iris, Augur, Hyperquack); name Salganik's *Bit by Bit* ethics framework as scaffolding. *(05-Measurement)*
- [ ] **Circumvention:** Snowflake & Conjure pluggable transports; I2P / garlic routing half-slide; sustainability/economics of circumvention infrastructure (who pays for bridges/relays/decoy routers). *(06-Circumvention)*
- [ ] **Conclusion:** AI content provenance (C2PA, watermarking) as a partial answer to synthetic-media epistemics; data-localization economics. *(07-Conclusion)*

## 4. Hands-on / activities (coordinate with #3)

- [ ] **Throttling-detection lab (Wehe)** — agenda Lecture 4 pairs throttling with detection; a short walkthrough of replay-with/without-tunnel methodology and its noise problems. *(02-DoS)*
- [ ] **Circumvention threat-model exercise** — match personas (diaspora journalist, domestic activist, casual streamer) to tool portfolios. *(06-Circumvention)*
- [ ] **Encore / same-origin side-channel demo** — animate onload/onerror as a one-bit censorship measurement. *(05-Measurement)*

## 5. Dated or weak figures to strengthen (deeper edit, beyond a refresh)

- [ ] **RPKI adoption** — quantify "needs wide deployment" with a live % of routes with valid ROAs. *(02-Technical/01-Protocols)*
- [ ] **Personalization "Bobble" findings** — the 2012 search-personalization numbers are a decade old (book flags this); needs a modern replication or current search-audit result. *(03-Platform/03-Personalization)*
- [ ] **Zero-rating field data** — our Chen-Feamster-Calandro Kenya/South Africa natural experiments are ~2014–2018; refresh with an A4AI/GSMA affordability report. *(04-Legal/03-PaidPrioritization, 05-Measurement)*
- [ ] **Statistical-detection math** (max-likelihood / IP-ID hypothesis testing) — dropped for lean-ness; re-add as an appendix if teaching a technical cohort. *(05-Measurement)*

---

*Generated from the 12 decks' `coverage-notes.md` "Suggested missing coverage" sections after the #5 overhaul (commit `d61f0b1`). Pick items per term; keep slides lean — not everything here needs to ship.*
title: Slides: missing-coverage backlog from the #5 overhaul (content depth, not refresh)

## Problem or Use Case

I want to run iMessage from Hermes on an always-on Mac without any cloud service or relay in the loop. No managed line, no webhook, no public URL. Just the local Messages.app database plus the [`imsg`](https://github.com/nicholasstephan/imsg) CLI, which drives IMCore directly on the machine.

I'm filing this before opening a PR because iMessage clearly already has attention here, and I'd rather check direction than burn review cycles on something that fights your roadmap:

- Photon (`plugins/platforms/photon/`, author NousResearch) is the managed Spectrum service. Plugin-based, and from the README it reads like the path you recommend to most people.
- BlueBubbles (`gateway/platforms/bluebubbles.py`) is the self-hosted Mac relay.
- Linq picked up channel docs recently.

So it isn't a duplicate (there's no imsg-CLI adapter in the tree), but it is a fourth iMessage path, and it leans on the local-Mac model rather than the managed-service direction Photon represents. Your contributor guide says to ask about exactly this kind of thing before building, so here I am.

## Proposed Solution

A native `imsg` adapter that shells out to the CLI:

- Inbound through `imsg watch --json --since-rowid`, with persistent resume state so a restart doesn't replay or drop messages.
- Outbound through `imsg send`; attachments through `imsg send --file`.
- Typing indicators and read receipts via IMCore, with `imsg launch` arming the bridge when the adapter connects.
- A small declarative rules engine for group access: top-down, first match wins, with `silent_drop` as the default deny so the bot never leaks its existence to an unauthorized sender. A legacy flat allowlist auto-synthesizes into rules, so existing configs keep working with no migration.

I already have the whole thing built and tested on a private branch: 68 passing tests, clean compile, adapter plus config/run/status/cron/send_message wiring plus a desktop setup card. I can open the PR today if you're interested.

The question I actually want answered: would you take an on-device, no-cloud iMessage path at all? And if yes, do you want it as a plugin under `plugins/platforms/` to match Photon, instead of wired into core `gateway/platforms/`? I'm glad to repackage it as a standalone plugin before submitting if that's the shape you'd prefer.

## Alternatives Considered

Photon covers the managed case well, but it's a third-party service on a shared or paid line. I specifically want zero external dependency: the user's own Mac, their own Apple ID, and nothing else sitting in the path.

BlueBubbles needs its server running plus a webhook exposed. The `imsg` CLI reads `chat.db` and talks to IMCore locally, so neither is required.

I could also just keep this private, since it works for me as is. But the no-relay, no-SaaS angle seems useful to more people than me, so I'd rather offer it if you'll have it.

## Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

## Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

## Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR (already built; just want a direction call on core vs plugin first)

## Notes

One known gap: `imsg react` (tapbacks) exits `-1743` on the macOS builds I tested, so reactions are a no-op for now. Everything else works: send, receive, typing, read receipts, attachments, and the group rules. I wrote it up as a known limitation and left it open for anyone who finds a working IMCore reaction path.
title: [Feature]: Native on-device iMessage adapter via the imsg CLI (no cloud relay), plugin or core?

body:
> This issue consolidates #1647, #1648, and #1661 into a single unified observability work item. Those issues are now closed and tracked here.

## Purpose

Define the full observability picture for the SSB platform — covering both **business / product metrics** and **operational / system metrics** — what we have today, the gaps, and the alerting required. This also incorporates the metrics audit action from the Lean Coffee session (Jun 24).

This is a requirements issue. It deliberately does not prescribe _how_ to deliver it (build it natively, use a third-party platform, etc.) — that is the implementer's decision. The goal is to state clearly **what we need to be able to see and be alerted on**.

---

## Context & background

Raised during the Lean Coffee session on Jun 24, the team recognised that there is currently no clear picture of what metrics are being collected across the Alpha platform, or whether those metrics are sufficient for understanding platform health and performance.

---

## Two cross-cutting gaps (apply across both business and system metrics)

**No common observability tool / single pane.** Where logs and metrics exist at all, they are fragmented across separate places with no unified view. Answering one question today means stitching several sources together by hand. There is no single place a person — technical or not — can open to understand how the platform is doing.

**No proper alerting when a metric flags a problem.** Capturing a metric or a log is not the same as being told when it goes wrong. Today there is no reliable path that turns a problem signal into an alert a human actually receives — so problems are found manually, late, or from a citizen/agency complaint.

Both points are in scope here: all metrics defined below need a common place to live and a dependable alerting path to a human.

---

## What we have today

### Business / product metrics
- **Chatbot** — usage, traffic, latency, RAG-degraded %, error rate: metrics + alerting exist.
- **Landing** — basic page/event analytics.
- **Forms / submissions / payments / email outcomes** — the underlying data is captured (database + logs) but is not turned into metrics, a dashboard, or alerts.
- **Forms funnel analytics** — instrumented in the code (via Umami) but not active in production (produces zero data).

### Operational / system metrics
- **Chatbot** — dashboard + alarms (cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, RAG) routed to chat. Fully instrumented; this is the model to replicate.
- **SES** — a send-failure alarm exists but is not wired to any notification target (it alerts no one).
- **ECS / RDS / ALB monitoring** — a monitoring module exists but is pointed at the retired platform, not the live stack.
- **Everything else** — the live forms API, landing, form builder, both databases, the submission queues, and the deploy path — has effectively no monitoring or alerting.

---

## Metrics we need

### Business / product metrics

**Funnel & conversion**
- Form views → starts
- Completion rate (started → submitted) and per-step drop-off
- Submission volume per service, per day/week
- Field-level validation-error frequency (friction points)
- Time-to-complete

**Payments**
- Payment conversion: payment-started → paid
- Payment abandonment rate & count, by service
- Revenue collected / pending, by service & MDA

**Delivery & outcomes**
- Citizen confirmation-email delivery rate (including bounces/complaints)
- MDA notification delivery rate — did the agency actually receive the submission
- MDA-notification fallback / "no MDA notified" rate (misconfiguration)
- Case-management webhook delivery success rate
- Submissions per MDA / per service

**Engagement**
- Chat usage, answered rate, chat → form handoff
- Landing search usage, feedback volume

### Operational / system metrics

**Availability**
- Uptime per surface: landing, forms, form builder, chat
- End-to-end success (scheduled synthetic test submission / payment)
- ALB 5xx / 4xx, healthy-host count, request rate — for the live API

**Latency / performance**
- API p50 / p95 / p99; page-load (SSR); chat turn latency

**Compute & data**
- ECS CPU/mem, OOM, task restarts, running-vs-desired (API + builder)
- RDS (forms + vector): CPU, connections, free storage, IOPS, read/write latency
- Serverless SSR errors / throttles / cold starts

**Async pipeline**
- Submission queue depth + age of oldest message
- Dead-letter queue count > 0 (failed email/processor jobs)
- Email send failures, bounce rate, complaint rate
- Bedrock invoke errors / throttles / model-not-enabled
- Case-management webhook HTTP failures / retries

**Release / deploy**
- ECS deployment circuit-breaker rollback (silent failed deploys)
- Build & promotion failures

**Security / edge**
- ACM certificate expiry
- WAF blocked / rate-limit (forms + landing)
- Auth failure spikes

**Cost / quota**
- Spend anomalies (especially model usage), service-quota headroom, storage-growth trend

---

## Alerting we need

**Business signals**
- No submissions / payments / emails for N hours (silent pipeline failure)
- Payment success rate drops below threshold
- MDA notification fails or falls back to the internal/test recipient
- Case-management webhook delivery failures
- Confirmation-email bounce/complaint spike

**System signals**
- Any surface down / failing health check
- 5xx rate, latency, ECS/RDS saturation thresholds breached
- Dead-letter queue non-empty / submission queue backing up
- SES send failures + bounce/complaint (wire the existing, currently-silent alarm)
- Deploy circuit-breaker rollback
- Certificate nearing expiry

**Alerts must reach the team via email at minimum.**

---

## Surfacing requirement

- **Business metrics**: must be visible on a dashboard non-technical stakeholders can read and filter themselves — self-serve, no queries/SQL — with breakdowns by service, MDA, and date.
- **System metrics**: a single at-a-glance health view per environment that engineers can scan.

How these are delivered is left to the implementer.

---

## Why now — evidence from a recent production audit

- 12 submissions sat in `pending_payment` (citizens started a paid form and never completed) — invisible.
- 3 summer-camp applications notified the citizen but not the MDA (form went live before its MDA recipient was configured) — no alert; only found by manual log analysis.
- Several submissions routed their MDA notification to the internal test inbox — no alert.
- The forms funnel produces zero data in production because tracking isn't switched on.
- Sandbox deploys failed for ~90 minutes while the sites looked fine — the ECS circuit breaker rolled each deploy back and nothing alerted.
- The only SES alarm in production has no notification target.
- The live forms/landing/builder stack, both databases, and the submission queues have no alarms — the existing monitoring watches the decommissioned platform.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A defined, documented set of business and system metrics is produced and is queryable.
- [ ] Metrics audit completed: all existing metrics inventoried, gaps identified, missing metrics prioritised.
- [ ] All metrics live in one common observability surface (single pane), not fragmented across systems.
- [ ] A stakeholder-facing business dashboard surfaces metrics without requiring technical queries.
- [ ] A single at-a-glance system health view exists per environment.
- [ ] No metric can indicate a problem without an alert reaching a human — email at minimum.
- [ ] Forms funnel tracking (Umami) is live in production.
- [ ] Monitoring of the retired platform is replaced with monitoring of the live stack.
- [ ] Production first; staging/sandbox can follow the same definition.
title: Platform observability — metrics audit, gaps & alerting (SSB platform)

- [x] I searched existing issues and this has not been proposed before

*Closest prior art, checked open and closed: the cost-tiering stack (#1744 / #1717 / #1716) fixes which **model** each SDD role runs on, and #1747 adds the **reasoning-effort** dimension of the same problem. #1835 is about dispatch **mechanism** (inline Agent vs Workflow fan-out). All three optimize how cheaply a dispatched subagent runs. This proposal is a different, prior axis: **whether to dispatch at all**. If maintainers consider it subsumed by that direction, happy to close.*

## What problem does this solve?

SDD is presented as the execution path for a written plan, with guidance on how to dispatch subagents cheaply (model tiering, effort) but **no boundary condition for when not to fan out at all**. Every plan goes through dispatch.

That silently assumes fan-out always pays. It doesn't. Dispatching a subagent per task costs:

- **Context rebuild, paid N times.** Each fresh subagent re-reads the plan, re-orients in the codebase, and reloads the files it needs from cold. For a plan of many *independent* tasks that isolation is a feature (the parent context stays lean, exploration is discarded). For a handful of *tightly-coupled* tasks that each need most of the same context, it is pure repeated overhead.
- **Review-gate and serialization latency** between tasks, again worth it when tasks are genuinely parallel, dead weight when they are a short dependent chain.

The isolation benefit that justifies dispatch is "the single inline context would otherwise balloon." That only holds above a certain plan size. **Below it, inline execution in one warm context is both faster and not meaningfully more expensive**, because the context stays bounded so there is no runaway to prevent. Above it, fan-out wins on both cost and (with real parallelism) speed.

Because SDD states no threshold, agents default to fan-out universally, and users experience it as "SDD is slow" on small changes and reach for inline by feel. The routing pressure in `using-superpowers` ("if there is even a 1% chance a skill applies you MUST invoke it") reinforces the always-dispatch default, so nothing pulls the other way.

## Proposed solution

Add a short **routing/boundary note** to SDD (and/or `executing-plans`), not a mechanism change, the same shape as the existing model-selection guidance:

> Route by plan size before dispatching. Use SDD when the plan has many tasks whose independent work can fan out in parallel, where isolating each in its own context keeps the orchestrator lean. For a small, tightly-coupled, few-task change, **run the implementation inline in one warm context** instead: the context stays bounded, and warm-context continuity beats repeated per-subagent re-orientation. When SDD feels slow, the usual cause is serial execution of tasks that were actually independent; fix the plan's decomposition to expose parallelism rather than accepting the overhead.

The discriminator is: task count, task independence, and whether the combined working context would plausibly exceed a warm-context budget. Harness-general; no per-harness mechanism required.

## What alternatives did you consider?

- **Do nothing.** Users keep paying fan-out overhead on small changes and route around SDD by intuition; the "SDD is slow / stalls" family of reports (e.g. #1545) partly reflects this.
- **Fold into the cost-tiering work (#1744 / #1747).** Those tune the cost of a *dispatched* role. This is orthogonal: it is the decision of whether to dispatch. Both are needed.
- **Leave it to the user to just not invoke SDD.** Fragile. It relies on the user overriding the collection's own always-dispatch default under exactly the conditions (time pressure, a written plan in hand) where they will follow the default instead.

## Is this appropriate for core Superpowers?

Yes. It is harness-general decision guidance about the collection's own skill boundary, the "when not to use this" that a good recommendation carries and this one currently omits. No mechanism, no per-harness conditional.

## Evidence

I can bring numbers if it would help decide: same small plan run inline vs via SDD, measured on wall-clock and output tokens, n≈4 per arm, pre-registered prediction (inline wins wall-clock at bounded/comparable token cost below the threshold; SDD wins above it once parallelism is real). 

## Environment

| Field | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Superpowers version | 6.1.1 (installed) |
| Harness | Claude Code |
| Harness version | 2.1.201 |
| Model | Claude Opus 4.8 |

## Context

 The problem surfaced running the superpowers flow on real changes where SDD on a small, coupled plan felt slower than just doing it inline, while the token-runaway fear that motivates dispatch only actually applies to long, many-task sessions whose single context grows unbounded. 

*Drafting disclosure: written collaboratively. Claude (Opus 4.8) drafted the text and swept the issue tracker for prior art; I directed the scope and reviewed every claim and rewrote in my language.*
title: subagent-driven-development: no inline-vs-dispatch threshold — small, tightly-coupled changes pay fan-out overhead for isolation they don't need

## Summary

Grow the merchant catalog beyond its current seed so `haven_discover_tools` / the dashboard surface a useful set of pay-per-call x402 (and MPP) merchants — and, more importantly, make growth **sustainable** by tapping the x402 ecosystem's discovery layer instead of hand-curating forever.

## Current state

The catalog ships with **4 seed rows** (migration [`019_merchant_catalog.ts`](packages/backend/src/db/migrations/019_merchant_catalog.ts)):

| Name | Category | Rail | Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|
| Soundside — text generation | media | x402 | mcp |
| Soundside — image generation | media | x402 | mcp |
| Soundside — song generation | media | x402 | mcp |
| Haven MPP demo resource | demo | mpp | http |

So today the only *real* third-party merchant is Soundside, and only one category (`media`) is represented. Each entry is validated by the read-only probe in [`lib/merchant-catalog.ts`](packages/backend/src/lib/merchant-catalog.ts) (expects HTTP 402 + parsable challenge; degrades after `DEGRADE_AFTER_FAILURES`). That probe is the asset we should lean on: **anything we add gets price/availability verified automatically**, so the cost of adding a candidate is low and a bad entry self-degrades rather than misleading users.

## Recommendation 1 (strategic): integrate the x402 Bazaar discovery layer

Coinbase's **x402 Bazaar** is now the canonical discovery index for x402 resources, with a machine-readable catalog and an MCP discovery endpoint:

- Paginated catalog: `GET https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/resources` (limit/offset)
- Semantic search: `GET …/v2/x402/discovery/search`
- MCP endpoint: `https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/mcp`

Reportedly ~10k paid resources across Base/Solana. Instead of (or alongside) hand-seeding rows, Haven could pull candidates from Bazaar, run each through our existing `probeCatalogEntry`, and persist only the ones that verify. This turns the catalog from a static seed into a self-refreshing index and is a natural extension of the existing `refreshCatalog` cron.

**Proposed shape:** a `lib/catalog-discovery.ts` that fetches Bazaar pages, maps each resource → `CatalogRow` shape (name/description/category/resource_url/rail/protocol/tool_name), and feeds them through the probe before insert. Keep it opt-in / rate-limited; respect Base vs Solana network support (we're Base/Gnosis today — filter to chains we can actually pay on).

## Recommendation 2 (tactical): seed a broader, hand-picked set now

The ecosystem clusters around a few proven categories. Seed representative merchants in each (exact resource URLs **must be confirmed by the probe before insert** — do not hardcode unverified endpoints):

- **AI inference** — pay-per-prompt LLM/model wrappers (new category `ai`/`inference`)
- **Web search** — agent search APIs (category `search`)
- **Image generation** — DALL·E-3-style endpoints (extends `media`)
- **Data / enrichment** — weather, crypto/market data, company lookup, email verification, prediction markets (category `data`)
- **Translation** (category `media` or `data`)
- **Code execution / sandboxes** (category `compute`)

Sources to mine for concrete, currently-live endpoints: the Bazaar catalog above, [x402scan.com/resources](https://www.x402scan.com/resources), and Agent.market. Each candidate goes through the same 402 probe.

## Why category diversity matters here (bookkeeping tie-in)

Categories aren't cosmetic — they feed the BAS account map in the accounting export ([`lib/bas-accounts.ts`](packages/backend/src/lib/bas-accounts.ts), via the merchant-catalog LATERAL join in [`lib/accounting-entry.ts`](packages/backend/src/lib/accounting-entry.ts)). A catalog with only `media` means almost every booked entry falls back to the default expense account. Broadening categories improves automatic BAS classification for the SIE/Fortnox export. New categories added here should get a matching BAS mapping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide: Bazaar-discovery integration (Rec 1) vs. expanded static seed (Rec 2) vs. both.
- [ ] If discovery: `lib/catalog-discovery.ts` + tests, gated behind the existing `refreshCatalog` cron, Base-only filtering, probe-before-persist.
- [ ] If static: a follow-up migration adding probe-verified rows across ≥3 new categories.
- [ ] Any new category has a BAS account mapping in `lib/bas-accounts.ts`.
- [ ] No unverified resource URLs land in `merchant_catalog` (probe is the gate).

## References

- Bazaar discovery: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/x402/bazaar
- x402scan marketplace: https://www.x402scan.com/resources
- x402 ecosystem directory: https://x402daily.xyz/resources/ecosystem/

---
*Filed from a catalog review session. The cheap, safe path is to lean on the existing probe as the trust gate and let discovery do the sourcing.*
title: Expand merchant catalog: integrate x402 Bazaar discovery + seed broader categories

body:
## Context
The Harbor HTTP API is plain `fetch` + multipart and is Worker-friendly, but `@mysten/seal` leans on WebCrypto + `@noble` curves + CPU-intensive BLS12-381. The Worker runs with `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` and `compatibility_date: 2026-05-21` (`apps/api/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc:17`), and `@mysten/sui` `^2.9.1` is already a dependency of `apps/api` (`apps/api/package.json`). Whether SEAL fits the Worker's compressed-bundle cap and CPU limit is the single highest-risk unknown gating the entire private-memory workstream (roadmap "The key runtime unknown (must spike early)" + §1 spike row).

## Goal / user story
As an engineer, I want a throwaway Worker that imports `@mysten/seal`, encrypts one blob and decrypts it back, so we can decide WHERE encryption runs (Worker vs queue consumer vs Node CLI/MCP) before investing in `HarborClient`/`seal.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A minimal Worker (or `apps/api` test entry) imports `@mysten/seal` + `@mysten/sui/keypairs/ed25519`, and encrypts a small (<10KB) `Uint8Array` against a Seal policy id on Sui testnet, returning ciphertext.
- [ ] The same Worker builds a `SessionKey` + `seal_approve` PTB and decrypts the ciphertext back to the original bytes (round-trip asserted byte-equal).
- [ ] `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (or a real deploy) reports the compressed bundle size, recorded against the Workers size cap; CPU ms for one encrypt+decrypt is noted.
- [ ] A written finding recommends where encryption runs (Worker / queue consumer / Node-only) backed by the bundle + CPU numbers.
- [ ] If the Worker busts limits, the fallback (encrypt in the queue consumer or Node CLI/MCP) is documented so the Harbor client/encrypted-path issues target the right runtime.

## Implementation notes
- Add `@mysten/seal` to a scratch package or `apps/api` (do NOT keep it in the prod bundle if the spike fails). `@mysten/sui` is already present.
- You need a real `seal_policy_id` on Sui **testnet** — create one via Harbor (a bucket create yields a Seal policy) or reuse the `seal-docs.wal.app` example policy; the demo sample target already points there (`CONTEXTMEM_DEMO_SAMPLE_TARGET` in `wrangler.jsonc`).
- `SessionKey` requires an Ed25519 signer: `decodeSuiPrivateKey(suiprivkey1...)` → `Ed25519Keypair`. Use `SuiGrpcClient` (already used in `packages/walrus/src/proof.ts`/`history.ts`/`resolve.ts`) for the `seal_approve` devInspect.
- Gotchas: `nodejs_compat` polyfills crypto, but BLS in `@noble/curves` is CPU-heavy (Worker CPU limit ~30s paid, lower on free) and the compressed-bundle cap is small. This is throwaway — do not ship to prod. Keep `tar`-based `packProofBundle` (`packages/walrus/src/storage.ts:231`) out; it's Node-only regardless.

## Sui Overflow angle
This de-risks the whole Sui-native private-memory demo. The answer (edge-encrypt vs offload) determines the live-demo architecture: whether the hackathon judges see encryption happen in the same Worker that serves recall, or in a queue/Node tier.

## Dependencies
None — do this first. Blocks the `HarborClient` issue and the private SEAL encrypted remember/recall issue.

_Part of the ContextMEM roadmap (#4) • Sui Overflow build._

body:
## Problem

Users on RunPod / cloud GPUs have no upfront sense of what a training run will cost. They pick a GPU (A40 / L4 / 4090 / A100), set `epochs`, `batch_size`, `grad_accum_steps`, `image_size`, etc., and then discover hours later that the run was 3x more expensive than expected — or VRAM-OOM'd halfway through.

Today the only knob users see in `cloud/runpod/README.md` is qualitative ("A40 recommended entry tier"). We should give them a cheap pre-flight estimate.

## Proposal

A CLI / helper that takes a training config (the YAMLs in `configs/examples/`) plus a GPU choice and prints:

- estimated steps per epoch (from dataset size + `batch_size` * `grad_accum_steps`)
- estimated total steps and wall-clock time
- estimated $ cost (wall-clock * GPU $/hr)
- a VRAM-fit sanity check (warn before OOM)

Invocation idea:

```
custom-sam-peft estimate-cost configs/examples/coco_text_lora.yaml --gpu a40 --provider runpod
```

## Approach options

1. **Lookup-table + closed-form.** Bake in measured throughput (img/s) per (GPU, peft method, image_size) from a small benchmark matrix; multiply by step count. Simple, deterministic, easy to ship. Numbers drift as code changes.
2. **Quick on-device probe.** Run a 50-step warm-up on the actual hardware before the user commits to the full run. More accurate but only useful once the pod is already paid for; doesn't help pre-flight planning.
3. **Hybrid.** Ship (1) as a `cost.yaml` reference table (GPU × peft × image_size → img/s + $/hr); add an opt-in flag to run (2) for calibration.

Lean toward (1) for v1 — pre-flight is the use case that actually saves money.

## Open questions

- Where does the $/hr table live? (`cloud/runpod/pricing.yaml`? Hard-coded with a "last updated" date?) Prices drift.
- Do we support providers beyond RunPod in v1, or land RunPod-only and generalize later?
- Throughput table: do we measure it ourselves (one-time CI matrix run) or accept user-contributed numbers via PRs?
- Should this be a standalone CLI subcommand or just a section in the notebook FORM cell so non-technical users see it without leaving Jupyter?

## Scope guard

Out of scope for v1: estimating final metric quality, recommending optimal hyperparameters, multi-GPU runs.
title: feat: estimate training-run cost ($) from config + GPU choice

body:
## Motivation

`POLYFILL_INTL` today installs `getCanonicalLocales` / `Locale` / `PluralRules` / `NumberFormat` / `DateTimeFormat`. Missing from the set: **`Collator`, `DisplayNames`, `ListFormat`, `RelativeTimeFormat`, `Segmenter`**. Real-world JS bundles built for browser distribution lean on these:

- **Mastodon** — `Intl.Collator` for username/locale sorting, `Intl.DisplayNames` in `initial_state.ts`
- **Hotwire / Stimulus** ecosystem — `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` for `<relative-time>` style helpers
- **Discourse / Forem** — `Intl.ListFormat`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- **Anything using `String.prototype` segmentation** — `Intl.Segmenter`

Without these, a server-side renderer using quickjs.rb to evaluate the same JS bundle that ships to browsers blows up the moment the bundle references one of them. Today the workaround is to monkey-patch shims at the JS layer, but that's a downstream-by-downstream tax.

## Measured polyfill sizes (rolldown + minify, `polyfill-force.js` + `en` locale data where applicable)

| Polyfill | Minified |
|---|---|
| Current `POLYFILL_INTL` bundle | 2.1 MB |
| `intl-collator` (`@formatjs/intl-collator@0.2.1`, force) | **4.8 MB** |
| `intl-displaynames` (force + en) | 0.11 MB |
| `intl-listformat` (force + en) | 0.04 MB |
| `intl-relativetimeformat` (force + en) | 0.04 MB |
| `intl-segmenter` (force) | 0.13 MB |

`Collator` is a striking outlier — it ships the full Unicode collation table (DUCET). The other four combined are ~0.32 MB. `@formatjs/intl-collator` itself was published on May 15, 2026 (v0.2.1, 3 days old as of this writing); the rest are mature (7.x–12.x).

Note: feature-flagging only controls *runtime load* — the bytecode is embedded in the compiled `.so` and shipped to every user regardless of whether their VM enables the feature.

## Design options

### A. Granular feature flags (one constant per Intl class)

```rb
POLYFILL_INTL_COLLATOR
POLYFILL_INTL_DISPLAYNAMES
POLYFILL_INTL_LISTFORMAT
POLYFILL_INTL_RELATIVETIME
POLYFILL_INTL_SEGMENTER
```

Each new constant adds: 1 entry in `polyfills/src/`, 1 entry in `rolldown.config.mjs`, 1 `qjsc_*` extern + load branch in `quickjsrb.c`, 1 RBS constant. Mechanical pattern.

**Pros**: opt-in per feature; runtime cost paid only when enabled.
**Cons**: gem `.so` grows by the sum of every embedded bytecode. `Collator` alone bloats the gem by ~5 MB.

### B. Granular flags for the small ones; `Collator` lives elsewhere

Same as A, but `Collator` ships as a separate companion gem (e.g. `quickjs-intl-collator`) that downstreams add only when needed. The companion gem declares a runtime dependency on quickjs.rb and registers its bytecode through a public-ish hook (e.g. `Quickjs::VM.register_polyfill(:intl_collator, bytecode)`).

**Pros**: keeps the core gem lean (~0.3 MB extra at most). Heavy-user opt-in is a `gem 'quickjs-intl-collator'` away.
**Cons**: needs a small extension API for external polyfill registration, which we don't have today. New gem to maintain.

### C. All-or-nothing bundled flag

`POLYFILL_INTL_EXTENDED` (or rename existing `POLYFILL_INTL` to mean "everything"). Single constant turns on every additional polyfill, including Collator.

**Pros**: simplest API surface.
**Cons**: forces ~5 MB even on users who only want DisplayNames. Doesn't match the existing "small footprint by default" philosophy.

### D. Build-time selection (env var / generator)

Polyfill set is decided when the gem is **built** (e.g. `INTL_POLYFILLS=collator,displaynames bundle install --path=...`). Default install ships the current minimal set; an env knob produces a fatter build.

**Pros**: zero `.so` cost for users who don't ask. Maximally flexible.
**Cons**: precompiled gems on RubyGems would have to choose one configuration (defeats the purpose); only useful for users building from source. Awkward UX.

## My take

**Lean toward B**: granular flags for DisplayNames / ListFormat / RelativeTimeFormat / Segmenter (cheap, fits the existing pattern), and `Collator` in a companion gem because its size genuinely warrants separating.

The cheap four together add ~0.32 MB to the `.so` — well within the existing budget, and matches the granularity of `POLYFILL_FILE` / `POLYFILL_ENCODING` / `POLYFILL_URL`. Collator's 4.8 MB is in a different league and would dominate the gem size; a companion gem keeps the choice with the downstream that actually needs it.

The companion-gem path needs one minor extension to quickjs.rb itself: a way for an external gem to register additional bytecode that VM construction can pick up via a feature symbol. Probably ~20 lines in `vm_m_initialize` plus a Ruby-level registry.

## What I'd like to confirm

1. Is B (granular for cheap ones + companion gem for Collator) directionally agreeable? Or is there a strong preference for keeping everything in one gem (A or C)?
2. If B, would you accept the small public API for external polyfill registration? Rough sketch: `Quickjs::VM.register_polyfill(symbol, bytecode_string)`, looked up during VM construction.
3. Should `RelativeTimeFormat` / `ListFormat` ship `en` locale data only (matching the existing pattern), or include all locales (FormatJS's `locale-data/index.js`)? `en`-only keeps the bundle small; all-locales is what most production apps want. Current `POLYFILL_INTL` is `en`-only and grew the bundle by ~140ms eval-load time on a warm cache.

Not blocking on this — willing to draft whichever direction is preferred.
title: RFC: Expanding the Intl polyfill set (Collator, DisplayNames, ListFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, Segmenter)

## What `tider` generated

```text
I agree with the “you don’t need organic to run FB ads” takes, but I wouldn’t wait on content either—start ads now using simple trust-first creatives you can make without being on camera, and give your Page a minimal “trust hub” so clicks don’t bounce.

What to make first (no face needed):
- 6–15s hands-only demo: show scale in your hand, a quick use, a close-up of texture/color. Big captions, clear benefit, one CTA.
- Photo carousel: 3–5 strong images with short overlay text (problem → outcome), final card with offer/FAQ.
- Social proof: screenshot a real review, add product photo, and a clear “Shop now” line.

Run paid now: Sales objective, broad 35+ on Facebook placements, 2–3 creatives in one ad set, small daily budget. Let the first week tell you which angle (demo vs proof vs benefit) pulls. Once you have traffic, add a simple retargeting ad that leans hard on reviews/returns/shipping clarity.

Hiring: hold the social media manager. If you spend, spend on assets—either a UGC creator to shoot 3–5 clips or a lightweight editor to turn your raw phone shots into usable posts/ads. That’s the highest ROI early.
```

## What I posted / wanted instead

The reply should have more clearly surfaced the Kova lens:

- real product visuals should not just be ad creatives
- they can be reused across ads, the Page, PDPs, and follow-up
- the same capture solves trust and content reuse

The current output is solid general FB-advice, but the Kova angle is barely visible.

## Gap

The prompt is allowing `--context=kova` to behave like a soft supporting lens instead of a strong framing constraint on threads about content creation / ads / social strategy.

This thread is a good Kova fit because it is specifically about:

- creating trust-first creatives without being on camera
- deciding what to produce first
- whether to skip ahead with ads
- whether hiring early makes sense

That should have triggered a stronger “same visual proof can be reused across channels” frame.

## Desired behavior

When `--context=kova` is present and the thread is about content creation, ads, social strategy, or trust assets, `Best Pick` should explicitly mention that the same real product visuals can be reused across ads, the Page, PDPs, and follow-up.

## Notes

This is a calibration example for the reply spec. It is not necessarily a hard CLI flag request; the main question is whether the inference rule should be stronger or whether we need a more explicit override later.
title: reply calibration: Kova angle missed on Facebook ads / content thread

body:
Package the skafinity / rotaliate procedural-music engine as a standalone s&box asset that other s&box developers can drop into their own games to get endless, deterministic procedural ska/reggae music from a shareable `vibe:tag:n` seed.

This is the inverse direction of the rest of this repo: skafinity is the *web* port of the rotaliate-client engine; this issue is about re-extracting that same engine from `../rotaliate-client` into a clean, reusable **s&box library/asset**. The algorithmic source of truth stays the C# in `reference/` (and the live rotaliate-client).

## Plausibility: ~8/10
The hard part is already done. The generator is effectively a dependency-free library; the only real work is wrapping the playback driver and severing two game-specific hooks. PRNG parity is already pinned and proven (the skafinity web port reproduces it bit-for-bit), so the determinism contract is solid.

## Scope

### Tier A — generator (drop-in, ~0 effort)
- `MusicGen.cs` and `VibeCodec.cs` import only `System.*` — no `Sandbox`/`Rotaliate`/`SoundStream` coupling. Lift verbatim into the package.
- Public API is already library-shaped: `GenerateSamples()`, the chunked `BeginPlan → RenderPitchedRange → FinishMono` path, and `VibeCodec.Encode/Apply/Fields`, all over a plain `MusicGen.Config`.

### Tier B — playback driver (~1–2 days)
Fork `MusicController.cs` into e.g. `SkafinityMusicPlayer : Component` and strip the two rotaliate-specific dependencies:
- **`PlayerData` persistence** (~20 call sites: tag, vibe, `MusicN`, volume, enable) → replace with component `[Property]` fields + an optional `Action<int> onAdvance` / persistence callback.
- **`LobbyNetworkManager` admin-follow** (`SyncWithAdmin`/`ApplyFollow`/`CanFollowAdmin`, ~80 lines) → delete, or expose as an optional hook.
- **Keep** the s&box `SoundStream`/`SoundHandle`/`Mixer` plumbing, `GameTask.RunInThreadAsync` worker fan-out, and the `[Property]` inspector knobs — that plumbing is exactly what makes this an s&box asset rather than the web port. The crossfade/look-ahead logic (`PushTransition`, `FillAhead`, `WriteSongBody`) is self-contained and reusable verbatim.

### Deliverables
- [ ] Package `MusicGen` + `VibeCodec` unchanged.
- [ ] `SkafinityMusicPlayer : Component` with the two hooks abstracted out.
- [ ] Minimal example scene + inspector-authorable vibe knobs.
- [ ] (optional) Port the `MusicScreen.razor` vibe-editor as a sample UI.
- [ ] (optional) A parity test asserting the packaged engine still matches the captured golden vectors.

## Open question — monetization (resolve before publishing)
Whether you can **charge** for this as an s&box asset is unconfirmed. s&box (Facepunch) distributes via its own registry (sbox.game / historically asset.party) and has leaned toward free community sharing with game-centric payouts rather than a paid per-asset store, but its commercial terms have shifted during development. **Verify before relying on it:**
- sbox.game and the official s&box docs/wiki publishing + licensing pages
- Facepunch's ToS / monetization & payout policy
- s&box Discord / forums for the current practical answer
title: Extract the procedural-music engine into a reusable s&box asset/package

## Context

Section 2001 currently implements the core estate tax calculation (subsections a, b, c) but is missing three additional subsections that handle special cases and coordination rules.

## Location

**File**: `src/TaxCode/Section2001.lean`  
**Lines**: 194-196 (TODOs at end of file)

## Missing Features

### IRC § 2001(d): Gift tax paid by spouse

**Description**: Adjustments when the decedent's spouse paid gift tax on prior gifts.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement adjustments for gift tax paid by spouse (IRC §2001(d))
```

**What's needed**:
- Model joint gifts and split gifts
- Calculate adjustments to tentative tax
- Coordinate with § 2513 (split gift elections)

### IRC § 2001(e): Coordination with § 2513 and § 2035

**Description**: Special rules for coordinating estate tax with gift-splitting elections and gifts made within 3 years of death.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement coordination of sections 2513 and 2035 (IRC §2001(e))
```

**What's needed**:
- § 2513: Gift-splitting between spouses
- § 2035: Gifts made within 3 years of death included in estate
- Adjustments to calculation when both apply

### IRC § 2001(f): Valuation of gifts

**Description**: Rules for valuing prior taxable gifts for purposes of the estate tax calculation.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement valuation of gifts logic (IRC §2001(f))
```

**What's needed**:
- Use gift tax return values (not date-of-death values)
- Handle cases where gift values have changed
- Model finality of gift tax valuations

## Suggested Approach

1. **Extend data structures**: Add fields to capture spouse gift tax info, split gift elections, etc.
2. **New calculation functions**: `apply_section_2001_d`, `coordinate_2513_and_2035`, `value_prior_gifts`
3. **Update main function**: Integrate new subsections into `section2001_b_computation`
4. **Add theorems**: Verify adjustments preserve tax law requirements

## Impact

These are **optional enhancements** - the core estate tax logic is complete. However, these subsections are needed for:
- Estates with substantial lifetime gifts
- Joint returns with split gifts
- Gifts made near death

## Priority

**LOW** - Nice to have, but core functionality is complete

## References

- IRC § 2001(d), (e), (f)
- Current implementation: Lines 113-116 (main computation)
- Related: § 2513 (gift splitting), § 2035 (3-year rule)
title: [FEATURE] Section 2001: Implement missing subsections (d), (e), (f)

body:
## Problem

The boilerplate has **no `.coderabbit.yaml` config or recipe**. CodeRabbit (the AI code review tool) is the workhorse for low/medium-risk PR auto-review in `nyc-re-tracker-2`, but more importantly, its **path-instruction system enforces multi-file consistency** in ways that no other tool currently does.

The pattern that's emerged: when one file changes, certain other files must also change. CodeRabbit blocks the PR if they don't. This catches an entire class of "I forgot to update the docs/taxonomy/test" bugs at review time.

## The multi-file sync pattern

`nyc-re-tracker-2` `.coderabbit.yaml` enforces three classes of cross-file consistency:

1. **Events ↔ Taxonomy ↔ LLM events** — if `events.ts` changes, `event-taxonomy.md` must too. If `event-taxonomy.md` LLM-events section changes, `posthog_llm.py` must too. If `prompts.py` changes a template materially, `<NAME>_PROMPT_VERSION` must bump.
2. **Memory budget guards (ETL)** — flag steps accumulating >100K rows, missing empty-batch guards on `full_replace`, large-geometry datasets without streaming.
3. **Path-specific instructions** — different review prompts for `api/` vs `ui/` vs `etl/` vs `transforms/` vs `schemas/`.

Without these, sync drift is a constant tax — a developer changes one side, ships, and the other side rots until someone notices.

## Why it matters

Concrete examples of bugs CodeRabbit caught in `nyc-re-tracker-2` (each would have shipped without it):
- New tracked button added to `events.ts` but no row in `event-taxonomy.md` → CodeRabbit blocked the PR until the taxonomy was updated
- Prompt template materially changed but `PROMPT_VERSION` not bumped → CodeRabbit caught it; would otherwise have polluted PostHog eval data
- Inngest step added with `for row in rows:` accumulating into a list → CodeRabbit flagged the OOM risk on the 2048MB Fly VM

## Reference impl in `nyc-re-tracker-2`

- `.coderabbit.yaml` (~150 lines, well-commented)
- Path instructions for `api/`, `ui/`, `etl/`, `transforms/`, `schemas/`, `docs/architecture/event-taxonomy.md`, `docs/operations/llm-observability.md`
- Memory budget rules in the path instructions for `etl/`
- Anti-patterns #27 + #28 in CLAUDE.md reference the enforcement
- Memory: DEAL-118 referenced in `MEMORY.md` (CodeRabbit installed, $5/mo via org license alongside gitleaks)

## Proposed boilerplate changes

- [ ] `.coderabbit.yaml.template` (or shipped at root if downstream projects can opt out) — base config with:
  - Sensible default review tone + scope
  - Placeholder path instructions for common patterns: `api/`, `ui/`, `tests/`, `docs/`
  - Comment stubs explaining how to add multi-file sync rules
- [ ] `recipes/integrations/coderabbit.md` — recipe covering: install, free tier vs. paid, the multi-file sync pattern (worked examples), how to design a path instruction
- [ ] `recipes/integrations/coderabbit-multi-file-sync.md` — sub-recipe with the events ↔ taxonomy ↔ LLM-events worked example as a template downstream projects can crib
- [ ] CLAUDE.md gets a § Code Review section explaining the role: low/medium-risk PRs use CodeRabbit auto-review; high-risk PRs require human review (this is already in nyc-re-tracker-2 CLAUDE.md verbatim)
- [ ] `bin/vibe setup --wizard coderabbit` (or fold into main setup) creates `.coderabbit.yaml` from template, opens browser to GitHub App install
- [ ] Doctor checks: `.coderabbit.yaml` syntactically valid? GitHub App installed?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.coderabbit.yaml.template` exists with documented placeholder path instructions
- [ ] `recipes/integrations/coderabbit.md` covers install + free-tier limits
- [ ] `recipes/integrations/coderabbit-multi-file-sync.md` documents the events ↔ taxonomy worked example
- [ ] CLAUDE.md PR Review Policy references CodeRabbit's role for low/medium-risk PRs
- [ ] Doctor validates config + GitHub App install
- [ ] Setup wizard scaffolds the config

## Open decisions

- **Default review tone:** CodeRabbit defaults to fairly polite, sometimes verbose. nyc-re-tracker-2 dialed it down. Document the tuning.
- **Free tier or paid:** CodeRabbit has a free tier; paid unlocks more features. Recipe should document the cut.
- **Auto-fix mode:** CodeRabbit can auto-suggest fixes inline. Should the boilerplate enable it by default? Lean yes (with the caveat that the agent should still review suggestions).
- **Interaction with #190 (plugin packaging):** if the boilerplate ships as a Claude Code plugin, where does `.coderabbit.yaml` live in the plugin manifest? Probably stays in the project root, not the plugin.

## Related

- Pairs with **`bin/posthog` issue** — CodeRabbit's events ↔ taxonomy ↔ LLM-events enforcement is the multi-file sync example
- Pairs with **CLI conventions doctrine** — CodeRabbit's role is explained in the PR review policy
- nyc-re-tracker-2 tickets: DEAL-118 (CodeRabbit install), various ad-hoc tuning over time
- Open boilerplate issue cluster #277, #268, #299 — once Paper integration lands, CodeRabbit can also enforce ds/ ↔ Paper Design DNA artboard sync (DNA artboard required when adding a ds/ component, per nyc-re-tracker-2 anti-pattern #23)
title: Add `.coderabbit.yaml` template + multi-file sync enforcement recipe
